{{infobox Onsen |Name = Ureshino Onsen |image = Ureshino onsen.jpg |Comment = |Location = {{ill|Saga Prefecture|ja|佐賀県|12=draft}} {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|12=draft}} {{ill|Ureshino Town|ja|嬉野町 (佐賀県)|lt=Ureshino Town|lt_ja=嬉野町|12=draft}} |Access = Railway : {{ill|Sasebo Line|ja|佐世保線|12=draft}} {{ill|Takeo Onsen Station|ja|武雄温泉駅|12=draft}} via {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|12=draft}} for about 30 minutes
West Kyushu Shinkansen Ureshino Onsen Station
''For other access methods, see [[#アクセス|Access]]'' |Water Type = {{ill|Chloride Hot Spring|ja|塩化物泉|12=draft}} |Temperature = |Discharge = |pH =7.8 |Liquid Classification = |Osmotic Pressure Classification = |Number of Accommodations = |Total Capacity = |Annual Bath Visitors = |Statistical Year = |External links = [https://spa-u.net/ Ureshino Onsen Tourism Association] |Special Notes = }} '''Ureshino Onsen''' (嬉野温泉) is a {{ill|Hot Spring|ja|温泉|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Saga Prefecture|ja|佐賀県|12=draft}}, {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Ureshino Town|ja|嬉野町 (佐賀県)|lt=Ureshino Town|lt_ja=嬉野町|12=draft}} (formerly part of {{ill|Hizen Province|ja|肥前国|12=draft}}). Along with {{ill|Takeo Onsen|ja|武雄温泉|12=draft}}, it is one of the representative hot springs of the prefecture. It has been selected as one of {{ill|Japan's 100 Views|ja|日本百景|12=draft}} and is trademarked by Ureshino City under the names “Japan’s Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs Ureshino Onsen” and “Saga–Ureshino Onsen.” == Water Type == * Sodium – Bicarbonate Salt / Chloride Hot Spring It is a baking soda spring renowned for its beauty-enhancing properties, leaving the skin exceptionally smooth after a {{ill|Bathing|ja|入浴|12=draft}}. Its water quality was chosen by {{ill|Satoshi Fujita|ja|藤田聡|12=draft}} as one of the {{ill|Japan's Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs|ja|日本三大美肌の湯|12=draft}} (the other two being {{ill|Hinokami Onsen|ja|斐乃上温泉|12=draft}} and {{ill|Kirekawa Onsen|ja|喜連川温泉|12=draft}}). == Onsen Town == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Siebold-no-yu.jpg|thumb|300px|{{Center|Siebold's Bath (シーボルトの湯)}} ]] This hot spring area, which rises in the heart of the town, is one of the largest onsen towns in Kyushu. Nearly 50 {{ill|Ryokan|ja|旅館|12=draft}} – both large and small – line the streets along the banks of the {{ill|Shioda River|ja|塩田川 (佐賀県)|lt=Shioda River|lt_ja=塩田川|12=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ureshino River|ja|嬉野川|12=draft}}), including Wataya Villa, where {{ill|Emperor Shōwa|ja|昭和天皇|12=draft}} stayed during the 38th {{ill|National Tree Planting Festival|ja|全国植樹祭|12=draft}} held in Saga Prefecture in 1987 (Showa 62). In addition, the oldest inn in Ureshino is said to be {{ill|Omuraya|ja|大村屋|12=draft}}, founded in 1830 (the first year of the Tenpō era). In the center of the shopping district’s footbath plaza, there is “{{ill|Siebold|ja|フィリップ・フランツ・フォン・シーボルト|lt=Siebold|lt_ja=シーボルト|12=draft}}’s Foot Bath,” which is available free of charge. Nearby stands the wooden, two-story (partly three-story) with one basement {{ill|Public Bath|ja|公衆浴場|12=draft}} “Furuyu Onsen,” constructed in 1924 (Taishō 13) to a design by a {{ill|German|ja|ドイツ人|12=draft}}. Although by around 2001 its interior and piping had deteriorated, the building’s exterior remained in nearly excellent condition{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀県の近代化遺産-佐賀県近代化遺産（建造物等）総合調査報告書-|year=2002|publisher=佐賀県教育委員会|page=182|series=佐賀県文化財調査報告書第153集}}. However, it was demolished on March 20, 2005 (Heisei 17) due to damage from the {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture Western Offshore Earthquake|ja|福岡県西方沖地震|12=draft}}. Later, in response to local demand, it was reconstructed to replicate its Taishō-era appearance and reopened on April 1, 2010 (Heisei 22) under the new name “Siebold’s Bath”{{Cite web |title=＜重点報道＠嬉野市＞わがまち今昔 シーボルトの湯 {{!}} まちの話題 {{!}} 佐賀新聞ニュース |url=https://www.saga-s.co.jp/articles/-/1114588 |website=佐賀新聞 |date=2024-04-09 |access-date=2024-04-09 |language=ja}}. Also known as the “Hot Spring for Beautiful Skin,” Ureshino Onsen is suitable for drinking. Its signature dish, the hot spring {{ill|Hot Spring Tofu|ja|湯豆腐|12=draft}}, prepared using the onsen water, is a renowned specialty of Ureshino. In Ureshino City the product is written as “Yudōfu,” and the name “Ureshino Onsen Yudōfu” is trademarked by the city. == History == [[File:Ureshino Onsen 01.jpg|thumb|280px|{{Center|Onsen Town|1=Spa Town|lt=Onsen Town}} ]] Ureshino Onsen first appears in historical records in the ''Hizen Province Fudoki'' ({{ill|Hizen Province Fudoki|ja|肥前国風土記|12=draft}}), compiled during the Nara period, with a description as a “hot spring that cures the ailments of all people,” although its name is not mentioned嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、272頁. According to legend, {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后|12=draft}} discovered the hot spring on her return from the {{ill|Conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea|ja|三韓征伐|12=draft}} and, while soothing her soldiers’ fatigue, exclaimed something akin to “How delightful!”—a remark that was later associated with the naming of “Ureshino.” Other legends tell of either Prince Takaso (from the ''Daidōji Kyuuki'') or an old woman (from the legend of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|12=draft}}) exclaiming “ureshi.” These tales, however, were retroactively linked after the name “Ureshino” (originally read “ureshino”) was established, and the exclamation is not considered directly connected to the place name. In fact, the term “ureshino” is first confirmed in historical documents during the Kamakura period, when it was written as “宇礼志野”嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、351～353頁. The origin of the name is attributed to a field located in the upper reaches of the Shioda River; because the word “末” (ure) means “tip” or “end,” the area was called “Sueshino” and later a kanji was assigned to form the name{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀地名うんちく事典|year=2005|publisher=佐賀新聞社|page=93}}. After a period with few records concerning the hot spring, by the late Sengoku period (1570s) records emerge of {{ill|Ryūzōji Takanobu|ja|龍造寺隆信|12=draft}} recommending hot spring therapy in Ureshino嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、710頁. During the {{ill|Edo Period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft}}, Ureshino Onsen flourished as Ureshino-juku, a {{ill|Post Town|ja|宿場町|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Nagasaki Kaidō|ja|長崎街道|12=draft}}. In 1656 (Meireki 2), during the time of the first lord of the {{ill|Hasuike Domain|ja|蓮池藩|12=draft}}, Nabeshima Naotoshi, management of the spring source – previously under the jurisdiction of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|12=draft}} – was transferred to the domain, and a roof was added to the open-air bath, converting it into a domain-run bathhouse. The post town was frequented by many travelers, and the state of Ureshino Onsen was recorded in works such as ''Wakan Sansai Zue'' and ''Edo Travelogue''. It appears that from this period it also became known as an entertainment hot spring. After World War II, Ureshino Onsen gained fame as an entertainment hot spring comparable to {{ill|Beppu Onsen|ja|別府温泉|lt=Beppu|lt_ja=別府|12=draft}} in the west. However, each onsen inn has its own distinctive style and character, and while many events are held, comparatively few new facilities have been introduced. In the former Ureshino Town (now part of {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|12=draft}}) tea has been cultivated for generations. For this reason, Ureshino City and its tourism association actively promote the area as '''"Hot Spring Land of Tea and Tofu"''', and various initiatives have been undertaken to link the two. In addition, a 2D character themed on hot springs, “Ureshino Rokka” (from {{ill|Onsen Musume|ja|温泉むすめ|12=draft}}), is used to promote the hot springs{{Cite web |url=https://onsen-musume.jp/character/ureshino_rikka |title=嬉野 六香 |access-date=2024-09-22 |publisher=株式会社エンバウンド |website=温泉むすめ公式サイト}}. == Access == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Tofu.jpg|thumb|190px|{{Center|A Famous Specialty from the Edo Period
'Hot Spring Tofu'}} ]] * Railway (access from {{ill|JR Kyushu|ja|九州旅客鉄道|lt=JR Kyushu|lt_ja=JR九州|12=draft}} stations) ** About 13 minutes by {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|12=draft}} from {{ill|Ureshino Onsen Station|ja|嬉野温泉駅|12=draft}} on the {{ill|West Kyushu Shinkansen|ja|西九州新幹線|12=draft}}. ** About 30 minutes by {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|12=draft}} from {{ill|Takeo Onsen Station|ja|武雄温泉駅|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Sasebo Line|ja|佐世保線|12=draft}}. ** About 1 hour by {{ill|Nishi-Hii Bus|ja|西肥自動車|lt=Nishi-Hii Bus|lt_ja=西肥バス|12=draft}} from {{ill|Sasebo Station|ja|佐世保駅|12=draft}} on the Sasebo Line. ** About 30 minutes by {{ill|Yūtoku Bus|ja|祐徳自動車|lt=Yūtoku Bus|lt_ja=祐徳バス|12=draft}} from {{ill|Hizen Kashima Station|ja|肥前鹿島駅|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Nagasaki Main Line|ja|長崎本線|12=draft}}. ** About 25 minutes by {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|12=draft}} from {{ill|Karinoki Station|ja|彼杵駅|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Omura Line|ja|大村線|12=draft}}. * Highway Bus *: Use the “{{ill|Kyushu-go|ja|九州号|12=draft}}” operated by {{ill|Kyushu Express Bus|ja|九州急行バス|12=draft}}. There are services that stop at the Ureshino Bus Center ({{ill|National Route 34|ja|国道34号|12=draft}}) in the hot spring town and services that stop only at the {{ill|Ureshino Interchange|ja|嬉野インターチェンジ|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Nagasaki Expressway|ja|長崎自動車道|12=draft}}. In recent years, the latter has far more frequent service – while the former runs only 4 times a day, the latter operates roughly every 30 minutes. ** About 2 hours from {{ill|Fukuoka City|ja|福岡市|12=draft}} (via {{ill|Hakata Bus Terminal|ja|博多バスターミナル|12=draft}} and {{ill|Nishitetsu Tenjin Express Bus Terminal|ja|西鉄天神高速バスターミナル|12=draft}}). ** About 1 hour from {{ill|Nagasaki City|ja|長崎市|12=draft}} (from {{ill|Nagasaki Station|ja|長崎駅|lt=Nagasaki Station Front|lt_ja=長崎駅前|12=draft}}). * Shared Taxi from the Airport *: With the opening of {{ill|Saga Airport|ja|佐賀空港|12=draft}}, local taxi companies began operating services. The travel time from Saga Airport is approximately 1 hour. * Private Car *: 5 minutes via the {{ill|Nagasaki Prefectural and Saga Prefectural Route 1 Sasebo-Ureshino Line|ja|長崎県道・佐賀県道1号佐世保嬉野線|12=draft}} from the Ureshino Interchange on the {{ill|Nagasaki Expressway|ja|長崎自動車道|12=draft}}. == References == == Related Literature == *{{Cite book |Language=Japanese Along with {{ill|Takeo Onsen|ja|武雄温泉|12=draft}}, it is one of the representative hot springs of the prefecture. It has been selected as one of {{ill|Japan's 100 Views|ja|日本百景|12=draft}} and is trademarked by Ureshino City under the names “Japan’s Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs Ureshino Onsen” and “Saga–Ureshino Onsen.” == Water Type == * Sodium – Bicarbonate Salt / Chloride Hot Spring It is a baking soda spring renowned for its beauty-enhancing properties, leaving the skin exceptionally smooth after a {{ill|Bathing|ja|入浴|12=draft}}. Its water quality was chosen by {{ill|Satoshi Fujita|ja|藤田聡|12=draft}} as one of the {{ill|Japan's Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs|ja|日本三大美肌の湯|12=draft}} (the other two being {{ill|Hinokami Onsen|ja|斐乃上温泉|12=draft}} and {{ill|Kirekawa Onsen|ja|喜連川温泉|12=draft}}). == Onsen Town == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Siebold-no-yu.jpg|thumb|300px|{{Center|Siebold's Bath (シーボルトの湯)}} ]] This hot spring area, which rises in the heart of the town, is one of the largest onsen towns in Kyushu. Nearly 50 {{ill|Ryokan|ja|旅館|12=draft}} – both large and small – line the streets along the banks of the {{ill|Shioda River|ja|塩田川 (佐賀県)|lt=Shioda River|lt_ja=塩田川|12=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ureshino River|ja|嬉野川|12=draft}}), including Wataya Villa, where {{ill|Emperor Shōwa|ja|昭和天皇|12=draft}} stayed during the 38th {{ill|National Tree Planting Festival|ja|全国植樹祭|12=draft}} held in Saga Prefecture in 1987 (Showa 62). In addition, the oldest inn in Ureshino is said to be {{ill|Omuraya|ja|大村屋|12=draft}}, founded in 1830 (the first year of the Tenpō era). In the center of the shopping district’s footbath plaza, there is “{{ill|Siebold|ja|フィリップ・フランツ・フォン・シーボルト|lt=Siebold|lt_ja=シーボルト|12=draft}}’s Foot Bath,” which is available free of charge. Nearby stands the wooden, two-story (partly three-story) with one basement {{ill|Public Bath|ja|公衆浴場|12=draft}} “Furuyu Onsen,” constructed in 1924 (Taishō 13) to a design by a {{ill|German|ja|ドイツ人|12=draft}}. Although by around 2001 its interior and piping had deteriorated, the building’s exterior remained in nearly excellent condition{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀県の近代化遺産-佐賀県近代化遺産（建造物等）総合調査報告書-|year=2002|publisher=佐賀県教育委員会|page=182|series=佐賀県文化財調査報告書第153集}}. However, it was demolished on March 20, 2005 (Heisei 17) due to damage from the {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture Western Offshore Earthquake|ja|福岡県西方沖地震|12=draft}}. Later, in response to local demand, it was reconstructed to replicate its Taishō-era appearance and reopened on April 1, 2010 (Heisei 22) under the new name “Siebold’s Bath”{{Cite web |title=＜重点報道＠嬉野市＞わがまち今昔 シーボルトの湯 {{!}} まちの話題 {{!}} 佐賀新聞ニュース |url=https://www.saga-s.co.jp/articles/-/1114588 |website=佐賀新聞 |date=2024-04-09 |access-date=2024-04-09 |language=ja}}. Also known as the “Hot Spring for Beautiful Skin,” Ureshino Onsen is suitable for drinking. Its signature dish, the hot spring {{ill|Hot Spring Tofu|ja|湯豆腐|12=draft}}, prepared using the onsen water, is a renowned specialty of Ureshino. In Ureshino City the product is written as “Yudōfu,” and the name “Ureshino Onsen Yudōfu” is trademarked by the city. == History == [[File:Ureshino Onsen 01.jpg|thumb|280px|{{Center|Onsen Town|1=Spa Town|lt=Onsen Town}} ]] Ureshino Onsen first appears in historical records in the ''Hizen Province Fudoki'' ({{ill|Hizen Province Fudoki|ja|肥前国風土記|12=draft}}), compiled during the Nara period, with a description as a “hot spring that cures the ailments of all people,” although its name is not mentioned嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、272頁. According to legend, {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后|12=draft}} discovered the hot spring on her return from the {{ill|Conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea|ja|三韓征伐|12=draft}} and, while soothing her soldiers’ fatigue, exclaimed something akin to “How delightful!”—a remark that was later associated with the naming of “Ureshino.” Other legends tell of either Prince Takaso (from the ''Daidōji Kyuuki'') or an old woman (from the legend of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|12=draft}}) exclaiming “ureshi.” These tales, however, were retroactively linked after the name “Ureshino” (originally read “ureshino”) was established, and the exclamation is not considered directly connected to the place name. In fact, the term “ureshino” is first confirmed in historical documents during the Kamakura period, when it was written as “宇礼志野”嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、351～353頁. The origin of the name is attributed to a field located in the upper reaches of the Shioda River; because the word “末” (ure) means “tip” or “end,” the area was called “Sueshino” and later a kanji was assigned to form the name{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀地名うんちく事典|year=2005|publisher=佐賀新聞社|page=93}}. After a period with few records concerning the hot spring, by the late Sengoku period (1570s) records emerge of {{ill|Ryūzōji Takanobu|ja|龍造寺隆信|12=draft}} recommending hot spring therapy in Ureshino嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、710頁. During the {{ill|Edo Period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft}}, Ureshino Onsen flourished as Ureshino-juku, a {{ill|Post Town|ja|宿場町|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Nagasaki Kaidō|ja|長崎街道|12=draft}}. In 1656 (Meireki 2), during the time of the first lord of the {{ill|Hasuike Domain|ja|蓮池藩|12=draft}}, Nabeshima Naotoshi, management of the spring source – previously under the jurisdiction of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|12=draft}} – was transferred to the domain, and a roof was added to the open-air bath, converting it into a domain-run bathhouse. The post town was frequented by many travelers, and the state of Ureshino Onsen was recorded in works such as ''Wakan Sansai Zue'' and ''Edo Travelogue''. It appears that from this period it also became known as an entertainment hot spring. After World War II, Ureshino Onsen gained fame as an entertainment hot spring comparable to {{ill|Beppu Onsen|ja|別府温泉|lt=Beppu|lt_ja=別府|12=draft}} in the west. However, each onsen inn has its own distinctive style and character, and while many events are held, comparatively few new facilities have been introduced. In the former Ureshino Town (now part of {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|12=draft}}) tea has been cultivated for generations. For this reason, Ureshino City and its tourism association actively promote the area as '''"Hot Spring Land of Tea and Tofu"''', and various initiatives have been undertaken to link the two. {{infobox Onsen |Name = Ureshino Onsen |image = Ureshino onsen.jpg |Comment = |Location = {{ill|Saga Prefecture|ja|佐賀県|12=draft}} {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|12=draft}} {{ill|Ureshino Town|ja|嬉野町 (佐賀県)|lt=Ureshino Town|lt_ja=嬉野町|12=draft}} |Access = Railway : {{ill|Sasebo Line|ja|佐世保線|12=draft}} {{ill|Takeo Onsen Station|ja|武雄温泉駅|12=draft}} via {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|12=draft}} for about 30 minutes

''For other access methods, see [[#アクセス|Access]]'' |Water Type = {{ill|Chloride Hot Spring|ja|塩化物泉|12=draft}} |Temperature = |Discharge = |pH =7.8 |Liquid Classification = |Osmotic Pressure Classification = |Number of Accommodations = |Total Capacity = |Annual Bath Visitors = |Statistical Year = |External links = [https://spa-u.net/ Ureshino Onsen Tourism Association] |Special Notes = }} '''Ureshino Onsen''' (嬉野温泉) is a {{ill|Hot Spring|ja|温泉|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Saga Prefecture|ja|佐賀県|12=draft}}, {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Ureshino Town|ja|嬉野町 (佐賀県)|lt=Ureshino Town|lt_ja=嬉野町|12=draft}} (formerly part of {{ill|Hizen Province|ja|肥前国|12=draft}}). Along with {{ill|Takeo Onsen|ja|武雄温泉|12=draft}}, it is one of the representative hot springs of the prefecture. It has been selected as one of {{ill|Japan's 100 Views|ja|日本百景|12=draft}} and is trademarked by Ureshino City under the names “Japan’s Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs Ureshino Onsen” and “Saga–Ureshino Onsen.” == Water Type == * Sodium – Bicarbonate Salt / Chloride Hot Spring It is a baking soda spring renowned for its beauty-enhancing properties, leaving the skin exceptionally smooth after a {{ill|Bathing|ja|入浴|12=draft}}. Its water quality was chosen by {{ill|Satoshi Fujita|ja|藤田聡|12=draft}} as one of the {{ill|Japan's Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs|ja|日本三大美肌の湯|12=draft}} (the other two being {{ill|Hinokami Onsen|ja|斐乃上温泉|12=draft}} and {{ill|Kirekawa Onsen|ja|喜連川温泉|12=draft}}). == Onsen Town == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Siebold-no-yu.jpg|thumb|300px|{{Center|Siebold's Bath (シーボルトの湯)}} ]] This hot spring area, which rises in the heart of the town, is one of the largest onsen towns in Kyushu. Nearly 50 {{ill|Ryokan|ja|旅館|12=draft}} – both large and small – line the streets along the banks of the {{ill|Shioda River|ja|塩田川 (佐賀県)|lt=Shioda River|lt_ja=塩田川|12=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ureshino River|ja|嬉野川|12=draft}}), including Wataya Villa, where {{ill|Emperor Shōwa|ja|昭和天皇|12=draft}} stayed during the 38th {{ill|National Tree Planting Festival|ja|全国植樹祭|12=draft}} held in Saga Prefecture in 1987 (Showa 62). In addition, the oldest inn in Ureshino is said to be {{ill|Omuraya|ja|大村屋|12=draft}}, founded in 1830 (the first year of the Tenpō era). In the center of the shopping district’s footbath plaza, there is “{{ill|Siebold|ja|フィリップ・フランツ・フォン・シーボルト|lt=Siebold|lt_ja=シーボルト|12=draft}}’s Foot Bath,” which is available free of charge. Nearby stands the wooden, two-story (partly three-story) with one basement {{ill|Public Bath|ja|公衆浴場|12=draft}} “Furuyu Onsen,” constructed in 1924 (Taishō 13) to a design by a {{ill|German|ja|ドイツ人|12=draft}}. Although by around 2001 its interior and piping had deteriorated, the building’s exterior remained in nearly excellent condition{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀県の近代化遺産-佐賀県近代化遺産（建造物等）総合調査報告書-|year=2002|publisher=佐賀県教育委員会|page=182|series=佐賀県文化財調査報告書第153集}}. However, it was demolished on March 20, 2005 (Heisei 17) due to damage from the {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture Western Offshore Earthquake|ja|福岡県西方沖地震|12=draft}}. Later, in response to local demand, it was reconstructed to replicate its Taishō-era appearance and reopened on April 1, 2010 (Heisei 22) under the new name “Siebold’s Bath”{{Cite web |title=＜重点報道＠嬉野市＞わがまち今昔 シーボルトの湯 {{!}} まちの話題 {{!}} 佐賀新聞ニュース |url=https://www.saga-s.co.jp/articles/-/1114588 |website=佐賀新聞 |date=2024-04-09 |access-date=2024-04-09 |language=ja}}. Also known as the “Hot Spring for Beautiful Skin,” Ureshino Onsen is suitable for drinking. Its signature dish, the hot spring {{ill|Hot Spring Tofu|ja|湯豆腐|12=draft}}, prepared using the onsen water, is a renowned specialty of Ureshino. In Ureshino City the product is written as “Yudōfu,” and the name “Ureshino Onsen Yudōfu” is trademarked by the city. == History == [[File:Ureshino Onsen 01.jpg|thumb|280px|{{Center|Onsen Town|1=Spa Town|lt=Onsen Town}} ]] Ureshino Onsen first appears in historical records in the ''Hizen Province Fudoki'' ({{ill|Hizen Province Fudoki|ja|肥前国風土記|12=draft}}), compiled during the Nara period, with a description as a “hot spring that cures the ailments of all people,” although its name is not mentioned嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、272頁. According to legend, {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后|12=draft}} discovered the hot spring on her return from the {{ill|Conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea|ja|三韓征伐|12=draft}} and, while soothing her soldiers’ fatigue, exclaimed something akin to “How delightful!”—a remark that was later associated with the naming of “Ureshino.” Other legends tell of either Prince Takaso (from the ''Daidōji Kyuuki'') or an old woman (from the legend of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|12=draft}}) exclaiming “ureshi.” These tales, however, were retroactively linked after the name “Ureshino” (originally read “ureshino”) was established, and the exclamation is not considered directly connected to the place name. In fact, the term “ureshino” is first confirmed in historical documents during the Kamakura period, when it was written as “宇礼志野”嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、351～353頁. The origin of the name is attributed to a field located in the upper reaches of the Shioda River; because the word “末” (ure) means “tip” or “end,” the area was called “Sueshino” and later a kanji was assigned to form the name{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀地名うんちく事典|year=2005|publisher=佐賀新聞社|page=93}}. After a period with few records concerning the hot spring, by the late Sengoku period (1570s) records emerge of {{ill|Ryūzōji Takanobu|ja|龍造寺隆信|12=draft}} recommending hot spring therapy in Ureshino嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、710頁. During the {{ill|Edo Period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft}}, Ureshino Onsen flourished as Ureshino-juku, a {{ill|Post Town|ja|宿場町|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Nagasaki Kaidō|ja|長崎街道|12=draft}}. In 1656 (Meireki 2), during the time of the first lord of the {{ill|Hasuike Domain|ja|蓮池藩|12=draft}}, Nabeshima Naotoshi, management of the spring source – previously under the jurisdiction of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|12=draft}} – was transferred to the domain, and a roof was added to the open-air bath, converting it into a domain-run bathhouse. The post town was frequented by many travelers, and the state of Ureshino Onsen was recorded in works such as ''Wakan Sansai Zue'' and ''Edo Travelogue''. It appears that from this period it also became known as an entertainment hot spring. After World War II, Ureshino Onsen gained fame as an entertainment hot spring comparable to {{ill|Beppu Onsen|ja|別府温泉|lt=Beppu|lt_ja=別府|12=draft}} in the west. However, each onsen inn has its own distinctive style and character, and while many events are held, comparatively few new facilities have been introduced. In the former Ureshino Town (now part of {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|12=draft}}) tea has been cultivated for generations. For this reason, Ureshino City and its tourism association actively promote the area as '''"Hot Spring Land of Tea and Tofu"''', and various initiatives have been undertaken to link the two. In addition, a 2D character themed on hot springs, “Ureshino Rokka” (from {{ill|Onsen Musume|ja|温泉むすめ|12=draft}}), is used to promote the hot springs{{Cite web |url=https://onsen-musume.jp/character/ureshino_rikka |title=嬉野 六香 |access-date=2024-09-22 |publisher=株式会社エンバウンド |website=温泉むすめ公式サイト}}. == Access == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Tofu.jpg|thumb|190px|{{Center|A Famous Specialty from the Edo Period

''For other access methods, see [[#アクセス|Access]]'' |Water Type = {{ill|Chloride Hot Spring|ja|塩化物泉|12=draft}} |Temperature = |Discharge = |pH =7.8 |Liquid Classification = |Osmotic Pressure Classification = |Number of Accommodations = |Total Capacity = |Annual Bath Visitors = |Statistical Year = |External links = [https://spa-u.net/ Ureshino Onsen Tourism Association] |Special Notes = }} '''Ureshino Onsen''' (嬉野温泉) is a {{ill|Hot Spring|ja|温泉|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Saga Prefecture|ja|佐賀県|12=draft}}, {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Ureshino Town|ja|嬉野町 (佐賀県)|lt=Ureshino Town|lt_ja=嬉野町|12=draft}} (formerly part of {{ill|Hizen Province|ja|肥前国|12=draft}}). Along with {{ill|Takeo Onsen|ja|武雄温泉|12=draft}}, it is one of the representative hot springs of the prefecture. It has been selected as one of {{ill|Japan's 100 Views|ja|日本百景|12=draft}} and is trademarked by Ureshino City under the names “Japan’s Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs Ureshino Onsen” and “Saga–Ureshino Onsen.” == Water Type == * Sodium – Bicarbonate Salt / Chloride Hot Spring It is a baking soda spring renowned for its beauty-enhancing properties, leaving the skin exceptionally smooth after a {{ill|Bathing|ja|入浴|12=draft}}. Its water quality was chosen by {{ill|Satoshi Fujita|ja|藤田聡|12=draft}} as one of the {{ill|Japan's Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs|ja|日本三大美肌の湯|12=draft}} (the other two being {{ill|Hinokami Onsen|ja|斐乃上温泉|12=draft}} and {{ill|Kirekawa Onsen|ja|喜連川温泉|12=draft}}). == Onsen Town == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Siebold-no-yu.jpg|thumb|300px|{{Center|Siebold's Bath (シーボルトの湯)}} ]] This hot spring area, which rises in the heart of the town, is one of the largest onsen towns in Kyushu. Nearly 50 {{ill|Ryokan|ja|旅館|12=draft}} – both large and small – line the streets along the banks of the {{ill|Shioda River|ja|塩田川 (佐賀県)|lt=Shioda River|lt_ja=塩田川|12=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ureshino River|ja|嬉野川|12=draft}}), including Wataya Villa, where {{ill|Emperor Shōwa|ja|昭和天皇|12=draft}} stayed during the 38th {{ill|National Tree Planting Festival|ja|全国植樹祭|12=draft}} held in Saga Prefecture in 1987 (Showa 62). In addition, the oldest inn in Ureshino is said to be {{ill|Omuraya|ja|大村屋|12=draft}}, founded in 1830 (the first year of the Tenpō era). In the center of the shopping district’s footbath plaza, there is “{{ill|Siebold|ja|フィリップ・フランツ・フォン・シーボルト|lt=Siebold|lt_ja=シーボルト|12=draft}}’s Foot Bath,” which is available free of charge. Nearby stands the wooden, two-story (partly three-story) with one basement {{ill|Public Bath|ja|公衆浴場|12=draft}} “Furuyu Onsen,” constructed in 1924 (Taishō 13) to a design by a {{ill|German|ja|ドイツ人|12=draft}}. Although by around 2001 its interior and piping had deteriorated, the building’s exterior remained in nearly excellent condition{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀県の近代化遺産-佐賀県近代化遺産（建造物等）総合調査報告書-|year=2002|publisher=佐賀県教育委員会|page=182|series=佐賀県文化財調査報告書第153集}}. However, it was demolished on March 20, 2005 (Heisei 17) due to damage from the {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture Western Offshore Earthquake|ja|福岡県西方沖地震|12=draft}}. Later, in response to local demand, it was reconstructed to replicate its Taishō-era appearance and reopened on April 1, 2010 (Heisei 22) under the new name “Siebold’s Bath”{{Cite web |title=＜重点報道＠嬉野市＞わがまち今昔 シーボルトの湯 {{!}} まちの話題 {{!}} 佐賀新聞ニュース |url=https://www.saga-s.co.jp/articles/-/1114588 |website=佐賀新聞 |date=2024-04-09 |access-date=2024-04-09 |language=ja}}. Also known as the “Hot Spring for Beautiful Skin,” Ureshino Onsen is suitable for drinking. Its signature dish, the hot spring {{ill|Hot Spring Tofu|ja|湯豆腐|12=draft}}, prepared using the onsen water, is a renowned specialty of Ureshino. In Ureshino City the product is written as “Yudōfu,” and the name “Ureshino Onsen Yudōfu” is trademarked by the city. == History == [[File:Ureshino Onsen 01.jpg|thumb|280px|{{Center|Onsen Town|1=Spa Town|lt=Onsen Town}} ]] Ureshino Onsen first appears in historical records in the ''Hizen Province Fudoki'' ({{ill|Hizen Province Fudoki|ja|肥前国風土記|12=draft}}), compiled during the Nara period, with a description as a “hot spring that cures the ailments of all people,” although its name is not mentioned嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、272頁. According to legend, {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后|12=draft}} discovered the hot spring on her return from the {{ill|Conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea|ja|三韓征伐|12=draft}} and, while soothing her soldiers’ fatigue, exclaimed something akin to “How delightful!”—a remark that was later associated with the naming of “Ureshino.” Other legends tell of either Prince Takaso (from the ''Daidōji Kyuuki'') or an old woman (from the legend of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|12=draft}}) exclaiming “ureshi.” These tales, however, were retroactively linked after the name “Ureshino” (originally read “ureshino”) was established, and the exclamation is not considered directly connected to the place name. In fact, the term “ureshino” is first confirmed in historical documents during the Kamakura period, when it was written as “宇礼志野”嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、351～353頁. The origin of the name is attributed to a field located in the upper reaches of the Shioda River; because the word “末” (ure) means “tip” or “end,” the area was called “Sueshino” and later a kanji was assigned to form the name{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀地名うんちく事典|year=2005|publisher=佐賀新聞社|page=93}}. After a period with few records concerning the hot spring, by the late Sengoku period (1570s) records emerge of {{ill|Ryūzōji Takanobu|ja|龍造寺隆信|12=draft}} recommending hot spring therapy in Ureshino嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、710頁. During the {{ill|Edo Period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft}}, Ureshino Onsen flourished as Ureshino-juku, a {{ill|Post Town|ja|宿場町|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Nagasaki Kaidō|ja|長崎街道|12=draft}}. In 1656 (Meireki 2), during the time of the first lord of the {{ill|Hasuike Domain|ja|蓮池藩|12=draft}}, Nabeshima Naotoshi, management of the spring source – previously under the jurisdiction of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|12=draft}} – was transferred to the domain, and a roof was added to the open-air bath, converting it into a domain-run bathhouse. The post town was frequented by many travelers, and the state of Ureshino Onsen was recorded in works such as ''Wakan Sansai Zue'' and ''Edo Travelogue''. It appears that from this period it also became known as an entertainment hot spring. After World War II, Ureshino Onsen gained fame as an entertainment hot spring comparable to {{ill|Beppu Onsen|ja|別府温泉|lt=Beppu|lt_ja=別府|12=draft}} in the west. However, each onsen inn has its own distinctive style and character, and while many events are held, comparatively few new facilities have been introduced. In the former Ureshino Town (now part of {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|12=draft}}) tea has been cultivated for generations. For this reason, Ureshino City and its tourism association actively promote the area as '''"Hot Spring Land of Tea and Tofu"''', and various initiatives have been undertaken to link the two. In addition, a 2D character themed on hot springs, “Ureshino Rokka” (from {{ill|Onsen Musume|ja|温泉むすめ|12=draft}}), is used to promote the hot springs{{Cite web |url=https://onsen-musume.jp/character/ureshino_rikka |title=嬉野 六香 |access-date=2024-09-22 |publisher=株式会社エンバウンド |website=温泉むすめ公式サイト}}. == Access == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Tofu.jpg|thumb|190px|{{Center|A Famous Specialty from the Edo Period

''For other access methods, see [[#アクセス|Access]]'' |Water Type = {{ill|Chloride Hot Spring|ja|塩化物泉|12=draft}} |Temperature = |Discharge = |pH =7.8 |Liquid Classification = |Osmotic Pressure Classification = |Number of Accommodations = |Total Capacity = |Annual Bath Visitors = |Statistical Year = |External links = [https://spa-u.net/ Ureshino Onsen Tourism Association] |Special Notes = }} '''Ureshino Onsen''' (嬉野温泉) is a {{ill|Hot Spring|ja|温泉|1=Onsen|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Saga Prefecture|ja|佐賀県|12=draft}}, {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Ureshino Town|ja|嬉野町 (佐賀県)|lt=Ureshino Town|lt_ja=嬉野町|12=draft}} (formerly part of {{ill|Hizen Province|ja|肥前国|12=draft}}). Along with {{ill|Takeo Onsen|ja|武雄温泉|12=draft}}, it is one of the representative hot springs of the prefecture. It has been selected as one of {{ill|Japan's 100 Views|ja|日本百景|12=draft}} and is trademarked by Ureshino City under the names “Japan’s Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs Ureshino Onsen” and “Saga–Ureshino Onsen.” == Water Type == * Sodium – Bicarbonate Salt / Chloride Hot Spring It is a baking soda spring renowned for its beauty-enhancing properties, leaving the skin exceptionally smooth after a {{ill|Bathing|ja|入浴|12=draft}}. Its water quality was chosen by {{ill|Satoshi Fujita|ja|藤田聡|12=draft}} as one of the {{ill|Japan's Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs|ja|日本三大美肌の湯|12=draft}} (the other two being {{ill|Hinokami Onsen|ja|斐乃上温泉|12=draft}} and {{ill|Kirekawa Onsen|ja|喜連川温泉|12=draft}}). == Onsen Town == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Siebold-no-yu.jpg|thumb|300px|{{Center|Siebold's Bath (シーボルトの湯)}} ]] This hot spring area, which rises in the heart of the town, is one of the largest onsen towns in Kyushu. Nearly 50 {{ill|Ryokan|ja|旅館|12=draft}} – both large and small – line the streets along the banks of the {{ill|Shioda River|ja|塩田川 (佐賀県)|lt=Shioda River|lt_ja=塩田川|12=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ureshino River|ja|嬉野川|12=draft}}), including Wataya Villa, where {{ill|Emperor Shōwa|ja|昭和天皇|12=draft}} stayed during the 38th {{ill|National Tree Planting Festival|ja|全国植樹祭|12=draft}} held in Saga Prefecture in 1987 (Showa 62). ''For other access methods, see [[#アクセス|Access]]'' |Water Type = {{ill|Chloride Hot Spring|ja|塩化物泉|12=draft}} |Temperature = |Discharge = |pH =7.8 |Liquid Classification = |Osmotic Pressure Classification = |Number of Accommodations = |Total Capacity = |Annual Bath Visitors = |Statistical Year = |External links = [https://spa-u.net/ Ureshino Onsen Tourism Association] |Special Notes = }} '''Ureshino Onsen''' (嬉野温泉) is a {{ill|Hot Spring|ja|温泉|1=Onsen|1=Onsen|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Saga Prefecture|ja|佐賀県|12=draft}}, {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Ureshino Town|ja|嬉野町 (佐賀県)|lt=Ureshino Town|lt_ja=嬉野町|12=draft}} (formerly part of {{ill|Hizen Province|ja|肥前国|12=draft}}). Along with {{ill|Takeo Onsen|ja|武雄温泉|12=draft}}, it is one of the representative hot springs of the prefecture. It has been selected as one of {{ill|Japan's 100 Views|ja|日本百景|12=draft}} and is trademarked by Ureshino City under the names “Japan’s Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs Ureshino Onsen” and “Saga–Ureshino Onsen.” == Water Type == * Sodium – Bicarbonate Salt / Chloride Hot Spring It is a baking soda spring renowned for its beauty-enhancing properties, leaving the skin exceptionally smooth after a {{ill|Bathing|ja|入浴|12=draft}}. Its water quality was chosen by {{ill|Satoshi Fujita|ja|藤田聡|12=draft}} as one of the {{ill|Japan's Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs|ja|日本三大美肌の湯|12=draft}} (the other two being {{ill|Hinokami Onsen|ja|斐乃上温泉|12=draft}} and {{ill|Kirekawa Onsen|ja|喜連川温泉|12=draft}}). == Onsen Town == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Siebold-no-yu.jpg|thumb|300px|{{Center|Siebold's Bath (シーボルトの湯)}} ]] This hot spring area, which rises in the heart of the town, is one of the largest onsen towns in Kyushu. Nearly 50 {{ill|Ryokan|ja|旅館|12=draft}} – both large and small – line the streets along the banks of the {{ill|Shioda River|ja|塩田川 (佐賀県)|lt=Shioda River|lt_ja=塩田川|12=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ureshino River|ja|嬉野川|12=draft}}), including Wataya Villa, where {{ill|Emperor Shōwa|ja|昭和天皇|12=draft}} stayed during the 38th {{ill|National Tree Planting Festival|ja|全国植樹祭|12=draft}} held in Saga Prefecture in 1987 (Showa 62). In addition, the oldest inn in Ureshino is said to be {{ill|Omuraya|ja|大村屋|12=draft}}, founded in 1830 (the first year of the Tenpō era). In the center of the shopping district’s footbath plaza, there is “{{ill|Siebold|ja|フィリップ・フランツ・フォン・シーボルト|lt=Siebold|lt_ja=シーボルト|12=draft}}’s Foot Bath,” which is available free of charge. Nearby stands the wooden, two-story (partly three-story) with one basement {{ill|Public Bath|ja|公衆浴場|12=draft}} “Furuyu Onsen,” constructed in 1924 (Taishō 13) to a design by a {{ill|German|ja|ドイツ人|12=draft}}. Although by around 2001 its interior and piping had deteriorated, the building’s exterior remained in nearly excellent condition{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀県の近代化遺産-佐賀県近代化遺産（建造物等）総合調査報告書-|year=2002|publisher=佐賀県教育委員会|page=182|series=佐賀県文化財調査報告書第153集}}. However, it was demolished on March 20, 2005 (Heisei 17) due to damage from the {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture Western Offshore Earthquake|ja|福岡県西方沖地震|12=draft}}. Later, in response to local demand, it was reconstructed to replicate its Taishō-era appearance and reopened on April 1, 2010 (Heisei 22) under the new name “Siebold’s Bath”{{Cite web |title=＜重点報道＠嬉野市＞わがまち今昔 シーボルトの湯 {{!}} まちの話題 {{!}} 佐賀新聞ニュース |url=https://www.saga-s.co.jp/articles/-/1114588 |website=佐賀新聞 |date=2024-04-09 |access-date=2024-04-09 |language=ja}}. Also known as the “Hot Spring for Beautiful Skin,” Ureshino Onsen is suitable for drinking. Its signature dish, the hot spring {{ill|Hot Spring Tofu|ja|湯豆腐|12=draft}}, prepared using the onsen water, is a renowned specialty of Ureshino. In Ureshino City the product is written as “Yudōfu,” and the name “Ureshino Onsen Yudōfu” is trademarked by the city. == History == [[File:Ureshino Onsen 01.jpg|thumb|280px|{{Center|Onsen Town|1=Spa Town|lt=Onsen Town}} ]] Ureshino Onsen first appears in historical records in the ''Hizen Province Fudoki'' ({{ill|Hizen Province Fudoki|ja|肥前国風土記|12=draft}}), compiled during the Nara period, with a description as a “hot spring that cures the ailments of all people,” although its name is not mentioned嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、272頁. According to legend, {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后|12=draft}} discovered the hot spring on her return from the {{ill|Conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea|ja|三韓征伐|12=draft}} and, while soothing her soldiers’ fatigue, exclaimed something akin to “How delightful!”—a remark that was later associated with the naming of “Ureshino.” Other legends tell of either Prince Takaso (from the ''Daidōji Kyuuki'') or an old woman (from the legend of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|12=draft}}) exclaiming “ureshi.” These tales, however, were retroactively linked after the name “Ureshino” (originally read “ureshino”) was established, and the exclamation is not considered directly connected to the place name. In fact, the term “ureshino” is first confirmed in historical documents during the Kamakura period, when it was written as “宇礼志野”嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、351～353頁. The origin of the name is attributed to a field located in the upper reaches of the Shioda River; because the word “末” (ure) means “tip” or “end,” the area was called “Sueshino” and later a kanji was assigned to form the name{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀地名うんちく事典|year=2005|publisher=佐賀新聞社|page=93}}. After a period with few records concerning the hot spring, by the late Sengoku period (1570s) records emerge of {{ill|Ryūzōji Takanobu|ja|龍造寺隆信|12=draft}} recommending hot spring therapy in Ureshino嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、710頁. During the {{ill|Edo Period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft}}, Ureshino Onsen flourished as Ureshino-juku, a {{ill|Post Town|ja|宿場町|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Nagasaki Kaidō|ja|長崎街道|12=draft}}. In 1656 (Meireki 2), during the time of the first lord of the {{ill|Hasuike Domain|ja|蓮池藩|12=draft}}, Nabeshima Naotoshi, management of the spring source – previously under the jurisdiction of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|12=draft}} – was transferred to the domain, and a roof was added to the open-air bath, converting it into a domain-run bathhouse. The post town was frequented by many travelers, and the state of Ureshino Onsen was recorded in works such as ''Wakan Sansai Zue'' and ''Edo Travelogue''. It appears that from this period it also became known as an entertainment hot spring. After World War II, Ureshino Onsen gained fame as an entertainment hot spring comparable to {{ill|Beppu Onsen|ja|別府温泉|lt=Beppu|lt_ja=別府|12=draft}} in the west. However, each onsen inn has its own distinctive style and character, and while many events are held, comparatively few new facilities have been introduced. In the former Ureshino Town (now part of {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|12=draft}}) tea has been cultivated for generations. For this reason, Ureshino City and its tourism association actively promote the area as '''"Hot Spring Land of Tea and Tofu"''', and various initiatives have been undertaken to link the two. In addition, a 2D character themed on hot springs, “Ureshino Rokka” (from {{ill|Onsen Musume|ja|温泉むすめ|12=draft}}), is used to promote the hot springs{{Cite web |url=https://onsen-musume.jp/character/ureshino_rikka |title=嬉野 六香 |access-date=2024-09-22 |publisher=株式会社エンバウンド |website=温泉むすめ公式サイト}}. == Access == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Tofu.jpg|thumb|190px|{{Center|A Famous Specialty from the Edo Period

Nearly 50 {{ill|Ryokan|ja|旅館|12=draft}} – both large and small – line the streets along the banks of the {{ill|Shioda River|ja|塩田川 (佐賀県)|lt=Shioda River|lt_ja=塩田川|12=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ureshino River|ja|嬉野川|12=draft}}), including Wataya Villa, where {{ill|Emperor Shōwa|ja|昭和天皇|12=draft}} stayed during the 38th {{ill|National Tree Planting Festival|ja|全国植樹祭|12=draft}} held in Saga Prefecture in 1987 (Showa 62). In addition, the oldest inn in Ureshino is said to be {{ill|Omuraya|ja|大村屋|12=draft}}, founded in 1830 (the first year of the Tenpō era). In the center of the shopping district’s footbath plaza, there is “{{ill|Siebold|ja|フィリップ・フランツ・フォン・シーボルト|lt=Siebold|lt_ja=シーボルト|12=draft}}’s Foot Bath,” which is available free of charge. Nearby stands the wooden, two-story (partly three-story) with one basement {{ill|Public Bath|ja|公衆浴場|12=draft}} “Furuyu Onsen,” constructed in 1924 (Taishō 13) to a design by a {{ill|German|ja|ドイツ人|12=draft}}. Although by around 2001 its interior and piping had deteriorated, the building’s exterior remained in nearly excellent condition{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀県の近代化遺産-佐賀県近代化遺産（建造物等）総合調査報告書-|year=2002|publisher=佐賀県教育委員会|page=182|series=佐賀県文化財調査報告書第153集}}. However, it was demolished on March 20, 2005 (Heisei 17) due to damage from the {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture Western Offshore Earthquake|ja|福岡県西方沖地震|12=draft}}. Later, in response to local demand, it was reconstructed to replicate its Taishō-era appearance and reopened on April 1, 2010 (Heisei 22) under the new name “Siebold’s Bath”{{Cite web |title=＜重点報道＠嬉野市＞わがまち今昔 シーボルトの湯 {{!}} まちの話題 {{!}} 佐賀新聞ニュース |url=https://www.saga-s.co.jp/articles/-/1114588 |website=佐賀新聞 |date=2024-04-09 |access-date=2024-04-09 |language=ja}}. Also known as the “Hot Spring for Beautiful Skin,” Ureshino Onsen is suitable for drinking. Its signature dish, the hot spring {{ill|Hot Spring Tofu|ja|湯豆腐|12=draft}}, prepared using the onsen water, is a renowned specialty of Ureshino. In Ureshino City the product is written as “Yudōfu,” and the name “Ureshino Onsen Yudōfu” is trademarked by the city. == History == [[File:Ureshino Onsen 01.jpg|thumb|280px|{{Center|Onsen Town|1=Spa Town|lt=Onsen Town}} ]] Ureshino Onsen first appears in historical records in the ''Hizen Province Fudoki'' ({{ill|Hizen Province Fudoki|ja|肥前国風土記|12=draft}}), compiled during the Nara period, with a description as a “hot spring that cures the ailments of all people,” although its name is not mentioned嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、272頁. According to legend, {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后|12=draft}} discovered the hot spring on her return from the {{ill|Conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea|ja|三韓征伐|12=draft}} and, while soothing her soldiers’ fatigue, exclaimed something akin to “How delightful!”—a remark that was later associated with the naming of “Ureshino.” Other legends tell of either Prince Takaso (from the ''Daidōji Kyuuki'') or an old woman (from the legend of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|12=draft}}) exclaiming “ureshi.” These tales, however, were retroactively linked after the name “Ureshino” (originally read “ureshino”) was established, and the exclamation is not considered directly connected to the place name. In fact, the term “ureshino” is first confirmed in historical documents during the Kamakura period, when it was written as “宇礼志野”嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、351～353頁. The origin of the name is attributed to a field located in the upper reaches of the Shioda River; because the word “末” (ure) means “tip” or “end,” the area was called “Sueshino” and later a kanji was assigned to form the name{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀地名うんちく事典|year=2005|publisher=佐賀新聞社|page=93}}. After a period with few records concerning the hot spring, by the late Sengoku period (1570s) records emerge of {{ill|Ryūzōji Takanobu|ja|龍造寺隆信|12=draft}} recommending hot spring therapy in Ureshino嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、710頁. During the {{ill|Edo Period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft}}, Ureshino Onsen flourished as Ureshino-juku, a {{ill|Post Town|ja|宿場町|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Nagasaki Kaidō|ja|長崎街道|12=draft}}. In 1656 (Meireki 2), during the time of the first lord of the {{ill|Hasuike Domain|ja|蓮池藩|12=draft}}, Nabeshima Naotoshi, management of the spring source – previously under the jurisdiction of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|12=draft}} – was transferred to the domain, and a roof was added to the open-air bath, converting it into a domain-run bathhouse. The post town was frequented by many travelers, and the state of Ureshino Onsen was recorded in works such as ''Wakan Sansai Zue'' and ''Edo Travelogue''. It appears that from this period it also became known as an entertainment hot spring. After World War II, Ureshino Onsen gained fame as an entertainment hot spring comparable to {{ill|Beppu Onsen|ja|別府温泉|lt=Beppu|lt_ja=別府|12=draft}} in the west. However, each onsen inn has its own distinctive style and character, and while many events are held, comparatively few new facilities have been introduced. In the former Ureshino Town (now part of {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|12=draft}}) tea has been cultivated for generations. For this reason, Ureshino City and its tourism association actively promote the area as '''"Hot Spring Land of Tea and Tofu"''', and various initiatives have been undertaken to link the two. In addition, a 2D character themed on hot springs, “Ureshino Rokka” (from {{ill|Onsen Musume|ja|温泉むすめ|12=draft}}), is used to promote the hot springs{{Cite web |url=https://onsen-musume.jp/character/ureshino_rikka |title=嬉野 六香 |access-date=2024-09-22 |publisher=株式会社エンバウンド |website=温泉むすめ公式サイト}}. == Access == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Tofu.jpg|thumb|190px|{{Center|A Famous Specialty from the Edo Period
'Hot Spring Tofu'}} ]] * Railway (access from {{ill|JR Kyushu|ja|九州旅客鉄道|lt=JR Kyushu|lt_ja=JR九州|12=draft}} stations) ** About 13 minutes by {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|12=draft}} from {{ill|Ureshino Onsen Station|ja|嬉野温泉駅|12=draft}} on the {{ill|West Kyushu Shinkansen|ja|西九州新幹線|12=draft}}. ** About 30 minutes by {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|12=draft}} from {{ill|Takeo Onsen Station|ja|武雄温泉駅|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Sasebo Line|ja|佐世保線|12=draft}}. ** About 1 hour by {{ill|Nishi-Hii Bus|ja|西肥自動車|lt=Nishi-Hii Bus|lt_ja=西肥バス|12=draft}} from {{ill|Sasebo Station|ja|佐世保駅|12=draft}} on the Sasebo Line. ** About 30 minutes by {{ill|Yūtoku Bus|ja|祐徳自動車|lt=Yūtoku Bus|lt_ja=祐徳バス|12=draft}} from {{ill|Hizen Kashima Station|ja|肥前鹿島駅|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Nagasaki Main Line|ja|長崎本線|12=draft}}. ** About 25 minutes by {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|12=draft}} from {{ill|Karinoki Station|ja|彼杵駅|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Omura Line|ja|大村線|12=draft}}. * Highway Bus *: Use the “{{ill|Kyushu-go|ja|九州号|12=draft}}” operated by {{ill|Kyushu Express Bus|ja|九州急行バス|12=draft}}. There are services that stop at the Ureshino Bus Center ({{ill|National Route 34|ja|国道34号|12=draft}}) in the hot spring town and services that stop only at the {{ill|Ureshino Interchange|ja|嬉野インターチェンジ|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Nagasaki Expressway|ja|長崎自動車道|12=draft}}. In recent years, the latter has far more frequent service – while the former runs only 4 times a day, the latter operates roughly every 30 minutes. ** About 2 hours from {{ill|Fukuoka City|ja|福岡市|12=draft}} (via {{ill|Hakata Bus Terminal|ja|博多バスターミナル|12=draft}} and {{ill|Nishitetsu Tenjin Express Bus Terminal|ja|西鉄天神高速バスターミナル|12=draft}}). ** About 1 hour from {{ill|Nagasaki City|ja|長崎市|12=draft}} (from {{ill|Nagasaki Station|ja|長崎駅|lt=Nagasaki Station Front|lt_ja=長崎駅前|12=draft}}). * Shared Taxi from the Airport *: With the opening of {{ill|Saga Airport|ja|佐賀空港|12=draft}}, local taxi companies began operating services. The travel time from Saga Airport is approximately 1 hour. * Private Car *: 5 minutes via the {{ill|Nagasaki Prefectural and Saga Prefectural Route 1 Sasebo-Ureshino Line|ja|長崎県道・佐賀県道1号佐世保嬉野線|12=draft}} from the Ureshino Interchange on the {{ill|Nagasaki Expressway|ja|長崎自動車道|12=draft}}. == References == == Related Literature == *{{Cite book |Language=Japanese |author=Masamichi Ikeda|year=1898|title=Ureshino Onsen Chronicles|id={{NDLJP|766546}}|quote= }} == See Also == {{commonscat|Ureshino Onsen}} * {{ill|Tourist Attractions in Saga Prefecture|ja|佐賀県の観光地|12=draft}} * {{ill|West Kyushu Shinkansen|ja|西九州新幹線|12=draft}} * {{ill|Ureshino Onsen Station|ja|嬉野温泉駅|12=draft}} * {{ill|Hizen Dream Road|ja|肥前夢街道|12=draft}} * {{ill|Wataya Along with {{ill|Takeo Onsen|ja|武雄温泉|12=draft|12=draft}}, it is one of the representative hot springs of the prefecture. It has been selected as one of {{ill|Japan's 100 Views|ja|日本百景|12=draft|12=draft}} and is trademarked by Ureshino City under the names “Japan’s Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs Ureshino Onsen” and “Saga–Ureshino Onsen.” == Water Type == * Sodium – Bicarbonate Salt / Chloride Hot Spring It is a baking soda spring renowned for its beauty-enhancing properties, leaving the skin exceptionally smooth after a {{ill|Bathing|ja|入浴|12=draft|12=draft}}. Its water quality was chosen by {{ill|Satoshi Fujita|ja|藤田聡|12=draft|12=draft}} as one of the {{ill|Japan's Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs|ja|日本三大美肌の湯|12=draft|12=draft}} (the other two being {{ill|Hinokami Onsen|ja|斐乃上温泉|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Kirekawa Onsen|ja|喜連川温泉|12=draft|12=draft}}). == Onsen Town == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Siebold-no-yu.jpg|thumb|300px|{{Center|Siebold's Bath (シーボルトの湯)}} ]] This hot spring area, which rises in the heart of the town, is one of the largest onsen towns in Kyushu. {{infobox Onsen |Name = Ureshino Onsen |image = Ureshino onsen.jpg |Comment = |Location = {{ill|Saga Prefecture|ja|佐賀県|12=draft|12=draft}} {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|12=draft|12=draft}} {{ill|Ureshino Town|ja|嬉野町 (佐賀県)|lt=Ureshino Town|lt_ja=嬉野町|12=draft|12=draft}} |Access = Railway : {{ill|Sasebo Line|ja|佐世保線|12=draft|12=draft}} {{ill|Takeo Onsen Station|ja|武雄温泉駅|12=draft|12=draft}} via {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|12=draft|12=draft}} for about 30 minutes
West Kyushu Shinkansen Ureshino Onsen Station
''For other access methods, see [[#アクセス|Access]]'' |Water Type = {{ill|Chloride Hot Spring|ja|塩化物泉|12=draft|12=draft}} |Temperature = |Discharge = |pH =7.8 |Liquid Classification = |Osmotic Pressure Classification = |Number of Accommodations = |Total Capacity = |Annual Bath Visitors = |Statistical Year = |External links = [https://spa-u.net/ Ureshino Onsen Tourism Association] |Special Notes = }} '''Ureshino Onsen''' (嬉野温泉) is a {{ill|Hot Spring|ja|温泉|1=Onsen|1=Onsen|12=draft|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Saga Prefecture|ja|佐賀県|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|12=draft|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Ureshino Town|ja|嬉野町 (佐賀県)|lt=Ureshino Town|lt_ja=嬉野町|12=draft|12=draft}} (formerly part of {{ill|Hizen Province|ja|肥前国|12=draft|12=draft}}). Along with {{ill|Takeo Onsen|ja|武雄温泉|12=draft|12=draft}}, it is one of the representative hot springs of the prefecture. It has been selected as one of {{ill|Japan's 100 Views|ja|日本百景|12=draft|12=draft}} and is trademarked by Ureshino City under the names “Japan’s Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs Ureshino Onsen” and “Saga–Ureshino Onsen.” == Water Type == * Sodium – Bicarbonate Salt / Chloride Hot Spring It is a baking soda spring renowned for its beauty-enhancing properties, leaving the skin exceptionally smooth after a {{ill|Bathing|ja|入浴|12=draft|12=draft}}. Its water quality was chosen by {{ill|Satoshi Fujita|ja|藤田聡|12=draft|12=draft}} as one of the {{ill|Japan's Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs|ja|日本三大美肌の湯|12=draft|12=draft}} (the other two being {{ill|Hinokami Onsen|ja|斐乃上温泉|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Kirekawa Onsen|ja|喜連川温泉|12=draft|12=draft}}). == Onsen Town == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Siebold-no-yu.jpg|thumb|300px|{{Center|Siebold's Bath (シーボルトの湯)}} ]] This hot spring area, which rises in the heart of the town, is one of the largest onsen towns in Kyushu. Nearly 50 {{ill|Ryokan|ja|旅館|12=draft|12=draft}} – both large and small – line the streets along the banks of the {{ill|Shioda River|ja|塩田川 (佐賀県)|lt=Shioda River|lt_ja=塩田川|12=draft|12=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ureshino River|ja|嬉野川|12=draft|12=draft}}), including Wataya Villa, where {{ill|Emperor Shōwa|ja|昭和天皇|12=draft|12=draft}} stayed during the 38th {{ill|National Tree Planting Festival|ja|全国植樹祭|12=draft|12=draft}} held in Saga Prefecture in 1987 (Showa 62). In addition, the oldest inn in Ureshino is said to be {{ill|Omuraya|ja|大村屋|12=draft|12=draft}}, founded in 1830 (the first year of the Tenpō era). In the center of the shopping district’s footbath plaza, there is “{{ill|Siebold|ja|フィリップ・フランツ・フォン・シーボルト|lt=Siebold|lt_ja=シーボルト|12=draft|12=draft}}’s Foot Bath,” which is available free of charge. Nearby stands the wooden, two-story (partly three-story) with one basement {{ill|Public Bath|ja|公衆浴場|1=public bathing|lt=Public Bathhouse|12=draft|12=draft}} “Furuyu Onsen,” constructed in 1924 (Taishō 13) to a design by a {{ill|German|ja|ドイツ人|12=draft|12=draft}}. Although by around 2001 its interior and piping had deteriorated, the building’s exterior remained in nearly excellent condition{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀県の近代化遺産-佐賀県近代化遺産（建造物等）総合調査報告書-|year=2002|publisher=佐賀県教育委員会|page=182|series=佐賀県文化財調査報告書第153集}}. However, it was demolished on March 20, 2005 (Heisei 17) due to damage from the {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture Western Offshore Earthquake|ja|福岡県西方沖地震|12=draft|12=draft}}. Later, in response to local demand, it was reconstructed to replicate its Taishō-era appearance and reopened on April 1, 2010 (Heisei 22) under the new name “Siebold’s Bath”{{Cite web |title=＜重点報道＠嬉野市＞わがまち今昔 シーボルトの湯 {{!}} まちの話題 {{!}} 佐賀新聞ニュース |url=https://www.saga-s.co.jp/articles/-/1114588 |website=佐賀新聞 |date=2024-04-09 |access-date=2024-04-09 |language=ja}}. Also known as the “Hot Spring for Beautiful Skin,” Ureshino Onsen is suitable for drinking. Its signature dish, the hot spring {{ill|Hot Spring Tofu|ja|湯豆腐|12=draft|12=draft}}, prepared using the onsen water, is a renowned specialty of Ureshino. In Ureshino City the product is written as “Yudōfu,” and the name “Ureshino Onsen Yudōfu” is trademarked by the city. == History == [[File:Ureshino Onsen 01.jpg|thumb|280px|{{Center|Onsen Town|1=Spa Town|lt=Onsen Town}} ]] Ureshino Onsen first appears in historical records in the ''Hizen Province Fudoki'' ({{ill|Hizen Province Fudoki|ja|肥前国風土記|12=draft|12=draft}}), compiled during the Nara period, with a description as a “hot spring that cures the ailments of all people,” although its name is not mentioned嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、272頁. According to legend, {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后|12=draft|12=draft}} discovered the hot spring on her return from the {{ill|Conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea|ja|三韓征伐|12=draft|12=draft}} and, while soothing her soldiers’ fatigue, exclaimed something akin to “How delightful!”—a remark that was later associated with the naming of “Ureshino.” Other legends tell of either Prince Takaso (from the ''Daidōji Kyuuki'') or an old woman (from the legend of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|12=draft|12=draft}}) exclaiming “ureshi.” These tales, however, were retroactively linked after the name “Ureshino” (originally read “ureshino”) was established, and the exclamation is not considered directly connected to the place name. In fact, the term “ureshino” is first confirmed in historical documents during the Kamakura period, when it was written as “宇礼志野”嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、351～353頁. The origin of the name is attributed to a field located in the upper reaches of the Shioda River; because the word “末” (ure) means “tip” or “end,” the area was called “Sueshino” and later a kanji was assigned to form the name{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀地名うんちく事典|year=2005|publisher=佐賀新聞社|page=93}}. After a period with few records concerning the hot spring, by the late Sengoku period (1570s) records emerge of {{ill|Ryūzōji Takanobu|ja|龍造寺隆信|12=draft|12=draft}} recommending hot spring therapy in Ureshino嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、710頁. During the {{ill|Edo Period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft|12=draft}}, Ureshino Onsen flourished as Ureshino-juku, a {{ill|Post Town|ja|宿場町|12=draft|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Nagasaki Kaidō|ja|長崎街道|12=draft|12=draft}}. In 1656 (Meireki 2), during the time of the first lord of the {{ill|Hasuike Domain|ja|蓮池藩|12=draft|12=draft}}, Nabeshima Naotoshi, management of the spring source – previously under the jurisdiction of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|12=draft|12=draft}} – was transferred to the domain, and a roof was added to the open-air bath, converting it into a domain-run bathhouse. The post town was frequented by many travelers, and the state of Ureshino Onsen was recorded in works such as ''Wakan Sansai Zue'' and ''Edo Travelogue''. It appears that from this period it also became known as an entertainment hot spring. After World War II, Ureshino Onsen gained fame as an entertainment hot spring comparable to {{ill|Beppu Onsen|ja|別府温泉|lt=Beppu|lt_ja=別府|12=draft|12=draft}} in the west. However, each onsen inn has its own distinctive style and character, and while many events are held, comparatively few new facilities have been introduced. In the former Ureshino Town (now part of {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|12=draft|12=draft}}) tea has been cultivated for generations. For this reason, Ureshino City and its tourism association actively promote the area as '''"Hot Spring Land of Tea and Tofu"''', and various initiatives have been undertaken to link the two. In addition, a 2D character themed on hot springs, “Ureshino Rokka” (from {{ill|Onsen Musume|ja|温泉むすめ|12=draft|12=draft}}), is used to promote the hot springs{{Cite web |url=https://onsen-musume.jp/character/ureshino_rikka |title=嬉野 六香 |access-date=2024-09-22 |publisher=株式会社エンバウンド |website=温泉むすめ公式サイト}}. == Access == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Tofu.jpg|thumb|190px|{{Center|A Famous Specialty from the Edo Period
'Hot Spring Tofu'}} ]] * Railway (access from {{ill|JR Kyushu|ja|九州旅客鉄道|lt=JR Kyushu|lt_ja=JR九州|12=draft|12=draft}} stations) ** About 13 minutes by {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|12=draft|12=draft}} from {{ill|Ureshino Onsen Station|ja|嬉野温泉駅|12=draft|12=draft}} on the {{ill|West Kyushu Shinkansen|ja|西九州新幹線|12=draft|12=draft}}. ** About 30 minutes by {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|12=draft|12=draft}} from {{ill|Takeo Onsen Station|ja|武雄温泉駅|12=draft|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Sasebo Line|ja|佐世保線|12=draft|12=draft}}. ** About 1 hour by {{ill|Nishi-Hii Bus|ja|西肥自動車|lt=Nishi-Hii Bus|lt_ja=西肥バス|12=draft|12=draft}} from {{ill|Sasebo Station|ja|佐世保駅|12=draft|12=draft}} on the Sasebo Line. ** About 30 minutes by {{ill|Yūtoku Bus|ja|祐徳自動車|lt=Yūtoku Bus|lt_ja=祐徳バス|12=draft|12=draft}} from {{ill|Hizen Kashima Station|ja|肥前鹿島駅|12=draft|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Nagasaki Main Line|ja|長崎本線|12=draft|12=draft}}. ** About 25 minutes by {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|12=draft|12=draft}} from {{ill|Karinoki Station|ja|彼杵駅|12=draft|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Omura Line|ja|大村線|12=draft|12=draft}}. * Highway Bus *: Use the “{{ill|Kyushu-go|ja|九州号|12=draft|12=draft}}” operated by {{ill|Kyushu Express Bus|ja|九州急行バス|12=draft|12=draft}}. There are services that stop at the Ureshino Bus Center ({{ill|National Route 34|ja|国道34号|12=draft|12=draft}}) in the hot spring town and services that stop only at the {{ill|Ureshino Interchange|ja|嬉野インターチェンジ|12=draft|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Nagasaki Expressway|ja|長崎自動車道|12=draft|12=draft}}. In recent years, the latter has far more frequent service – while the former runs only 4 times a day, the latter operates roughly every 30 minutes. ** About 2 hours from {{ill|Fukuoka City|ja|福岡市|12=draft|12=draft}} (via {{ill|Hakata Bus Terminal|ja|博多バスターミナル|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Nishitetsu Tenjin Express Bus Terminal|ja|西鉄天神高速バスターミナル|12=draft|12=draft}}). ** About 1 hour from {{ill|Nagasaki City|ja|長崎市|12=draft|12=draft}} (from {{ill|Nagasaki Station|ja|長崎駅|lt=Nagasaki Station Front|lt_ja=長崎駅前|12=draft|12=draft}}). * Shared Taxi from the Airport *: With the opening of {{ill|Saga Airport|ja|佐賀空港|12=draft|12=draft}}, local taxi companies began operating services. The travel time from Saga Airport is approximately 1 hour. * Private Car *: 5 minutes via the {{ill|Nagasaki Prefectural and Saga Prefectural Route 1 Sasebo-Ureshino Line|ja|長崎県道・佐賀県道1号佐世保嬉野線|12=draft|12=draft}} from the Ureshino Interchange on the {{ill|Nagasaki Expressway|ja|長崎自動車道|12=draft|12=draft}}. == References == == Related Literature == *{{Cite book ''For other access methods, see [[#アクセス|Access]]'' |Water Type = {{ill|Chloride Hot Spring|ja|塩化物泉|1=Bring spring|12=draft|12=draft}} |Temperature = |Discharge = |pH =7.8 |Liquid Classification = |Osmotic Pressure Classification = |Number of Accommodations = |Total Capacity = |Annual Bath Visitors = |Statistical Year = |External links = [https://spa-u.net/ Ureshino Onsen Tourism Association] |Special Notes = }} '''Ureshino Onsen''' (嬉野温泉) is a {{ill|Hot Spring|ja|温泉|1=Onsen|1=Onsen|12=draft|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Saga Prefecture|ja|佐賀県|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|12=draft|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Ureshino Town|ja|嬉野町 (佐賀県)|lt=Ureshino Town|lt_ja=嬉野町|12=draft|12=draft}} (formerly part of {{ill|Hizen Province|ja|肥前国|12=draft|12=draft}}). Along with {{ill|Takeo Onsen|ja|武雄温泉|12=draft|12=draft}}, it is one of the representative hot springs of the prefecture. It has been selected as one of {{ill|Japan's 100 Views|ja|日本百景|12=draft|12=draft}} and is trademarked by Ureshino City under the names “Japan’s Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs Ureshino Onsen” and “Saga–Ureshino Onsen.” == Water Type == * Sodium – Bicarbonate Salt / Chloride Hot Spring It is a baking soda spring renowned for its beauty-enhancing properties, leaving the skin exceptionally smooth after a {{ill|Bathing|ja|入浴|12=draft|12=draft}}. Its water quality was chosen by {{ill|Satoshi Fujita|ja|藤田聡|12=draft|12=draft}} as one of the {{ill|Japan's Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs|ja|日本三大美肌の湯|12=draft|12=draft}} (the other two being {{ill|Hinokami Onsen|ja|斐乃上温泉|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Kirekawa Onsen|ja|喜連川温泉|12=draft|12=draft}}). == Onsen Town == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Siebold-no-yu.jpg|thumb|300px|{{Center|Siebold's Bath (シーボルトの湯)}} ]] This hot spring area, which rises in the heart of the town, is one of the largest onsen towns in Kyushu. Nearly 50 {{ill|Ryokan|ja|旅館|12=draft|12=draft}} – both large and small – line the streets along the banks of the {{ill|Shioda River|ja|塩田川 (佐賀県)|lt=Shioda River|lt_ja=塩田川|12=draft|12=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ureshino River|ja|嬉野川|12=draft|12=draft}}), including Wataya Villa, where {{ill|Emperor Shōwa|ja|昭和天皇|12=draft|12=draft}} stayed during the 38th {{ill|National Tree Planting Festival|ja|全国植樹祭|12=draft|12=draft}} held in Saga Prefecture in 1987 (Showa 62). In addition, the oldest inn in Ureshino is said to be {{ill|Omuraya|ja|大村屋|12=draft|12=draft}}, founded in 1830 (the first year of the Tenpō era). In the center of the shopping district’s footbath plaza, there is “{{ill|Siebold|ja|フィリップ・フランツ・フォン・シーボルト|lt=Siebold|lt_ja=シーボルト|12=draft|12=draft}}’s Foot Bath,” which is available free of charge. Nearby stands the wooden, two-story (partly three-story) with one basement {{ill|Public Bath|ja|公衆浴場|1=public bathing|lt=Public Bathhouse|12=draft|12=draft}} “Furuyu Onsen,” constructed in 1924 (Taishō 13) to a design by a {{ill|German|ja|ドイツ人|12=draft|12=draft}}. Although by around 2001 its interior and piping had deteriorated, the building’s exterior remained in nearly excellent condition{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀県の近代化遺産-佐賀県近代化遺産（建造物等）総合調査報告書-|year=2002|publisher=佐賀県教育委員会|page=182|series=佐賀県文化財調査報告書第153集}}. However, it was demolished on March 20, 2005 (Heisei 17) due to damage from the {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture Western Offshore Earthquake|ja|福岡県西方沖地震|12=draft|12=draft}}. Later, in response to local demand, it was reconstructed to replicate its Taishō-era appearance and reopened on April 1, 2010 (Heisei 22) under the new name “Siebold’s Bath”{{Cite web |title=＜重点報道＠嬉野市＞わがまち今昔 シーボルトの湯 {{!}} まちの話題 {{!}} 佐賀新聞ニュース |url=https://www.saga-s.co.jp/articles/-/1114588 |website=佐賀新聞 |date=2024-04-09 |access-date=2024-04-09 |language=ja}}. Also known as the “Hot Spring for Beautiful Skin,” Ureshino Onsen is suitable for drinking. Its signature dish, the hot spring {{ill|Hot Spring Tofu|ja|湯豆腐|12=draft|12=draft}}, prepared using the onsen water, is a renowned specialty of Ureshino. In Ureshino City the product is written as “Yudōfu,” and the name “Ureshino Onsen Yudōfu” is trademarked by the city. == History == [[File:Ureshino Onsen 01.jpg|thumb|280px|{{Center|Onsen Town|1=Spa Town|lt=Onsen Town}} ]] Ureshino Onsen first appears in historical records in the ''Hizen Province Fudoki'' ({{ill|Hizen Province Fudoki|ja|肥前国風土記|12=draft|12=draft}}), compiled during the Nara period, with a description as a “hot spring that cures the ailments of all people,” although its name is not mentioned嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、272頁. According to legend, {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后|12=draft|12=draft}} discovered the hot spring on her return from the {{ill|Conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea|ja|三韓征伐|12=draft|12=draft}} and, while soothing her soldiers’ fatigue, exclaimed something akin to “How delightful!”—a remark that was later associated with the naming of “Ureshino.” Other legends tell of either Prince Takaso (from the ''Daidōji Kyuuki'') or an old woman (from the legend of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|12=draft|12=draft}}) exclaiming “ureshi.” These tales, however, were retroactively linked after the name “Ureshino” (originally read “ureshino”) was established, and the exclamation is not considered directly connected to the place name. In fact, the term “ureshino” is first confirmed in historical documents during the Kamakura period, when it was written as “宇礼志野”嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、351～353頁. The origin of the name is attributed to a field located in the upper reaches of the Shioda River; because the word “末” (ure) means “tip” or “end,” the area was called “Sueshino” and later a kanji was assigned to form the name{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀地名うんちく事典|year=2005|publisher=佐賀新聞社|page=93}}. After a period with few records concerning the hot spring, by the late Sengoku period (1570s) records emerge of {{ill|Ryūzōji Takanobu|ja|龍造寺隆信|12=draft|12=draft}} recommending hot spring therapy in Ureshino嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、710頁. During the {{ill|Edo Period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft|12=draft}}, Ureshino Onsen flourished as Ureshino-juku, a {{ill|Post Town|ja|宿場町|12=draft|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Nagasaki Kaidō|ja|長崎街道|12=draft|12=draft}}. In 1656 (Meireki 2), during the time of the first lord of the {{ill|Hasuike Domain|ja|蓮池藩|12=draft|12=draft}}, Nabeshima Naotoshi, management of the spring source – previously under the jurisdiction of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|12=draft|12=draft}} – was transferred to the domain, and a roof was added to the open-air bath, converting it into a domain-run bathhouse. The post town was frequented by many travelers, and the state of Ureshino Onsen was recorded in works such as ''Wakan Sansai Zue'' and ''Edo Travelogue''. It appears that from this period it also became known as an entertainment hot spring. After World War II, Ureshino Onsen gained fame as an entertainment hot spring comparable to {{ill|Beppu Onsen|ja|別府温泉|lt=Beppu|lt_ja=別府|12=draft|12=draft}} in the west. However, each onsen inn has its own distinctive style and character, and while many events are held, comparatively few new facilities have been introduced. In the former Ureshino Town (now part of {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|12=draft|12=draft}}) tea has been cultivated for generations. For this reason, Ureshino City and its tourism association actively promote the area as '''"Hot Spring Land of Tea and Tofu"''', and various initiatives have been undertaken to link the two. In addition, a 2D character themed on hot springs, “Ureshino Rokka” (from {{ill|Onsen Musume|ja|温泉むすめ|12=draft|12=draft}}), is used to promote the hot springs{{Cite web |url=https://onsen-musume.jp/character/ureshino_rikka |title=嬉野 六香 |access-date=2024-09-22 |publisher=株式会社エンバウンド |website=温泉むすめ公式サイト}}. == Access == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Tofu.jpg|thumb|190px|{{Center|A Famous Specialty from the Edo Period
'Hot Spring Tofu'}} ]] * Railway (access from {{ill|JR Kyushu|ja|九州旅客鉄道|lt=JR Kyushu|lt_ja=JR九州|12=draft|12=draft}} stations) ** About 13 minutes by {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|12=draft|12=draft}} from {{ill|Ureshino Onsen Station|ja|嬉野温泉駅|12=draft|12=draft}} on the {{ill|West Kyushu Shinkansen|ja|西九州新幹線|12=draft|12=draft}}. ** About 30 minutes by {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|12=draft|12=draft}} from {{ill|Takeo Onsen Station|ja|武雄温泉駅|12=draft|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Sasebo Line|ja|佐世保線|12=draft|12=draft}}. ** About 1 hour by {{ill|Nishi-Hii Bus|ja|西肥自動車|lt=Nishi-Hii Bus|lt_ja=西肥バス|12=draft|12=draft}} from {{ill|Sasebo Station|ja|佐世保駅|12=draft|12=draft}} on the Sasebo Line. ** About 30 minutes by {{ill|Yūtoku Bus|ja|祐徳自動車|lt=Yūtoku Bus|lt_ja=祐徳バス|12=draft|12=draft}} from {{ill|Hizen Kashima Station|ja|肥前鹿島駅|12=draft|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Nagasaki Main Line|ja|長崎本線|12=draft|12=draft}}. ** About 25 minutes by {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|12=draft|12=draft}} from {{ill|Karinoki Station|ja|彼杵駅|12=draft|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Omura Line|ja|大村線|12=draft|12=draft}}. * Highway Bus *: Use the “{{ill|Kyushu-go|ja|九州号|12=draft|12=draft}}” operated by {{ill|Kyushu Express Bus|ja|九州急行バス|12=draft|12=draft}}. There are services that stop at the Ureshino Bus Center ({{ill|National Route 34|ja|国道34号|12=draft|12=draft}}) in the hot spring town and services that stop only at the {{ill|Ureshino Interchange|ja|嬉野インターチェンジ|12=draft|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Nagasaki Expressway|ja|長崎自動車道|12=draft|12=draft}}. In recent years, the latter has far more frequent service – while the former runs only 4 times a day, the latter operates roughly every 30 minutes. ** About 2 hours from {{ill|Fukuoka City|ja|福岡市|12=draft|12=draft}} (via {{ill|Hakata Bus Terminal|ja|博多バスターミナル|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Nishitetsu Tenjin Express Bus Terminal|ja|西鉄天神高速バスターミナル|12=draft|12=draft}}). ** About 1 hour from {{ill|Nagasaki City|ja|長崎市|12=draft|12=draft}} (from {{ill|Nagasaki Station|ja|長崎駅|lt=Nagasaki Station Front|lt_ja=長崎駅前|12=draft|12=draft}}). * Shared Taxi from the Airport *: With the opening of {{ill|Saga Airport|ja|佐賀空港|12=draft|12=draft}}, local taxi companies began operating services. The travel time from Saga Airport is approximately 1 hour. * Private Car *: 5 minutes via the {{ill|Nagasaki Prefectural and Saga Prefectural Route 1 Sasebo-Ureshino Line|ja|長崎県道・佐賀県道1号佐世保嬉野線|12=draft|12=draft}} from the Ureshino Interchange on the {{ill|Nagasaki Expressway|ja|長崎自動車道|12=draft|12=draft}}. == References == == Related Literature == *{{Cite book
