{{infobox Onsen |Name = Ureshino Onsen |image = Ureshino onsen.jpg |Comment = |Location = {{ill|Saga Prefecture|ja|佐賀県|12=draft|12=draft}} {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|12=draft|12=draft}} {{ill|Ureshino Town|ja|嬉野町 (佐賀県)|lt=Ureshino Town|lt_ja=嬉野町|12=draft|12=draft}} |Access = Railway : {{ill|Sasebo Line|ja|佐世保線|12=draft|12=draft}} {{ill|Takeo Onsen Station|ja|武雄温泉駅|12=draft|12=draft}} via {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|12=draft|12=draft}} for about 30 minutes
West Kyushu Shinkansen Ureshino Onsen Station
''For other access methods, see [[#アクセス|Access]]'' |Water Type = {{ill|Chloride Hot Spring|ja|塩化物泉|1=Brine spring|12=draft|12=draft}} |Temperature = |Discharge = |pH =7.8 |Liquid Classification = |Osmotic Pressure Classification = |Number of Accommodations = |Total Capacity = |Annual Bath Visitors = |Statistical Year = |External links = [https://spa-u.net/ Ureshino Onsen Tourism Association] |Special Notes = }} '''Ureshino Onsen''' (嬉野温泉) is a {{ill|Hot Spring|ja|温泉|1=Onsen|1=Onsen|12=draft|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Saga Prefecture|ja|佐賀県|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|12=draft|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Ureshino Town|ja|嬉野町 (佐賀県)|lt=Ureshino Town|lt_ja=嬉野町|12=draft|12=draft}} (formerly part of {{ill|Hizen Province|ja|肥前国|12=draft|12=draft}}). Along with {{ill|Takeo Onsen|ja|武雄温泉|12=draft|12=draft}}, it is one of the representative hot springs of the prefecture. It has been selected as one of {{ill|Japan's 100 Views|ja|日本百景|12=draft|12=draft}} and is trademarked by Ureshino City under the names “Japan’s Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs Ureshino Onsen” and “Saga–Ureshino Onsen.” == Water Type == * Sodium – Bicarbonate Salt / Chloride Hot Spring It is a baking soda spring renowned for its beauty-enhancing properties, leaving the skin exceptionally smooth after a {{ill|Bathing|ja|入浴|12=draft|12=draft}}. Its water quality was chosen by {{ill|Satoshi Fujita|ja|藤田聡|12=draft|12=draft}} as one of the {{ill|Japan's Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs|ja|日本三大美肌の湯|12=draft|12=draft}} (the other two being {{ill|Hinokami Onsen|ja|斐乃上温泉|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Kirekawa Onsen|ja|喜連川温泉|12=draft|12=draft}}). == Onsen Town == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Siebold-no-yu.jpg|thumb|300px|{{Center|Siebold's Bath (シーボルトの湯)}} ]] This hot spring area, which rises in the heart of the town, is one of the largest onsen towns in Kyushu. Nearly 50 {{ill|Ryokan|ja|旅館|12=draft|12=draft}} – both large and small – line the streets along the banks of the {{ill|Shioda River|ja|塩田川 (佐賀県)|lt=Shioda River|lt_ja=塩田川|12=draft|12=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ureshino River|ja|嬉野川|12=draft|12=draft}}), including Wataya Villa, where {{ill|Emperor Shōwa|ja|昭和天皇|12=draft|12=draft}} stayed during the 38th {{ill|National Tree Planting Festival|ja|全国植樹祭|12=draft|12=draft}} held in Saga Prefecture in 1987 (Showa 62). In addition, the oldest inn in Ureshino is said to be {{ill|Omuraya|ja|大村屋|12=draft|12=draft}}, founded in 1830 (the first year of the Tenpō era). In the center of the shopping district’s footbath plaza, there is “{{ill|Siebold|ja|フィリップ・フランツ・フォン・シーボルト|lt=Siebold|lt_ja=シーボルト|12=draft|12=draft}}’s Foot Bath,” which is available free of charge. Nearby stands the wooden, two-story (partly three-story) with one basement {{ill|Public Bath|ja|公衆浴場|1=public bathing|lt=Public Bathhouse|12=draft|12=draft}} “Furuyu Onsen,” constructed in 1924 (Taishō 13) to a design by a {{ill|German|ja|ドイツ人|12=draft|12=draft}}. Although by around 2001 its interior and piping had deteriorated, the building’s exterior remained in nearly excellent condition{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀県の近代化遺産-佐賀県近代化遺産（建造物等）総合調査報告書-|year=2002|publisher=佐賀県教育委員会|page=182|series=佐賀県文化財調査報告書第153集}}. However, it was demolished on March 20, 2005 (Heisei 17) due to damage from the {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture Western Offshore Earthquake|ja|福岡県西方沖地震|12=draft|12=draft}}. Later, in response to local demand, it was reconstructed to replicate its Taishō-era appearance and reopened on April 1, 2010 (Heisei 22) under the new name “Siebold’s Bath”{{Cite web |title=＜重点報道＠嬉野市＞わがまち今昔 シーボルトの湯 {{!}} まちの話題 {{!}} 佐賀新聞ニュース |url=https://www.saga-s.co.jp/articles/-/1114588 |website=佐賀新聞 |date=2024-04-09 |access-date=2024-04-09 |language=ja}}. Also known as the “Hot Spring for Beautiful Skin,” Ureshino Onsen is suitable for drinking. Its signature dish, the hot spring {{ill|Hot Spring Tofu|ja|湯豆腐|12=draft|12=draft}}, prepared using the onsen water, is a renowned specialty of Ureshino. In Ureshino City the product is written as “Yudōfu,” and the name “Ureshino Onsen Yudōfu” is trademarked by the city. == History == [[File:Ureshino Onsen 01.jpg|thumb|280px|{{Center|Onsen Town|1=Spa Town|lt=Onsen Town}} ]] Ureshino Onsen first appears in historical records in the ''Hizen Province Fudoki'' ({{ill|Hizen Province Fudoki|ja|肥前国風土記|12=draft|12=draft}}), compiled during the Nara period, with a description as a “hot spring that cures the ailments of all people,” although its name is not mentioned嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、272頁. According to legend, {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后|12=draft|12=draft}} discovered the hot spring on her return from the {{ill|Conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea|ja|三韓征伐|12=draft|12=draft}} and, while soothing her soldiers’ fatigue, exclaimed something akin to “How delightful!”—a remark that was later associated with the naming of “Ureshino.” Other legends tell of either Prince Takaso (from the ''Daidōji Kyuuki'') or an old woman (from the legend of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|12=draft|12=draft}}) exclaiming “ureshi.” These tales, however, were retroactively linked after the name “Ureshino” (originally read “ureshino”) was established, and the exclamation is not considered directly connected to the place name. In fact, the term “ureshino” is first confirmed in historical documents during the Kamakura period, when it was written as “宇礼志野”嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、351～353頁. The origin of the name is attributed to a field located in the upper reaches of the Shioda River; because the word “末” (ure) means “tip” or “end,” the area was called “Sueshino” and later a kanji was assigned to form the name{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀地名うんちく事典|year=2005|publisher=佐賀新聞社|page=93}}. After a period with few records concerning the hot spring, by the late Sengoku period (1570s) records emerge of {{ill|Ryūzōji Takanobu|ja|龍造寺隆信|12=draft|12=draft}} recommending hot spring therapy in Ureshino嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、710頁. During the {{ill|Edo Period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft|12=draft}}, Ureshino Onsen flourished as Ureshino-juku, a {{ill|Post Town|ja|宿場町|12=draft|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Nagasaki Kaidō|ja|長崎街道|12=draft|12=draft}}. In 1656 (Meireki 2), during the time of the first lord of the {{ill|Hasuike Domain|ja|蓮池藩|12=draft|12=draft}}, Nabeshima Naotoshi, management of the spring source – previously under the jurisdiction of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|12=draft|12=draft}} – was transferred to the domain, and a roof was added to the open-air bath, converting it into a domain-run bathhouse. The post town was frequented by many travelers, and the state of Ureshino Onsen was recorded in works such as ''Wakan Sansai Zue'' and ''Edo Travelogue''. It appears that from this period it also became known as an entertainment hot spring. After World War II, Ureshino Onsen gained fame as an entertainment hot spring comparable to {{ill|Beppu Onsen|ja|別府温泉|lt=Beppu|lt_ja=別府|12=draft|12=draft}} in the west. However, each onsen inn has its own distinctive style and character, and while many events are held, comparatively few new facilities have been introduced. In the former Ureshino Town (now part of {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|12=draft|12=draft}}) tea has been cultivated for generations. For this reason, Ureshino City and its tourism association actively promote the area as '''"Hot Spring Land of Tea and Tofu"''', and various initiatives have been undertaken to link the two. In addition, a 2D character themed on hot springs, “Ureshino Rokka” (from {{ill|Onsen Musume|ja|温泉むすめ|12=draft|12=draft}}), is used to promote the hot springs{{Cite web |url=https://onsen-musume.jp/character/ureshino_rikka |title=嬉野 六香 |access-date=2024-09-22 |publisher=株式会社エンバウンド |website=温泉むすめ公式サイト}}. == Access == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Tofu.jpg|thumb|190px|{{Center|A Famous Specialty from the Edo Period

''For other access methods, see [[#アクセス|Access]]'' |Water Type = {{ill|Chloride Hot Spring|ja|塩化物泉|1=Brine spring|12=draft|12=draft}} |Temperature = |Discharge = |pH =7.8 |Liquid Classification = |Osmotic Pressure Classification = |Number of Accommodations = |Total Capacity = |Annual Bath Visitors = |Statistical Year = |External links = [https://spa-u.net/ Ureshino Onsen Tourism Association] |Special Notes = }} '''Ureshino Onsen''' (嬉野温泉) is a {{ill|Hot Spring|ja|温泉|1=Onsen|1=Onsen|12=draft|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Saga Prefecture|ja|佐賀県|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|12=draft|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Ureshino Town|ja|嬉野町 (佐賀県)|lt=Ureshino Town|lt_ja=嬉野町|12=draft|12=draft}} (formerly part of {{ill|Hizen Province|ja|肥前国|12=draft|12=draft}}). Along with {{ill|Takeo Onsen|ja|武雄温泉|12=draft|12=draft}}, it is one of the representative hot springs of the prefecture. It has been selected as one of {{ill|Japan's 100 Views|ja|日本百景|12=draft|12=draft}} and is trademarked by Ureshino City under the names “Japan’s Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs Ureshino Onsen” and “Saga–Ureshino Onsen.” == Water Type == * Sodium – Bicarbonate Salt / Chloride Hot Spring It is a baking soda spring renowned for its beauty-enhancing properties, leaving the skin exceptionally smooth after a {{ill|Bathing|ja|入浴|12=draft|12=draft}}. Its water quality was chosen by {{ill|Satoshi Fujita|ja|藤田聡|12=draft|12=draft}} as one of the {{ill|Japan's Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs|ja|日本三大美肌の湯|12=draft|12=draft}} (the other two being {{ill|Hinokami Onsen|ja|斐乃上温泉|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Kirekawa Onsen|ja|喜連川温泉|12=draft|12=draft}}). == Onsen Town == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Siebold-no-yu.jpg|thumb|300px|{{Center|Siebold's Bath (シーボルトの湯)}} ]] This hot spring area, which rises in the heart of the town, is one of the largest onsen towns in Kyushu. Nearly 50 {{ill|Ryokan|ja|旅館|12=draft|12=draft}} – both large and small – line the streets along the banks of the {{ill|Shioda River|ja|塩田川 (佐賀県)|lt=Shioda River|lt_ja=塩田川|12=draft|12=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ureshino River|ja|嬉野川|12=draft|12=draft}}), including Wataya Villa, where {{ill|Emperor Shōwa|ja|昭和天皇|12=draft|12=draft}} stayed during the 38th {{ill|National Tree Planting Festival|ja|全国植樹祭|12=draft|12=draft}} held in Saga Prefecture in 1987 (Showa 62). In addition, the oldest inn in Ureshino is said to be {{ill|Omuraya|ja|大村屋|12=draft|12=draft}}, founded in 1830 (the first year of the Tenpō era). In the center of the shopping district’s footbath plaza, there is “{{ill|Siebold|ja|フィリップ・フランツ・フォン・シーボルト|lt=Siebold|lt_ja=シーボルト|12=draft|12=draft}}’s Foot Bath,” which is available free of charge. Nearby stands the wooden, two-story (partly three-story) with one basement {{ill|Public Bath|ja|公衆浴場|1=public bathing|lt=Public Bathhouse|12=draft|12=draft}} “Furuyu Onsen,” constructed in 1924 (Taishō 13) to a design by a {{ill|German|ja|ドイツ人|12=draft|12=draft}}. Although by around 2001 its interior and piping had deteriorated, the building’s exterior remained in nearly excellent condition{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀県の近代化遺産-佐賀県近代化遺産（建造物等）総合調査報告書-|year=2002|publisher=佐賀県教育委員会|page=182|series=佐賀県文化財調査報告書第153集}}. However, it was demolished on March 20, 2005 (Heisei 17) due to damage from the {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture Western Offshore Earthquake|ja|福岡県西方沖地震|12=draft|12=draft}}. Later, in response to local demand, it was reconstructed to replicate its Taishō-era appearance and reopened on April 1, 2010 (Heisei 22) under the new name “Siebold’s Bath”{{Cite web |title=＜重点報道＠嬉野市＞わがまち今昔 シーボルトの湯 {{!}} まちの話題 {{!}} 佐賀新聞ニュース |url=https://www.saga-s.co.jp/articles/-/1114588 |website=佐賀新聞 |date=2024-04-09 |access-date=2024-04-09 |language=ja}}. Also known as the “Hot Spring for Beautiful Skin,” Ureshino Onsen is suitable for drinking. Its signature dish, the hot spring {{ill|Hot Spring Tofu|ja|湯豆腐|12=draft|12=draft}}, prepared using the onsen water, is a renowned specialty of Ureshino. In Ureshino City the product is written as “Yudōfu,” and the name “Ureshino Onsen Yudōfu” is trademarked by the city. == History == [[File:Ureshino Onsen 01.jpg|thumb|280px|{{Center|Onsen Town|1=Spa Town|lt=Onsen Town}} ]] Ureshino Onsen first appears in historical records in the ''Hizen Province Fudoki'' ({{ill|Hizen Province Fudoki|ja|肥前国風土記|12=draft|12=draft}}), compiled during the Nara period, with a description as a “hot spring that cures the ailments of all people,” although its name is not mentioned嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、272頁. According to legend, {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后|12=draft|12=draft}} discovered the hot spring on her return from the {{ill|Conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea|ja|三韓征伐|12=draft|12=draft}} and, while soothing her soldiers’ fatigue, exclaimed something akin to “How delightful!”—a remark that was later associated with the naming of “Ureshino.” Other legends tell of either Prince Takaso (from the ''Daidōji Kyuuki'') or an old woman (from the legend of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|12=draft|12=draft}}) exclaiming “ureshi.” These tales, however, were retroactively linked after the name “Ureshino” (originally read “ureshino”) was established, and the exclamation is not considered directly connected to the place name. In fact, the term “ureshino” is first confirmed in historical documents during the Kamakura period, when it was written as “宇礼志野”嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、351～353頁. The origin of the name is attributed to a field located in the upper reaches of the Shioda River; because the word “末” (ure) means “tip” or “end,” the area was called “Sueshino” and later a kanji was assigned to form the name{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀地名うんちく事典|year=2005|publisher=佐賀新聞社|page=93}}. After a period with few records concerning the hot spring, by the late Sengoku period (1570s) records emerge of {{ill|Ryūzōji Takanobu|ja|龍造寺隆信|12=draft|12=draft}} recommending hot spring therapy in Ureshino嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、710頁. During the {{ill|Edo Period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft|12=draft}}, Ureshino Onsen flourished as Ureshino-juku, a {{ill|Post Town|ja|宿場町|12=draft|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Nagasaki Kaidō|ja|長崎街道|12=draft|12=draft}}. In 1656 (Meireki 2), during the time of the first lord of the {{ill|Hasuike Domain|ja|蓮池藩|12=draft|12=draft}}, Nabeshima Naotoshi, management of the spring source – previously under the jurisdiction of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|12=draft|12=draft}} – was transferred to the domain, and a roof was added to the open-air bath, converting it into a domain-run bathhouse. The post town was frequented by many travelers, and the state of Ureshino Onsen was recorded in works such as ''Wakan Sansai Zue'' and ''Edo Travelogue''. It appears that from this period it also became known as an entertainment hot spring. After World War II, Ureshino Onsen gained fame as an entertainment hot spring comparable to {{ill|Beppu Onsen|ja|別府温泉|lt=Beppu|lt_ja=別府|12=draft|12=draft}} in the west. However, each onsen inn has its own distinctive style and character, and while many events are held, comparatively few new facilities have been introduced. In the former Ureshino Town (now part of {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|12=draft|12=draft}}) tea has been cultivated for generations. For this reason, Ureshino City and its tourism association actively promote the area as '''"Hot Spring Land of Tea and Tofu"''', and various initiatives have been undertaken to link the two. In addition, a 2D character themed on hot springs, “Ureshino Rokka” (from {{ill|Onsen Musume|ja|温泉むすめ|12=draft|12=draft}}), is used to promote the hot springs{{Cite web |url=https://onsen-musume.jp/character/ureshino_rikka |title=嬉野 六香 |access-date=2024-09-22 |publisher=株式会社エンバウンド |website=温泉むすめ公式サイト}}. == Access == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Tofu.jpg|thumb|190px|{{Center|A Famous Specialty from the Edo Period
'Hot Spring Tofu'}} ]] * Railway (access from {{ill|JR Kyushu|ja|九州旅客鉄道|lt=JR Kyushu|lt_ja=JR九州|12=draft|12=draft}} stations) ** About 13 minutes by {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|12=draft|12=draft}} from {{ill|Ureshino Onsen Station|ja|嬉野温泉駅|12=draft|12=draft}} on the {{ill|West Kyushu Shinkansen|ja|西九州新幹線|12=draft|12=draft}}. ** About 30 minutes by {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|12=draft|12=draft}} from {{ill|Takeo Onsen Station|ja|武雄温泉駅|12=draft|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Sasebo Line|ja|佐世保線|12=draft|12=draft}}. ** About 1 hour by {{ill|Nishi-Hii Bus|ja|西肥自動車|lt=Nishi-Hii Bus|lt_ja=西肥バス|12=draft|12=draft}} from {{ill|Sasebo Station|ja|佐世保駅|12=draft|12=draft}} on the Sasebo Line. ** About 30 minutes by {{ill|Yūtoku Bus|ja|祐徳自動車|lt=Yūtoku Bus|lt_ja=祐徳バス|12=draft|12=draft}} from {{ill|Hizen Kashima Station|ja|肥前鹿島駅|12=draft|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Nagasaki Main Line|ja|長崎本線|12=draft|12=draft}}. ** About 25 minutes by {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|12=draft|12=draft}} from {{ill|Karinoki Station|ja|彼杵駅|12=draft|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Omura Line|ja|大村線|12=draft|12=draft}}. * Highway Bus *: Use the “{{ill|Kyushu-go|ja|九州号|12=draft|12=draft}}” operated by {{ill|Kyushu Express Bus|ja|九州急行バス|12=draft|12=draft}}. There are services that stop at the Ureshino Bus Center ({{ill|National Route 34|ja|国道34号|12=draft|12=draft}}) in the hot spring town and services that stop only at the {{ill|Ureshino Interchange|ja|嬉野インターチェンジ|12=draft|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Nagasaki Expressway|ja|長崎自動車道|12=draft|12=draft}}. In recent years, the latter has far more frequent service – while the former runs only 4 times a day, the latter operates roughly every 30 minutes. ** About 2 hours from {{ill|Fukuoka City|ja|福岡市|12=draft|12=draft}} (via {{ill|Hakata Bus Terminal|ja|博多バスターミナル|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Nishitetsu Tenjin Express Bus Terminal|ja|西鉄天神高速バスターミナル|12=draft|12=draft}}). ** About 1 hour from {{ill|Nagasaki City|ja|長崎市|12=draft|12=draft}} (from {{ill|Nagasaki Station|ja|長崎駅|lt=Nagasaki Station Front|lt_ja=長崎駅前|12=draft|12=draft}}). * Shared Taxi from the Airport *: With the opening of {{ill|Saga Airport|ja|佐賀空港|12=draft|12=draft}}, local taxi companies began operating services. The travel time from Saga Airport is approximately 1 hour. * Private Car *: 5 minutes via the {{ill|Nagasaki Prefectural and Saga Prefectural Route 1 Sasebo-Ureshino Line|ja|長崎県道・佐賀県道1号佐世保嬉野線|12=draft|12=draft}} from the Ureshino Interchange on the {{ill|Nagasaki Expressway|ja|長崎自動車道|12=draft|12=draft}}. == References == == Related Literature == *{{Cite book |Language=Japanese |author=Masamichi Ikeda|year=1898|title=Ureshino Onsen Chronicles|id={{NDLJP|766546}}|quote= }} == See Also == {{commonscat|Ureshino Onsen}} * {{ill|Tourist Attractions in Saga Prefecture|ja|佐賀県の観光地|12=draft|12=draft}} * {{ill|West Kyushu Shinkansen|ja|西九州新幹線|12=draft|12=draft}} * {{ill|Ureshino Onsen Station|ja|嬉野温泉駅|12=draft|12=draft}} * {{ill|Hizen Dream Road|ja|肥前夢街道|12=draft|12=draft}} * {{ill|Wataya Villa|ja|和多屋別荘|12=draft|12=draft}} * {{ill|Irifune-sō|ja|入船荘|12=draft|12=draft}} * {{ill|Soapland|ja|ソープランド|12=draft|12=draft}} * {{ill|Yagita Yūki|ja|柳田悠岐|12=draft|12=draft}} … (conducts self-training at Ureshino Onsen every year). * The townscape of {{ill|Shiodazu|ja|塩田津|12=draft|12=draft}} ({{ill|Important Preservation District for Groups of Traditional Buildings|ja|重要伝統的建造物群保存地区|12=draft|12=draft}}) … the post town following Ureshino-juku. == External Links == * [https://spa-u.net/ Ureshino Onsen Tourism Association] * [https://www.nicovideo.jp/watch/1269845231 Nico Nico Douga Ureshino Onsen Public Bath “Siebold’s Bath”] (Provided by {{ill|Saga Shimbun|ja|佐賀新聞|12=draft|12=draft}}) {{Portal bar|Japan|Saga Prefecture|Hot Springs}} ''' ''' ''' ''' {{Onsen}} {{draft categories| }} {{draft categories| [[Category:Hot Springs in Saga Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Saga Prefecture]] [[Category:Geography of Ureshino City]] [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:Onsens]] [[Category:Onsen Shrines]] [[Category:Legends]] [[Category:Onsen Origin Myth]] [[Category:pgoodbye $1 11]] [[Category: Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Un11]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:Text replacement - The post town was frequented by many travelers, and the state of Ureshino Onsen was recorded in works such as ''Wakan Sansai Zue'' and ''Edo Travelogue''. It appears that from this period it also became known as an entertainment hot spring. After World War II, Ureshino Onsen gained fame as an entertainment hot spring comparable to {{ill|Beppu Onsen|ja|別府温泉|lt=Beppu|lt_ja=別府|12=draft|12=draft}} in the west. However, each onsen inn has its own distinctive style and character, and while many events are held, comparatively few new facilities have been introduced. In the former Ureshino Town (now part of {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|12=draft|12=draft}}) tea has been cultivated for generations. For this reason, Ureshino City and its tourism association actively promote the area as '''"Hot Spring Land of Tea and Tofu"''', and various initiatives have been undertaken to link the two. In addition, a 2D character themed on hot springs, “Ureshino Rokka” (from {{ill|Onsen Musume|ja|温泉むすめ|12=draft|12=draft}}), is used to promote the hot springs{{Cite web |url=https://onsen-musume.jp/character/ureshino_rikka |title=嬉野 六香 |access-date=2024-09-22 |publisher=株式会社エンバウンド |website=温泉むすめ公式サイト}}. == Access == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Tofu.jpg|thumb|190px|{{Center|A Famous Specialty from the Edo Period

West Kyushu Shinkansen Ureshino Onsen Station
''For other access methods, see [[#アクセス|Access]]'' |Water Type = {{ill|Chloride Hot Spring|ja|塩化物泉|1=Brine spring|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |Temperature = |Discharge = |pH =7.8 |Liquid Classification = |Osmotic Pressure Classification = |Number of Accommodations = |Total Capacity = |Annual Bath Visitors = |Statistical Year = |External links = [https://spa-u.net/ Ureshino Onsen Tourism Association] |Special Notes = }} '''Ureshino Onsen''' (嬉野温泉) is a {{ill|Hot Spring|ja|温泉|1=Onsen|1=Onsen|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Saga Prefecture|ja|佐賀県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Ureshino Town|ja|嬉野町 (佐賀県)|lt=Ureshino Town|lt_ja=嬉野町|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (formerly part of {{ill|Hizen Province|ja|肥前国|qq=draft|qq=draft}}). Along with {{ill|Takeo Onsen|ja|武雄温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it is one of the representative hot springs of the prefecture. It has been selected as one of {{ill|Japan's 100 Views|ja|日本百景|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and is trademarked by Ureshino City under the names “Japan’s Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs Ureshino Onsen” and “Saga–Ureshino Onsen.” == Water Type == * Sodium – Bicarbonate Salt / Chloride Hot Spring It is a baking soda spring renowned for its beauty-enhancing properties, leaving the skin exceptionally smooth after a {{ill|Bathing|ja|入浴|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Its water quality was chosen by {{ill|Satoshi Fujita|ja|藤田聡|qq=draft|qq=draft}} as one of the {{ill|Japan's Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs|ja|日本三大美肌の湯|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (the other two being {{ill|Hinokami Onsen|ja|斐乃上温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Kirekawa Onsen|ja|喜連川温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft}}). == Onsen Town == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Siebold-no-yu.jpg|thumb|300px|{{Center|Siebold's Bath (シーボルトの湯)}} ]] This hot spring area, which rises in the heart of the town, is one of the largest onsen towns in Kyushu. Nearly 50 {{ill|Ryokan|ja|旅館|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – both large and small – line the streets along the banks of the {{ill|Shioda River|ja|塩田川 (佐賀県)|lt=Shioda River|lt_ja=塩田川|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ureshino River|ja|嬉野川|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), including Wataya Villa, where {{ill|Emperor Shōwa|ja|昭和天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}} stayed during the 38th {{ill|National Tree Planting Festival|ja|全国植樹祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} held in Saga Prefecture in 1987 (Showa 62). In addition, the oldest inn in Ureshino is said to be {{ill|Omuraya|ja|大村屋|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, founded in 1830 (the first year of the Tenpō era). In the center of the shopping district’s footbath plaza, there is “{{ill|Siebold|ja|フィリップ・フランツ・フォン・シーボルト|lt=Siebold|lt_ja=シーボルト|qq=draft|qq=draft}}’s Foot Bath,” which is available free of charge. Nearby stands the wooden, two-story (partly three-story) with one basement {{ill|Public Bath|ja|公衆浴場|1=public bathing|lt=Public Bathhouse|qq=draft|qq=draft}} “Furuyu Onsen,” constructed in 1924 (Taishō 13) to a design by a {{ill|German|ja|ドイツ人|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Although by around 2001 its interior and piping had deteriorated, the building’s exterior remained in nearly excellent condition{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀県の近代化遺産-佐賀県近代化遺産（建造物等）総合調査報告書-|year=2002|publisher=佐賀県教育委員会|page=182|series=佐賀県文化財調査報告書第153集}}. However, it was demolished on March 20, 2005 (Heisei 17) due to damage from the {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture Western Offshore Earthquake|ja|福岡県西方沖地震|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Later, in response to local demand, it was reconstructed to replicate its Taishō-era appearance and reopened on April 1, 2010 (Heisei 22) under the new name “Siebold’s Bath”{{Cite web |title=＜重点報道＠嬉野市＞わがまち今昔 シーボルトの湯 {{!}} まちの話題 {{!}} 佐賀新聞ニュース |url=https://www.saga-s.co.jp/articles/-/1114588 |website=佐賀新聞 |date=2024-04-09 |access-date=2024-04-09 |language=ja}}. Also known as the “Hot Spring for Beautiful Skin,” Ureshino Onsen is suitable for drinking. Its signature dish, the hot spring {{ill|Hot Spring Tofu|ja|湯豆腐|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, prepared using the onsen water, is a renowned specialty of Ureshino. In Ureshino City the product is written as “Yudōfu,” and the name “Ureshino Onsen Yudōfu” is trademarked by the city. == History == [[File:Ureshino Onsen 01.jpg|thumb|280px|{{Center|Onsen Town|1=Spa Town|lt=Onsen Town}} ]] Ureshino Onsen first appears in historical records in the ''Hizen Province Fudoki'' ({{ill|Hizen Province Fudoki|ja|肥前国風土記|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), compiled during the Nara period, with a description as a “hot spring that cures the ailments of all people,” although its name is not mentioned嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、272頁. According to legend, {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后|qq=draft|qq=draft}} discovered the hot spring on her return from the {{ill|Conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea|ja|三韓征伐|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and, while soothing her soldiers’ fatigue, exclaimed something akin to “How delightful!”—a remark that was later associated with the naming of “Ureshino.” Other legends tell of either Prince Takaso (from the ''Daidōji Kyuuki'') or an old woman (from the legend of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) exclaiming “ureshi.” These tales, however, were retroactively linked after the name “Ureshino” (originally read “ureshino”) was established, and the exclamation is not considered directly connected to the place name. In fact, the term “ureshino” is first confirmed in historical documents during the Kamakura period, when it was written as “宇礼志野”嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、351～353頁. The origin of the name is attributed to a field located in the upper reaches of the Shioda River; because the word “末” (ure) means “tip” or “end,” the area was called “Sueshino” and later a kanji was assigned to form the name{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀地名うんちく事典|year=2005|publisher=佐賀新聞社|page=93}}. After a period with few records concerning the hot spring, by the late Sengoku period (1570s) records emerge of {{ill|Ryūzōji Takanobu|ja|龍造寺隆信|qq=draft|qq=draft}} recommending hot spring therapy in Ureshino嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、710頁. {{infobox Onsen |Name = Ureshino Onsen |image = Ureshino onsen.jpg |Comment = |Location = {{ill|Saga Prefecture|ja|佐賀県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Ureshino Town|ja|嬉野町 (佐賀県)|lt=Ureshino Town|lt_ja=嬉野町|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |Access = Railway : {{ill|Sasebo Line|ja|佐世保線|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Takeo Onsen Station|ja|武雄温泉駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} via {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|qq=draft|qq=draft}} for about 30 minutes
West Kyushu Shinkansen Ureshino Onsen Station
''For other access methods, see [[#アクセス|Access]]'' |Water Type = {{ill|Chloride Hot Spring|ja|塩化物泉|1=Brine spring|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |Temperature = |Discharge = |pH =7.8 |Liquid Classification = |Osmotic Pressure Classification = |Number of Accommodations = |Total Capacity = |Annual Bath Visitors = |Statistical Year = |External links = [https://spa-u.net/ Ureshino Onsen Tourism Association] |Special Notes = }} '''Ureshino Onsen''' (嬉野温泉) is a {{ill|Hot Spring|ja|温泉|1=Onsen|1=Onsen|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Saga Prefecture|ja|佐賀県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Ureshino Town|ja|嬉野町 (佐賀県)|lt=Ureshino Town|lt_ja=嬉野町|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (formerly part of {{ill|Hizen Province|ja|肥前国|qq=draft|qq=draft}}). Along with {{ill|Takeo Onsen|ja|武雄温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it is one of the representative hot springs of the prefecture. It has been selected as one of {{ill|Japan's 100 Views|ja|日本百景|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and is trademarked by Ureshino City under the names “Japan’s Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs Ureshino Onsen” and “Saga–Ureshino Onsen.” == Water Type == * Sodium – Bicarbonate Salt / Chloride Hot Spring It is a baking soda spring renowned for its beauty-enhancing properties, leaving the skin exceptionally smooth after a {{ill|Bathing|ja|入浴|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Its water quality was chosen by {{ill|Satoshi Fujita|ja|藤田聡|qq=draft|qq=draft}} as one of the {{ill|Japan's Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs|ja|日本三大美肌の湯|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (the other two being {{ill|Hinokami Onsen|ja|斐乃上温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Kirekawa Onsen|ja|喜連川温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft}}). == Onsen Town == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Siebold-no-yu.jpg|thumb|300px|{{Center|Siebold's Bath (シーボルトの湯)}} ]] This hot spring area, which rises in the heart of the town, is one of the largest onsen towns in Kyushu. Nearly 50 {{ill|Ryokan|ja|旅館|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – both large and small – line the streets along the banks of the {{ill|Shioda River|ja|塩田川 (佐賀県)|lt=Shioda River|lt_ja=塩田川|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ureshino River|ja|嬉野川|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), including Wataya Villa, where {{ill|Emperor Shōwa|ja|昭和天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}} stayed during the 38th {{ill|National Tree Planting Festival|ja|全国植樹祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} held in Saga Prefecture in 1987 (Showa 62). In addition, the oldest inn in Ureshino is said to be {{ill|Omuraya|ja|大村屋|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, founded in 1830 (the first year of the Tenpō era). In the center of the shopping district’s footbath plaza, there is “{{ill|Siebold|ja|フィリップ・フランツ・フォン・シーボルト|lt=Siebold|lt_ja=シーボルト|qq=draft|qq=draft}}’s Foot Bath,” which is available free of charge. Nearby stands the wooden, two-story (partly three-story) with one basement {{ill|Public Bath|ja|公衆浴場|1=public bathing|lt=Public Bathhouse|qq=draft|qq=draft}} “Furuyu Onsen,” constructed in 1924 (Taishō 13) to a design by a {{ill|German|ja|ドイツ人|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Although by around 2001 its interior and piping had deteriorated, the building’s exterior remained in nearly excellent condition{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀県の近代化遺産-佐賀県近代化遺産（建造物等）総合調査報告書-|year=2002|publisher=佐賀県教育委員会|page=182|series=佐賀県文化財調査報告書第153集}}. However, it was demolished on March 20, 2005 (Heisei 17) due to damage from the {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture Western Offshore Earthquake|ja|福岡県西方沖地震|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Later, in response to local demand, it was reconstructed to replicate its Taishō-era appearance and reopened on April 1, 2010 (Heisei 22) under the new name “Siebold’s Bath”{{Cite web |title=＜重点報道＠嬉野市＞わがまち今昔 シーボルトの湯 {{!}} まちの話題 {{!}} 佐賀新聞ニュース |url=https://www.saga-s.co.jp/articles/-/1114588 |website=佐賀新聞 |date=2024-04-09 |access-date=2024-04-09 |language=ja}}. Also known as the “Hot Spring for Beautiful Skin,” Ureshino Onsen is suitable for drinking. Its signature dish, the hot spring {{ill|Hot Spring Tofu|ja|湯豆腐|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, prepared using the onsen water, is a renowned specialty of Ureshino. In Ureshino City the product is written as “Yudōfu,” and the name “Ureshino Onsen Yudōfu” is trademarked by the city. == History == [[File:Ureshino Onsen 01.jpg|thumb|280px|{{Center|Onsen Town|1=Spa Town|lt=Onsen Town}} ]] Ureshino Onsen first appears in historical records in the ''Hizen Province Fudoki'' ({{ill|Hizen Province Fudoki|ja|肥前国風土記|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), compiled during the Nara period, with a description as a “hot spring that cures the ailments of all people,” although its name is not mentioned嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、272頁. According to legend, {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后|qq=draft|qq=draft}} discovered the hot spring on her return from the {{ill|Conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea|ja|三韓征伐|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and, while soothing her soldiers’ fatigue, exclaimed something akin to “How delightful!”—a remark that was later associated with the naming of “Ureshino.” Other legends tell of either Prince Takaso (from the ''Daidōji Kyuuki'') or an old woman (from the legend of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) exclaiming “ureshi.” These tales, however, were retroactively linked after the name “Ureshino” (originally read “ureshino”) was established, and the exclamation is not considered directly connected to the place name. In fact, the term “ureshino” is first confirmed in historical documents during the Kamakura period, when it was written as “宇礼志野”嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、351～353頁. The origin of the name is attributed to a field located in the upper reaches of the Shioda River; because the word “末” (ure) means “tip” or “end,” the area was called “Sueshino” and later a kanji was assigned to form the name{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀地名うんちく事典|year=2005|publisher=佐賀新聞社|page=93}}. After a period with few records concerning the hot spring, by the late Sengoku period (1570s) records emerge of {{ill|Ryūzōji Takanobu|ja|龍造寺隆信|qq=draft|qq=draft}} recommending hot spring therapy in Ureshino嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、710頁. During the {{ill|Edo Period|ja|江戸時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Ureshino Onsen flourished as Ureshino-juku, a {{ill|Post Town|ja|宿場町|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|Nagasaki Kaidō|ja|長崎街道|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In 1656 (Meireki 2), during the time of the first lord of the {{ill|Hasuike Domain|ja|蓮池藩|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Nabeshima Naotoshi, management of the spring source – previously under the jurisdiction of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – was transferred to the domain, and a roof was added to the open-air bath, converting it into a domain-run bathhouse. The post town was frequented by many travelers, and the state of Ureshino Onsen was recorded in works such as ''Wakan Sansai Zue'' and ''Edo Travelogue''. It appears that from this period it also became known as an entertainment hot spring. After World War II, Ureshino Onsen gained fame as an entertainment hot spring comparable to {{ill|Beppu Onsen|ja|別府温泉|lt=Beppu|lt_ja=別府|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the west. However, each onsen inn has its own distinctive style and character, and while many events are held, comparatively few new facilities have been introduced. In the former Ureshino Town (now part of {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) tea has been cultivated for generations. For this reason, Ureshino City and its tourism association actively promote the area as '''"Hot Spring Land of Tea and Tofu"''', and various initiatives have been undertaken to link the two. In addition, a 2D character themed on hot springs, “Ureshino Rokka” (from {{ill|Onsen Musume|ja|温泉むすめ|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), is used to promote the hot springs{{Cite web |url=https://onsen-musume.jp/character/ureshino_rikka |title=嬉野 六香 |access-date=2024-09-22 |publisher=株式会社エンバウンド |website=温泉むすめ公式サイト}}. == Access == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Tofu.jpg|thumb|190px|{{Center|A Famous Specialty from the Edo Period
'Hot Spring Tofu'}} ]] * Railway (access from {{ill|JR Kyushu|ja|九州旅客鉄道|lt=JR Kyushu|lt_ja=JR九州|qq=draft|qq=draft}} stations) ** About 13 minutes by {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|qq=draft|qq=draft}} from {{ill|Ureshino Onsen Station|ja|嬉野温泉駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|West Kyushu Shinkansen|ja|西九州新幹線|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. ** About 30 minutes by {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|qq=draft|qq=draft}} from {{ill|Takeo Onsen Station|ja|武雄温泉駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|Sasebo Line|ja|佐世保線|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. ** About 1 hour by {{ill|Nishi-Hii Bus|ja|西肥自動車|lt=Nishi-Hii Bus|lt_ja=西肥バス|qq=draft|qq=draft}} from {{ill|Sasebo Station|ja|佐世保駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the Sasebo Line. ** About 30 minutes by {{ill|Yūtoku Bus|ja|祐徳自動車|lt=Yūtoku Bus|lt_ja=祐徳バス|qq=draft|qq=draft}} from {{ill|Hizen Kashima Station|ja|肥前鹿島駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|Nagasaki Main Line|ja|長崎本線|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. ** About 25 minutes by {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|qq=draft|qq=draft}} from {{ill|Karinoki Station|ja|彼杵駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|Omura Line|ja|大村線|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. * Highway Bus *: Use the “{{ill|Kyushu-go|ja|九州号|qq=draft|qq=draft}}” operated by {{ill|Kyushu Express Bus|ja|九州急行バス|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. There are services that stop at the Ureshino Bus Center ({{ill|National Route 34|ja|国道34号|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) in the hot spring town and services that stop only at the {{ill|Ureshino Interchange|ja|嬉野インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|Nagasaki Expressway|ja|長崎自動車道|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In recent years, the latter has far more frequent service – while the former runs only 4 times a day, the latter operates roughly every 30 minutes. ** About 2 hours from {{ill|Fukuoka City|ja|福岡市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (via {{ill|Hakata Bus Terminal|ja|博多バスターミナル|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Nishitetsu Tenjin Express Bus Terminal|ja|西鉄天神高速バスターミナル|qq=draft|qq=draft}}). ** About 1 hour from {{ill|Nagasaki City|ja|長崎市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (from {{ill|Nagasaki Station|ja|長崎駅|lt=Nagasaki Station Front|lt_ja=長崎駅前|qq=draft|qq=draft}}). * Shared Taxi from the Airport *: With the opening of {{ill|Saga Airport|ja|佐賀空港|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, local taxi companies began operating services. The travel time from Saga Airport is approximately 1 hour. * Private Car *: 5 minutes via the {{ill|Nagasaki Prefectural and Saga Prefectural Route 1 Sasebo-Ureshino Line|ja|長崎県道・佐賀県道1号佐世保嬉野線|qq=draft|qq=draft}} from the Ureshino Interchange on the {{ill|Nagasaki Expressway|ja|長崎自動車道|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == References == == Related Literature == *{{Cite book |Language=Japanese |author=Masamichi Ikeda|year=1898|title=Ureshino Onsen Chronicles|id={{NDLJP|766546}}|quote= }} == See Also == {{commonscat|Ureshino Onsen}} * {{ill|Tourist Attractions in Saga {{日本の温泉地 |名称 = 嬉野温泉 |画像 = Ureshino onsen.jpg |コメント = |所在地 = [[佐賀県]][[嬉野市]][[嬉野町 (佐賀県)|嬉野町]] |交通アクセス = 鉄道 : [[佐世保線]][[武雄温泉駅]]より[[JR九州バス]]で約30分
西九州新幹線嬉野温泉駅
''他のアクセス方法は、下の[[#アクセス|アクセス]]を参照のこと'' |泉質 = [[塩化物泉]] |泉温 = |湧出量 = |pH =7.8 |液性の分類 = |浸透圧の分類 = |宿泊施設数 = |総収容人員数 = |年間浴客数 = |統計年度 = |外部リンク = [https://spa-u.net/ 嬉野温泉観光協会] |特記事項 = }} '''嬉野温泉'''（うれしのおんせん）は[[佐賀県]][[嬉野市]][[嬉野町 (佐賀県)|嬉野町]]（旧国[[肥前国]]）にある[[温泉]]。[[武雄温泉]]と並び県を代表する温泉である。[[日本百景]]の一つに選ばれ、「日本三大美肌の湯・嬉野温泉」、「佐賀・嬉野温泉」の名称で嬉野市により商標登録されている。 == 泉質 == * ナトリウム - 炭酸水素塩・塩化物泉 美肌に効果がある重曹泉で、[[入浴]]した後につるつる感がある。その泉質は[[藤田聡]]によって「[[日本三大美肌の湯]]」に選ばれている（残り2つは[[斐乃上温泉]]、[[喜連川温泉]]）。 == 温泉街 == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Siebold-no-yu.jpg|thumb|300px|{{Center| シーボルトの湯}} ]] 町の中心地に湧く温泉地で、九州でも有数の大温泉街である。[[塩田川 (佐賀県)|塩田川]]（[[嬉野川]]）を挟んで大小50軒近くの[[旅館]]が軒を並べ、その中には、1987年（昭和62年）に佐賀県で行われた第38回[[全国植樹祭]]の際に[[昭和天皇]]が宿泊した[[和多屋別荘]]等がある。また、嬉野の中で最も古い旅館は[[1830年]]（天保元年）に創業した旅館大村屋といわれる。 商店街中心部の足湯広場には、「[[フィリップ・フランツ・フォン・シーボルト|シーボルト]]の足湯」があり、無料で利用できる。近くには[[1924年]]（大正13年）に[[ドイツ人]]の設計で造られた木造2階建て（一部3階）・地下１階の[[公衆浴場]]「古湯温泉」があり、2001年前後時点では、内部や配管の老朽化があったものの建物外観はほぼ良好な保存状態だった{{Cite book|和書 |title=佐賀県の近代化遺産-佐賀県近代化遺産（建造物等）総合調査報告書- |year=2002 |publisher=佐賀県教育委員会 |page=182 |series=佐賀県文化財調査報告書第153集}}。しかし、2005年（平成17年）3月20日に発生した[[福岡県西方沖地震]]の影響で取り壊された。その後、地元の要望を受けて2010年（平成22年）4月1日に、大正時代の姿に再現され{{Cite web |title=＜重点報道＠嬉野市＞わがまち今昔 シーボルトの湯 {{!}} まちの話題 {{!}} 佐賀新聞ニュース |url=https://www.saga-s.co.jp/articles/-/1114588 |website=佐賀新聞 |date=2024-04-09 |access-date=2024-04-09 |language=ja}}、新名称「シーボルトの湯」として再開された。 美肌の湯とも呼称される嬉野温泉は、飲用にも適しており、中でも温泉を使って炊いているという温泉[[湯豆腐]]は嬉野を代表する名物である。また嬉野市においては「湯どうふ」と表記されており、「嬉野温泉湯どうふ」の名称は嬉野市により商標登録されている。 == 歴史 == [[File:Ureshino Onsen 01.jpg|thumb|280px|{{Center| 温泉街}} ]] 嬉野温泉は、奈良時代に編纂された『[[肥前国風土記]]』に「万人の病を治す温泉」との記述が初出であるが、温泉の名称は記されていない嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980年、272頁。 伝説によると[[神功皇后]]が[[三韓征伐]]の帰途に温泉を発見し、兵士の疲れを癒した際「あな、うれしや」と感歎したことが「嬉野」の地名になったとするが、それ以外にも高祖太子（『大定寺旧記』）や老婆（『豊玉姫神社の社伝』）が「嬉し」と発言した伝説があり、これらは地名「うれしの」が「嬉野」の文字になった後、類推されたもので、地名「うれしの」と「嬉し」発言は直接的に関係が無いとされる。なお、「うれしの」との文言が初めて史料で確認されるのは鎌倉時代で、当時は「宇礼志野」と書かれていた嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980年、351～353頁。地名の由来は、塩田川の上流にある野であるため先端を意味する末（うれ）から「末し野」と呼ばれ、[[瑞祥地名|後に漢字を当てた地名]]とされる{{Cite book|和書 |title=佐賀地名うんちく事典 |year=2005 |publisher=佐賀新聞社 |page=93}}。 その後しばらく、温泉に関する史料がないが、戦国時代末期（1570年代）になると、[[龍造寺隆信]]が嬉野での湯治をすすめた記録が現れる嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980年、710頁。 [[江戸時代]]には[[長崎街道]]の[[宿場町]]・嬉野宿として栄えた。明暦２（1656）年[[蓮池藩]]初代藩主鍋島直澄の時、豊玉姫神社の管理下だった泉源の管理が蓮池藩に移り、露天風呂から屋根がかけられ藩営浴場となった。宿場には多くの往来があり、中でも『和漢三才図会』や『江戸紀行』などに嬉野温泉の様子が記され、この頃から歓楽温泉としても知られていたようである。 戦後は西の[[別府温泉|別府]]といわれるほど歓楽温泉として名を馳せた。だが、各の温泉旅館は風格が調っており、それぞれが趣を持った風呂を持っている。また、イベントも多く実施されているが、他の温泉地と比較すると、新たな施設の投入は少ない方である。 [[嬉野市]]の[[嬉野町 (佐賀県)|旧嬉野町]]では、古くから[[茶]]が栽培されている。そのため、嬉野市や観光協会では、'''「お茶といで湯の」温泉地'''であることを積極的に宣伝しており、両者を結びつけた様々な取組みも行っている。また、温泉をモチーフにした2次元キャラクター「嬉野六香」（[[温泉むすめ]]）が、温泉のPRに活用されている{{Cite web |url=https://onsen-musume.jp/character/ureshino_rikka |title=嬉野 六香 |access-date=2024-09-22 |publisher=株式会社エンバウンド |website=温泉むすめ公式サイト}}。 == アクセス == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Tofu.jpg|thumb|190px|{{Center| 江戸時代からの名物
『温泉湯豆腐』}} ]] * 鉄道（[[九州旅客鉄道|JR九州]]駅からのアクセス） ** [[西九州新幹線]] [[嬉野温泉駅]]より[[JR九州バス]]で約13分。 ** [[佐世保線]] [[武雄温泉駅]]よりJR九州バスで約30分。 ** 佐世保線 [[佐世保駅]]から[[西肥自動車|西肥バス]]で約1時間。 ** [[長崎本線]] [[肥前鹿島駅]]から[[祐徳自動車|祐徳バス]]で約30分。 ** [[大村線]] [[彼杵駅]]からJR九州バスで約25分。 * 高速バス *: [[九州急行バス]]が運行する「[[九州号]]」を利用。温泉街にある[[嬉野バスセンター]]（[[国道34号]]）を経由する便と[[長崎自動車道]] [[嬉野インターチェンジ]]のみに停車する便とがあり、近年は路線高速化の影響で後者の本数が圧倒的に多い。前者が1日4本しかないのに対し、後者はおよそ30分に1本の割合で運行されている。 ** [[福岡市]]（[[博多バスターミナル]]・[[西鉄天神高速バスターミナル]]）から約2時間 ** [[長崎市]]（[[長崎駅|長崎駅前]]）から約1時間 * 空港乗合タクシー *: [[佐賀空港]]の開港にあわせ、地元タクシー会社が運行を開始。佐賀空港からの所要時間はおよそ1時間 * 自家用車 *: 長崎自動車道 嬉野インターチェンジより[[長崎県道・佐賀県道1号佐世保嬉野線]]経由で5分。 == 脚注 == ==関連文献== *{{Cite book |和書 |author=池田政道|year=1898|title=嬉野温泉誌|id={{NDLJP|766546}}|quote= }} == 関連項目 == {{commonscat|Ureshino Onsen}} *[[佐賀県の観光地]] * [[西九州新幹線]] * [[嬉野温泉駅]] * [[肥前夢街道]] * [[和多屋別荘]] * [[入船荘]] * [[ソープランド]] * [[柳田悠岐]]…毎年嬉野温泉で自主トレを行うため。 * [[塩田津]]の町並み（[[重要伝統的建造物群保存地区]]）…嬉野宿の次の宿場町 == 外部リンク == * [https://spa-u.net/ 嬉野温泉観光協会] * [https://www.nicovideo.jp/watch/1269845231 ニコニコ動画 嬉野温泉の公衆浴場「シーボルトの湯」]（[[佐賀新聞]]提供） {{温泉}} {{Portal bar|日本|佐賀県|温泉}} {{DEFAULTSORT:うれしのおんせん}} [[Category:佐賀県の温泉]] [[Category:佐賀県の歴史]] [[Category:嬉野市の地理]]

{{日本の温泉地 |名称 = 嬉野温泉 |画像 = Ureshino onsen.jpg |コメント = |所在地 = [[佐賀県]][[嬉野市]][[嬉野町 (佐賀県)|嬉野町]] |交通アクセス = 鉄道 : [[佐世保線]][[武雄温泉駅]]より[[JR九州バス]]で約30分
西九州新幹線嬉野温泉駅
''他のアクセス方法は、下の[[#アクセス|アクセス]]を参照のこと'' |泉質 = [[塩化物泉]] |泉温 = |湧出量 = |pH =7.8 |液性の分類 = |浸透圧の分類 = |宿泊施設数 = |総収容人員数 = |年間浴客数 = |統計年度 = |外部リンク = [https://spa-u.net/ 嬉野温泉観光協会] |特記事項 = }} '''嬉野温泉'''（うれしのおんせん）は[[佐賀県]][[嬉野市]][[嬉野町 (佐賀県)|嬉野町]]（旧国[[肥前国]]）にある[[温泉]]。[[武雄温泉]]と並び県を代表する温泉である。[[日本百景]]の一つに選ばれ、「日本三大美肌の湯・嬉野温泉」、「佐賀・嬉野温泉」の名称で嬉野市により商標登録されている。 == 泉質 == * ナトリウム - 炭酸水素塩・塩化物泉 美肌に効果がある重曹泉で、[[入浴]]した後につるつる感がある。その泉質は[[藤田聡]]によって「[[日本三大美肌の湯]]」に選ばれている（残り2つは[[斐乃上温泉]]、[[喜連川温泉]]）。 == 温泉街 == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Siebold-no-yu.jpg|thumb|300px|{{Center| シーボルトの湯}} ]] 町の中心地に湧く温泉地で、九州でも有数の大温泉街である。[[塩田川 (佐賀県)|塩田川]]（[[嬉野川]]）を挟んで大小50軒近くの[[旅館]]が軒を並べ、その中には、1987年（昭和62年）に佐賀県で行われた第38回[[全国植樹祭]]の際に[[昭和天皇]]が宿泊した[[和多屋別荘]]等がある。また、嬉野の中で最も古い旅館は[[1830年]]（天保元年）に創業した旅館大村屋といわれる。 商店街中心部の足湯広場には、「[[フィリップ・フランツ・フォン・シーボルト|シーボルト]]の足湯」があり、無料で利用できる。近くには[[1924年]]（大正13年）に[[ドイツ人]]の設計で造られた木造2階建て（一部3階）・地下１階の[[公衆浴場]]「古湯温泉」があり、2001年前後時点では、内部や配管の老朽化があったものの建物外観はほぼ良好な保存状態だった{{Cite book|和書 |title=佐賀県の近代化遺産-佐賀県近代化遺産（建造物等）総合調査報告書- |year=2002 |publisher=佐賀県教育委員会 |page=182 |series=佐賀県文化財調査報告書第153集}}。しかし、2005年（平成17年）3月20日に発生した[[福岡県西方沖地震]]の影響で取り壊された。その後、地元の要望を受けて2010年（平成22年）4月1日に、大正時代の姿に再現され{{Cite web |title=＜重点報道＠嬉野市＞わがまち今昔 シーボルトの湯 {{!}} まちの話題 {{!}} 佐賀新聞ニュース |url=https://www.saga-s.co.jp/articles/-/1114588 |website=佐賀新聞 |date=2024-04-09 |access-date=2024-04-09 |language=ja}}、新名称「シーボルトの湯」として再開された。 美肌の湯とも呼称される嬉野温泉は、飲用にも適しており、中でも温泉を使って炊いているという温泉[[湯豆腐]]は嬉野を代表する名物である。また嬉野市においては「湯どうふ」と表記されており、「嬉野温泉湯どうふ」の名称は嬉野市により商標登録されている。 == 歴史 == [[File:Ureshino Onsen 01.jpg|thumb|280px|{{Center| 温泉街}} ]] 江戸時代からの名物
『温泉湯豆腐』}} ]] * 鉄道（[[九州旅客鉄道|JR九州]]駅からのアクセス） ** [[西九州新幹線]] [[嬉野温泉駅]]より[[JR九州バス]]で約13分。 ** [[佐世保線]] [[武雄温泉駅]]よりJR九州バスで約30分。 ** 佐世保線 [[佐世保駅]]から[[西肥自動車|西肥バス]]で約1時間。 ** [[長崎本線]] [[肥前鹿島駅]]から[[祐徳自動車|祐徳バス]]で約30分。 ** [[大村線]] [[彼杵駅]]からJR九州バスで約25分。 * 高速バス *: [[九州急行バス]]が運行する「[[九州号]]」を利用。温泉街にある[[嬉野バスセンター]]（[[国道34号]]）を経由する便と[[長崎自動車道]] [[嬉野インターチェンジ]]のみに停車する便とがあり、近年は路線高速化の影響で後者の本数が圧倒的に多い。前者が1日4本しかないのに対し、後者はおよそ30分に1本の割合で運行されている。 ** [[福岡市]]（[[博多バスターミナル]]・[[西鉄天神高速バスターミナル]]）から約2時間 ** [[長崎市]]（[[長崎駅|長崎駅前]]）から約1時間 * 空港乗合タクシー *: [[佐賀空港]]の開港にあわせ、地元タクシー会社が運行を開始。佐賀空港からの所要時間はおよそ1時間 * 自家用車 *: 長崎自動車道 嬉野インターチェンジより[[長崎県道・佐賀県道1号佐世保嬉野線]]経由で5分。 == 脚注 == ==関連文献== *{{Cite book |和書 |author=池田政道|year=1898|title=嬉野温泉誌|id={{NDLJP|766546}}|quote= }} == 関連項目 == {{commonscat|Ureshino Onsen}} *[[佐賀県の観光地]] * [[西九州新幹線]] * [[嬉野温泉駅]] * [[肥前夢街道]] * [[和多屋別荘]] * [[入船荘]] * [[ソープランド]] * [[柳田悠岐]]…毎年嬉野温泉で自主トレを行うため。 * [[塩田津]]の町並み（[[重要伝統的建造物群保存地区]]）…嬉野宿の次の宿場町 == 外部リンク == * [https://spa-u.net/ 嬉野温泉観光協会] * [https://www.nicovideo.jp/watch/1269845231 ニコニコ動画 嬉野温泉の公衆浴場「シーボルトの湯」]（[[佐賀新聞]]提供） {{温泉}} {{Portal bar|日本|佐賀県|温泉}} {{DEFAULTSORT:うれしのおんせん}} [[Category:佐賀県の温泉]] [[Category:佐賀県の歴史]] [[Category:嬉野市の地理]]

{{infobox Onsen |Name = Ureshino Onsen |image = Ureshino onsen.jpg |Comment = |Location = {{ill|Saga Prefecture|ja|佐賀県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Ureshino Town|ja|嬉野町 (佐賀県)|lt=Ureshino Town|lt_ja=嬉野町|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |Access = Railway : {{ill|Sasebo Line|ja|佐世保線|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Takeo Onsen Station|ja|武雄温泉駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} via {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|qq=draft|qq=draft}} for about 30 minutes
West Kyushu Shinkansen Ureshino Onsen Station
''For other access methods, see [[#アクセス|Access]]'' |Water Type = {{ill|Chloride Hot Spring|ja|塩化物泉|1=Brine spring|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |Temperature = |Discharge = |pH =7.8 |Liquid Classification = |Osmotic Pressure Classification = |Number of Accommodations = |Total Capacity = |Annual Bath Visitors = |Statistical Year = |External links = [https://spa-u.net/ Ureshino Onsen Tourism Association] |Special Notes = }} '''Ureshino Onsen''' (嬉野温泉) is a {{ill|Hot Spring|ja|温泉|1=Onsen|1=Onsen|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Saga Prefecture|ja|佐賀県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Ureshino Town|ja|嬉野町 (佐賀県)|lt=Ureshino Town|lt_ja=嬉野町|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (formerly part of {{ill|Hizen Province|ja|肥前国|qq=draft|qq=draft}}). Along with {{ill|Takeo Onsen|ja|武雄温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it is one of the representative hot springs of the prefecture. It has been selected as one of {{ill|Japan's 100 Views|ja|日本百景|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and is trademarked by Ureshino City under the names “Japan’s Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs Ureshino Onsen” and “Saga–Ureshino Onsen.” == Water Type == * Sodium – Bicarbonate Salt / Chloride Hot Spring It is a baking soda spring renowned for its beauty-enhancing properties, leaving the skin exceptionally smooth after a {{ill|Bathing|ja|入浴|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Its water quality was chosen by {{ill|Satoshi Fujita|ja|藤田聡|qq=draft|qq=draft}} as one of the {{ill|Japan's Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs|ja|日本三大美肌の湯|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (the other two being {{ill|Hinokami Onsen|ja|斐乃上温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Kirekawa Onsen|ja|喜連川温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft}}). == Onsen Town == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Siebold-no-yu.jpg|thumb|300px|{{Center|Siebold's Bath (シーボルトの湯)}} ]] This hot spring area, which rises in the heart of the town, is one of the largest onsen towns in Kyushu. Nearly 50 {{ill|Ryokan|ja|旅館|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – both large and small – line the streets along the banks of the {{ill|Shioda River|ja|塩田川 (佐賀県)|lt=Shioda River|lt_ja=塩田川|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ureshino River|ja|嬉野川|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), including Wataya Villa, where {{ill|Emperor Shōwa|ja|昭和天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}} stayed during the 38th {{ill|National Tree Planting Festival|ja|全国植樹祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} held in Saga Prefecture in 1987 (Showa 62). In addition, the oldest inn in Ureshino is said to be {{ill|Omuraya|ja|大村屋|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, founded in 1830 (the first year of the Tenpō era). In the center of the shopping district’s footbath plaza, there is “{{ill|Siebold|ja|フィリップ・フランツ・フォン・シーボルト|lt=Siebold|lt_ja=シーボルト|qq=draft|qq=draft}}’s Foot Bath,” which is available free of charge. Nearby stands the wooden, two-story (partly three-story) with one basement {{ill|Public Bath|ja|公衆浴場|1=public bathing|lt=Public Bathhouse|qq=draft|qq=draft}} “Furuyu Onsen,” constructed in 1924 (Taishō 13) to a design by a {{ill|German|ja|ドイツ人|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Although by around 2001 its interior and piping had deteriorated, the building’s exterior remained in nearly excellent condition{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀県の近代化遺産-佐賀県近代化遺産（建造物等）総合調査報告書-|year=2002|publisher=佐賀県教育委員会|page=182|series=佐賀県文化財調査報告書第153集}}. However, it was demolished on March 20, 2005 (Heisei 17) due to damage from the {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture Western Offshore Earthquake|ja|福岡県西方沖地震|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Later, in response to local demand, it was reconstructed to replicate its Taishō-era appearance and reopened on April 1, 2010 (Heisei 22) under the new name “Siebold’s Bath”{{Cite web |title=＜重点報道＠嬉野市＞わがまち今昔 シーボルトの湯 {{!}} まちの話題 {{!}} 佐賀新聞ニュース |url=https://www.saga-s.co.jp/articles/-/1114588 |website=佐賀新聞 |date=2024-04-09 |access-date=2024-04-09 |language=ja}}. Also known as the “Hot Spring for Beautiful Skin,” Ureshino Onsen is suitable for drinking. Its signature dish, the hot spring {{ill|Hot Spring Tofu|ja|湯豆腐|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, prepared using the onsen water, is a renowned specialty of Ureshino. In Ureshino City the product is written as “Yudōfu,” and the name “Ureshino Onsen Yudōfu” is trademarked by the city. == History == [[File:Ureshino Onsen 01.jpg|thumb|280px|{{Center|Onsen Town|1=Spa Town|lt=Onsen Town}} ]] Ureshino Onsen first appears in historical records in the ''Hizen Province Fudoki'' ({{ill|Hizen Province Fudoki|ja|肥前国風土記|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), compiled during the Nara period, with a description as a “hot spring that cures the ailments of all people,” although its name is not mentioned嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、272頁. According to legend, {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后|qq=draft|qq=draft}} discovered the hot spring on her return from the {{ill|Conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea|ja|三韓征伐|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and, while soothing her soldiers’ fatigue, exclaimed something akin to “How delightful!”—a remark that was later associated with the naming of “Ureshino.” Other legends tell of either Prince Takaso (from the ''Daidōji Kyuuki'') or an old woman (from the legend of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) exclaiming “ureshi.” These tales, however, were retroactively linked after the name “Ureshino” (originally read “ureshino”) was established, and the exclamation is not considered directly connected to the place name. In fact, the term “ureshino” is first confirmed in historical documents during the Kamakura period, when it was written as “宇礼志野”嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、351～353頁. The origin of the name is attributed to a field located in the upper reaches of the Shioda River; because the word “末” (ure) means “tip” or “end,” the area was called “Sueshino” and later a kanji was assigned to form the name{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀地名うんちく事典|year=2005|publisher=佐賀新聞社|page=93}}. After a period with few records concerning the hot spring, by the late Sengoku period (1570s) records emerge of {{ill|Ryūzōji Takanobu|ja|龍造寺隆信|qq=draft|qq=draft}} recommending hot spring therapy in Ureshino嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、710頁. During the {{ill|Edo Period|ja|江戸時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Ureshino Onsen flourished as Ureshino-juku, a {{ill|Post Town|ja|宿場町|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|Nagasaki Kaidō|ja|長崎街道|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In 1656 (Meireki 2), during the time of the first lord of the {{ill|Hasuike Domain|ja|蓮池藩|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Nabeshima Naotoshi, management of the spring source – previously under the jurisdiction of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – was transferred to the domain, and a roof was added to the open-air bath, converting it into a domain-run bathhouse. The post town was frequented by many travelers, and the state of Ureshino Onsen was recorded in works such as ''Wakan Sansai Zue'' and ''Edo Travelogue''. It appears that from this period it also became known as an entertainment hot spring. After World War II, Ureshino Onsen gained fame as an entertainment hot spring comparable to {{ill|Beppu Onsen|ja|別府温泉|lt=Beppu|lt_ja=別府|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the west. However, each onsen inn has its own distinctive style and character, and while many events are held, comparatively few new facilities have been introduced. In the former Ureshino Town (now part of {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) tea has been cultivated for generations. For this reason, Ureshino City and its tourism association actively promote the area as '''"Hot Spring Land of Tea and Tofu"''', and various initiatives have been undertaken to link the two. In addition, a 2D character themed on hot springs, “Ureshino Rokka” (from {{ill|Onsen Musume|ja|温泉むすめ|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), is used to promote the hot springs{{Cite web |url=https://onsen-musume.jp/character/ureshino_rikka |title=嬉野 六香 |access-date=2024-09-22 |publisher=株式会社エンバウンド |website=温泉むすめ公式サイト}}. == Access == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Tofu.jpg|thumb|190px|{{Center|A Famous Specialty from the Edo Period

''For other access methods, see [[#アクセス|Access]]'' |Water Type = {{ill|Chloride Hot Spring|ja|塩化物泉|1=Brine spring|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |Temperature = |Discharge = |pH =7.8 |Liquid Classification = |Osmotic Pressure Classification = |Number of Accommodations = |Total Capacity = |Annual Bath Visitors = |Statistical Year = |External links = [https://spa-u.net/ Ureshino Onsen Tourism Association] |Special Notes = }} '''Ureshino Onsen''' (嬉野温泉) is a {{ill|Hot Spring|ja|温泉|1=Onsen|1=Onsen|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Saga Prefecture|ja|佐賀県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Ureshino Town|ja|嬉野町 (佐賀県)|lt=Ureshino Town|lt_ja=嬉野町|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (formerly part of {{ill|Hizen Province|ja|肥前国|qq=draft|qq=draft}}). Along with {{ill|Takeo Onsen|ja|武雄温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it is one of the representative hot springs of the prefecture. It has been selected as one of {{ill|Japan's 100 Views|ja|日本百景|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and is trademarked by Ureshino City under the names “Japan’s Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs Ureshino Onsen” and “Saga–Ureshino Onsen.” == Water Type == * Sodium – Bicarbonate Salt / Chloride Hot Spring It is a baking soda spring renowned for its beauty-enhancing properties, leaving the skin exceptionally smooth after a {{ill|Bathing|ja|入浴|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Its water quality was chosen by {{ill|Satoshi Fujita|ja|藤田聡|qq=draft|qq=draft}} as one of the {{ill|Japan's Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs|ja|日本三大美肌の湯|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (the other two being {{ill|Hinokami Onsen|ja|斐乃上温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Kirekawa Onsen|ja|喜連川温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft}}). == Onsen Town == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Siebold-no-yu.jpg|thumb|300px|{{Center|Siebold's Bath (シーボルトの湯)}} ]] This hot spring area, which rises in the heart of the town, is one of the largest onsen towns in Kyushu. Nearly 50 {{ill|Ryokan|ja|旅館|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – both large and small – line the streets along the banks of the {{ill|Shioda River|ja|塩田川 (佐賀県)|lt=Shioda River|lt_ja=塩田川|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ureshino River|ja|嬉野川|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), including Wataya Villa, where {{ill|Emperor Shōwa|ja|昭和天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}} stayed during the 38th {{ill|National Tree Planting Festival|ja|全国植樹祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} held in Saga Prefecture in 1987 (Showa 62). In addition, the oldest inn in Ureshino is said to be {{ill|Omuraya|ja|大村屋|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, founded in 1830 (the first year of the Tenpō era). In the center of the shopping district’s footbath plaza, there is “{{ill|Siebold|ja|フィリップ・フランツ・フォン・シーボルト|lt=Siebold|lt_ja=シーボルト|qq=draft|qq=draft}}’s Foot Bath,” which is available free of charge. {{infobox Onsen |Name = Ureshino Onsen |image = Ureshino onsen.jpg |Comment = |Location = {{ill|Saga Prefecture|ja|佐賀県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Ureshino Town|ja|嬉野町 (佐賀県)|lt=Ureshino Town|lt_ja=嬉野町|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |Access = Railway : {{ill|Sasebo Line|ja|佐世保線|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Takeo Onsen Station|ja|武雄温泉駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} via {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|qq=draft|qq=draft}} for about 30 minutes
West Kyushu Shinkansen Ureshino Onsen Station
''For other access methods, see [[#アクセス|Access]]'' |Water Type = {{ill|Chloride Hot Spring|ja|塩化物泉|1=Brine spring|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |Temperature = |Discharge = |pH =7.8 |Liquid Classification = |Osmotic Pressure Classification = |Number of Accommodations = |Total Capacity = |Annual Bath Visitors = |Statistical Year = |External links = [https://spa-u.net/ Ureshino Onsen Tourism Association] |Special Notes = }} '''Ureshino Onsen''' (嬉野温泉) is a {{ill|Hot Spring|ja|温泉|1=Onsen|1=Onsen|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Saga Prefecture|ja|佐賀県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Ureshino Town|ja|嬉野町 (佐賀県)|lt=Ureshino Town|lt_ja=嬉野町|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (formerly part of {{ill|Hizen Province|ja|肥前国|qq=draft|qq=draft}}). Along with {{ill|Takeo Onsen|ja|武雄温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it is one of the representative hot springs of the prefecture. It has been selected as one of {{ill|Japan's 100 Views|ja|日本百景|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and is trademarked by Ureshino City under the names “Japan’s Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs Ureshino Onsen” and “Saga–Ureshino Onsen.” == Water Type == * Sodium – Bicarbonate Salt / Chloride Hot Spring It is a baking soda spring renowned for its beauty-enhancing properties, leaving the skin exceptionally smooth after a {{ill|Bathing|ja|入浴|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Its water quality was chosen by {{ill|Satoshi Fujita|ja|藤田聡|qq=draft|qq=draft}} as one of the {{ill|Japan's Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs|ja|日本三大美肌の湯|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (the other two being {{ill|Hinokami Onsen|ja|斐乃上温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Kirekawa Onsen|ja|喜連川温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft}}). == Onsen Town == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Siebold-no-yu.jpg|thumb|300px|{{Center|Siebold's Bath (シーボルトの湯)}} ]] This hot spring area, which rises in the heart of the town, is one of the largest onsen towns in Kyushu. Nearly 50 {{ill|Ryokan|ja|旅館|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – both large and small – line the streets along the banks of the {{ill|Shioda River|ja|塩田川 (佐賀県)|lt=Shioda River|lt_ja=塩田川|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ureshino River|ja|嬉野川|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), including Wataya Villa, where {{ill|Emperor Shōwa|ja|昭和天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}} stayed during the 38th {{ill|National Tree Planting Festival|ja|全国植樹祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} held in Saga Prefecture in 1987 (Showa 62). In addition, the oldest inn in Ureshino is said to be {{ill|Omuraya|ja|大村屋|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, founded in 1830 (the first year of the Tenpō era). In the center of the shopping district’s footbath plaza, there is “{{ill|Siebold|ja|フィリップ・フランツ・フォン・シーボルト|lt=Siebold|lt_ja=シーボルト|qq=draft|qq=draft}}’s Foot Bath,” which is available free of charge. Nearby stands the wooden, two-story (partly three-story) with one basement {{ill|Public Bath|ja|公衆浴場|1=public bathing|lt=Public Bathhouse|qq=draft|qq=draft}} “Furuyu Onsen,” constructed in 1924 (Taishō 13) to a design by a {{ill|German|ja|ドイツ人|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Although by around 2001 its interior and piping had deteriorated, the building’s exterior remained in nearly excellent condition{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀県の近代化遺産-佐賀県近代化遺産（建造物等）総合調査報告書-|year=2002|publisher=佐賀県教育委員会|page=182|series=佐賀県文化財調査報告書第153集}}. However, it was demolished on March 20, 2005 (Heisei 17) due to damage from the {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture Western Offshore Earthquake|ja|福岡県西方沖地震|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Later, in response to local demand, it was reconstructed to replicate its Taishō-era appearance and reopened on April 1, 2010 (Heisei 22) under the new name “Siebold’s Bath”{{Cite web |title=＜重点報道＠嬉野市＞わがまち今昔 シーボルトの湯 {{!}} まちの話題 {{!}} 佐賀新聞ニュース |url=https://www.saga-s.co.jp/articles/-/1114588 |website=佐賀新聞 |date=2024-04-09 |access-date=2024-04-09 |language=ja}}. Also known as the “Hot Spring for Beautiful Skin,” Ureshino Onsen is suitable for drinking. Its signature dish, the hot spring {{ill|Hot Spring Tofu|ja|湯豆腐|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, prepared using the onsen water, is a renowned specialty of Ureshino. In Ureshino City the product is written as “Yudōfu,” and the name “Ureshino Onsen Yudōfu” is trademarked by the city. == History == [[File:Ureshino Onsen 01.jpg|thumb|280px|{{Center|Onsen Town|1=Spa Town|lt=Onsen Town}} ]] Ureshino Onsen first appears in historical records in the ''Hizen Province Fudoki'' ({{ill|Hizen Province Fudoki|ja|肥前国風土記|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), compiled during the Nara period, with a description as a “hot spring that cures the ailments of all people,” although its name is not mentioned嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、272頁. According to legend, {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后|qq=draft|qq=draft}} discovered the hot spring on her return from the {{ill|Conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea|ja|三韓征伐|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and, while soothing her soldiers’ fatigue, exclaimed something akin to “How delightful!”—a remark that was later associated with the naming of “Ureshino.” Other legends tell of either Prince Takaso (from the ''Daidōji Kyuuki'') or an old woman (from the legend of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) exclaiming “ureshi.” These tales, however, were retroactively linked after the name “Ureshino” (originally read “ureshino”) was established, and the exclamation is not considered directly connected to the place name. In fact, the term “ureshino” is first confirmed in historical documents during the Kamakura period, when it was written as “宇礼志野”嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、351～353頁. The origin of the name is attributed to a field located in the upper reaches of the Shioda River; because the word “末” (ure) means “tip” or “end,” the area was called “Sueshino” and later a kanji was assigned to form the name{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀地名うんちく事典|year=2005|publisher=佐賀新聞社|page=93}}. After a period with few records concerning the hot spring, by the late Sengoku period (1570s) records emerge of {{ill|Ryūzōji Takanobu|ja|龍造寺隆信|qq=draft|qq=draft}} recommending hot spring therapy in Ureshino嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、710頁. During the {{ill|Edo Period|ja|江戸時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Ureshino Onsen flourished as Ureshino-juku, a {{ill|Post Town|ja|宿場町|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|Nagasaki Kaidō|ja|長崎街道|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In 1656 (Meireki 2), during the time of the first lord of the {{ill|Hasuike Domain|ja|蓮池藩|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Nabeshima Naotoshi, management of the spring source – previously under the jurisdiction of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – was transferred to the domain, and a roof was added to the open-air bath, converting it into a domain-run bathhouse. The post town was frequented by many travelers, and the state of Ureshino Onsen was recorded in works such as ''Wakan Sansai Zue'' and ''Edo Travelogue''. It appears that from this period it also became known as an entertainment hot spring. After World War II, Ureshino Onsen gained fame as an entertainment hot spring comparable to {{ill|Beppu Onsen|ja|別府温泉|lt=Beppu|lt_ja=別府|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the west. However, each onsen inn has its own distinctive style and character, and while many events are held, comparatively few new facilities have been introduced. In the former Ureshino Town (now part of {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) tea has been cultivated for generations. For this reason, Ureshino City and its tourism association actively promote the area as '''"Hot Spring Land of Tea and Tofu"''', and various initiatives have been undertaken to link the two. In addition, a 2D character themed on hot springs, “Ureshino Rokka” (from {{ill|Onsen Musume|ja|温泉むすめ|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), is used to promote the hot springs{{Cite web |url=https://onsen-musume.jp/character/ureshino_rikka |title=嬉野 六香 |access-date=2024-09-22 |publisher=株式会社エンバウンド |website=温泉むすめ公式サイト}}. == Access == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Tofu.jpg|thumb|190px|{{Center|A Famous Specialty from the Edo Period

''For other access methods, see [[#アクセス|Access]]'' |Water Type = {{ill|Chloride Hot Spring|ja|塩化物泉|1=Brine spring|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |Temperature = |Discharge = |pH =7.8 |Liquid Classification = |Osmotic Pressure Classification = |Number of Accommodations = |Total Capacity = |Annual Bath Visitors = |Statistical Year = |External links = [https://spa-u.net/ Ureshino Onsen Tourism Association] |Special Notes = }} '''Ureshino Onsen''' (嬉野温泉) is a {{ill|Hot Spring|ja|温泉|1=Onsen|1=Onsen|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Saga Prefecture|ja|佐賀県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Ureshino Town|ja|嬉野町 (佐賀県)|lt=Ureshino Town|lt_ja=嬉野町|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (formerly part of {{ill|Hizen Province|ja|肥前国|qq=draft|qq=draft}}). Along with {{ill|Takeo Onsen|ja|武雄温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it is one of the representative hot springs of the prefecture. It has been selected as one of {{ill|Japan's 100 Views|ja|日本百景|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and is trademarked by Ureshino City under the names “Japan’s Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs Ureshino Onsen” and “Saga–Ureshino Onsen.” == Water Type == * Sodium – Bicarbonate Salt / Chloride Hot Spring It is a baking soda spring renowned for its beauty-enhancing properties, leaving the skin exceptionally smooth after a {{ill|Bathing|ja|入浴|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Its water quality was chosen by {{ill|Satoshi Fujita|ja|藤田聡|qq=draft|qq=draft}} as one of the {{ill|Japan's Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs|ja|日本三大美肌の湯|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (the other two being {{ill|Hinokami Onsen|ja|斐乃上温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Kirekawa Onsen|ja|喜連川温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft}}). == Onsen Town == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Siebold-no-yu.jpg|thumb|300px|{{Center|Siebold's Bath (シーボルトの湯)}} ]] This hot spring area, which rises in the heart of the town, is one of the largest onsen towns in Kyushu. Nearly 50 {{ill|Ryokan|ja|旅館|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – both large and small – line the streets along the banks of the {{ill|Shioda River|ja|塩田川 (佐賀県)|lt=Shioda River|lt_ja=塩田川|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ureshino River|ja|嬉野川|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), including Wataya Villa, where {{ill|Emperor Shōwa|ja|昭和天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}} stayed during the 38th {{ill|National Tree Planting Festival|ja|全国植樹祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} held in Saga Prefecture in 1987 (Showa 62). In addition, the oldest inn in Ureshino is said to be {{ill|Omuraya|ja|大村屋|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, founded in 1830 (the first year of the Tenpō era). In the center of the shopping district’s footbath plaza, there is “{{ill|Siebold|ja|フィリップ・フランツ・フォン・シーボルト|lt=Siebold|lt_ja=シーボルト|qq=draft|qq=draft}}’s Foot Bath,” which is available free of charge. Nearby stands the wooden, two-story (partly three-story) with one basement {{ill|Public Bath|ja|公衆浴場|1=public bathing|lt=Public Bathhouse|qq=draft|qq=draft}} “Furuyu Onsen,” constructed in 1924 (Taishō 13) to a design by a {{ill|German|ja|ドイツ人|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Although by around 2001 its interior and piping had deteriorated, the building’s exterior remained in nearly excellent condition{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀県の近代化遺産-佐賀県近代化遺産（建造物等）総合調査報告書-|year=2002|publisher=佐賀県教育委員会|page=182|series=佐賀県文化財調査報告書第153集}}. However, it was demolished on March 20, 2005 (Heisei 17) due to damage from the {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture Western Offshore Earthquake|ja|福岡県西方沖地震|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Later, in response to local demand, it was reconstructed to replicate its Taishō-era appearance and reopened on April 1, 2010 (Heisei 22) under the new name “Siebold’s Bath”{{Cite web |title=＜重点報道＠嬉野市＞わがまち今昔 シーボルトの湯 {{!}} まちの話題 {{!}} 佐賀新聞ニュース |url=https://www.saga-s.co.jp/articles/-/1114588 |website=佐賀新聞 |date=2024-04-09 |access-date=2024-04-09 |language=ja}}. Also known as the “Hot Spring for Beautiful Skin,” Ureshino Onsen is suitable for drinking. Its signature dish, the hot spring {{ill|Hot Spring Tofu|ja|湯豆腐|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, prepared using the onsen water, is a renowned specialty of Ureshino. In Ureshino City the product is written as “Yudōfu,” and the name “Ureshino Onsen Yudōfu” is trademarked by the city. == History == [[File:Ureshino Onsen 01.jpg|thumb|280px|{{Center|Onsen Town|1=Spa Town|lt=Onsen Town}} ]] Ureshino Onsen first appears in historical records in the ''Hizen Province Fudoki'' ({{ill|Hizen Province Fudoki|ja|肥前国風土記|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), compiled during the Nara period, with a description as a “hot spring that cures the ailments of all people,” although its name is not mentioned嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、272頁. According to legend, {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后|qq=draft|qq=draft}} discovered the hot spring on her return from the {{ill|Conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea|ja|三韓征伐|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and, while soothing her soldiers’ fatigue, exclaimed something akin to “How delightful!”—a remark that was later associated with the naming of “Ureshino.” Other legends tell of either Prince Takaso (from the ''Daidōji Kyuuki'') or an old woman (from the legend of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) exclaiming “ureshi.” These tales, however, were retroactively linked after the name “Ureshino” (originally read “ureshino”) was established, and the exclamation is not considered directly connected to the place name. In fact, the term “ureshino” is first confirmed in historical documents during the Kamakura period, when it was written as “宇礼志野”嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、351～353頁. The origin of the name is attributed to a field located in the upper reaches of the Shioda River; because the word “末” (ure) means “tip” or “end,” the area was called “Sueshino” and later a kanji was assigned to form the name{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀地名うんちく事典|year=2005|publisher=佐賀新聞社|page=93}}. After a period with few records concerning the hot spring, by the late Sengoku period (1570s) records emerge of {{ill|Ryūzōji Takanobu|ja|龍造寺隆信|qq=draft|qq=draft}} recommending hot spring therapy in Ureshino嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、710頁. During the {{ill|Edo Period|ja|江戸時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Ureshino Onsen flourished as Ureshino-juku, a {{ill|Post Town|ja|宿場町|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|Nagasaki Kaidō|ja|長崎街道|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In 1656 (Meireki 2), during the time of the first lord of the {{ill|Hasuike Domain|ja|蓮池藩|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Nabeshima Naotoshi, management of the spring source – previously under the jurisdiction of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – was transferred to the domain, and a roof was added to the open-air bath, converting it into a domain-run bathhouse. The post town was frequented by many travelers, and the state of Ureshino Onsen was recorded in works such as ''Wakan Sansai Zue'' and ''Edo Travelogue''. It appears that from this period it also became known as an entertainment hot spring. After World War II, Ureshino Onsen gained fame as an entertainment hot spring comparable to {{ill|Beppu Onsen|ja|別府温泉|lt=Beppu|lt_ja=別府|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the west. However, each onsen inn has its own distinctive style and character, and while many events are held, comparatively few new facilities have been introduced. In the former Ureshino Town (now part of {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) tea has been cultivated for generations. For this reason, Ureshino City and its tourism association actively promote the area as '''"Hot Spring Land of Tea and Tofu"''', and various initiatives have been undertaken to link the two. In addition, a 2D character themed on hot springs, “Ureshino Rokka” (from {{ill|Onsen Musume|ja|温泉むすめ|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), is used to promote the hot springs{{Cite web |url=https://onsen-musume.jp/character/ureshino_rikka |title=嬉野 六香 |access-date=2024-09-22 |publisher=株式会社エンバウンド |website=温泉むすめ公式サイト}}. == Access == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Tofu.jpg|thumb|190px|{{Center|A Famous Specialty from the Edo Period
'Hot Spring Tofu'}} ]] * Railway (access from {{ill|JR Kyushu|ja|九州旅客鉄道|lt=JR Kyushu|lt_ja=JR九州|qq=draft|qq=draft}} stations) ** About 13 minutes by {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|qq=draft|qq=draft}} from {{ill|Ureshino Onsen Station|ja|嬉野温泉駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|West Kyushu Shinkansen|ja|西九州新幹線|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. ** About 30 minutes by {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|qq=draft|qq=draft}} from {{ill|Takeo Onsen Station|ja|武雄温泉駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|Sasebo Line|ja|佐世保線|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. ** About 1 hour by {{ill|Nishi-Hii Bus|ja|西肥自動車|lt=Nishi-Hii Bus|lt_ja=西肥バス|qq=draft|qq=draft}} from {{ill|Sasebo Station|ja|佐世保駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the Sasebo Line. ** About 30 minutes by {{ill|Yūtoku Bus|ja|祐徳自動車|lt=Yūtoku Bus|lt_ja=祐徳バス|qq=draft|qq=draft}} from {{ill|Hizen Kashima Station|ja|肥前鹿島駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|Nagasaki Main Line|ja|長崎本線|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. ** About 25 minutes by {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|qq=draft|qq=draft}} from {{ill|Karinoki Station|ja|彼杵駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|Omura Line|ja|大村線|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. * Highway Bus *: Use the “{{ill|Kyushu-go|ja|九州号|qq=draft|qq=draft}}” operated by {{ill|Kyushu Express Bus|ja|九州急行バス|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. There are services that stop at the Ureshino Bus Center ({{ill|National Route 34|ja|国道34号|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) in the hot spring town and services that stop only at the {{ill|Ureshino Interchange|ja|嬉野インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|Nagasaki Expressway|ja|長崎自動車道|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In recent years, the latter has far more frequent service – while the former runs only 4 times a day, the latter operates roughly every 30 minutes. ** About 2 hours from {{ill|Fukuoka City|ja|福岡市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (via {{ill|Hakata Bus Terminal|ja|博多バスターミナル|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Nishitetsu Tenjin Express Bus Terminal|ja|西鉄天神高速バスターミナル|qq=draft|qq=draft}}). ** About 1 hour from {{ill|Nagasaki City|ja|長崎市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (from {{ill|Nagasaki Station|ja|長崎駅|lt=Nagasaki Station Front|lt_ja=長崎駅前|qq=draft|qq=draft}}). * Shared Taxi from the Airport *: With the opening of {{ill|Saga Airport|ja|佐賀空港|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, local taxi companies began operating services. The travel time from Saga Airport is approximately 1 hour. * Private Car *: 5 minutes via the {{ill|Nagasaki Prefectural and Saga Prefectural Route 1 Sasebo-Ureshino Line|ja|長崎県道・佐賀県道1号佐世保嬉野線|qq=draft|qq=draft}} from the Ureshino Interchange on the {{ill|Nagasaki Expressway|ja|長崎自動車道|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == References == == Related Literature == *{{Cite book
