{{infobox Onsen |Name = Ureshino Onsen |image = Ureshino onsen.jpg |Comment = |Location = {{ill|Saga Prefecture|ja|佐賀県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Ureshino Town|ja|嬉野町 (佐賀県)|lt=Ureshino Town|lt_ja=嬉野町|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |Access = Railway : {{ill|Sasebo Line|ja|佐世保線|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Takeo Onsen Station|ja|武雄温泉駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} via {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|qq=draft|qq=draft}} for about 30 minutes
West Kyushu Shinkansen Ureshino Onsen Station
''For other access methods, see [[#アクセス|Access]]'' |Water Type = {{ill|Chloride Hot Spring|ja|塩化物泉|1=Brine spring|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |Temperature = |Discharge = |pH =7.8 |Liquid Classification = |Osmotic Pressure Classification = |Number of Accommodations = |Total Capacity = |Annual Bath Visitors = |Statistical Year = |External links = [https://spa-u.net/ Ureshino Onsen Tourism Association] |Special Notes = }} '''Ureshino Onsen''' (嬉野温泉) is a {{ill|Hot Spring|ja|温泉|1=Onsen|1=Onsen|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Saga Prefecture|ja|佐賀県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Ureshino Town|ja|嬉野町 (佐賀県)|lt=Ureshino Town|lt_ja=嬉野町|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (formerly part of {{ill|Hizen Province|ja|肥前国|qq=draft|qq=draft}}). Along with {{ill|Takeo Onsen|ja|武雄温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it is one of the representative hot springs of the prefecture. It has been selected as one of {{ill|Japan's 100 Views|ja|日本百景|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and is trademarked by Ureshino City under the names “Japan’s Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs Ureshino Onsen” and “Saga–Ureshino Onsen.” == Water Type == * Sodium – Bicarbonate Salt / Chloride Hot Spring It is a baking soda spring renowned for its beauty-enhancing properties, leaving the skin exceptionally smooth after a {{ill|Bathing|ja|入浴|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Its water quality was chosen by {{ill|Satoshi Fujita|ja|藤田聡|qq=draft|qq=draft}} as one of the {{ill|Japan's Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs|ja|日本三大美肌の湯|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (the other two being {{ill|Hinokami Onsen|ja|斐乃上温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Kirekawa Onsen|ja|喜連川温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft}}). == Onsen Town == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Siebold-no-yu.jpg|thumb|300px|{{Center|Siebold's Bath (シーボルトの湯)}} ]] This hot spring area, which rises in the heart of the town, is one of the largest onsen towns in Kyushu. Nearly 50 {{ill|Ryokan|ja|旅館|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – both large and small – line the streets along the banks of the {{ill|Shioda River|ja|塩田川 (佐賀県)|lt=Shioda River|lt_ja=塩田川|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ureshino River|ja|嬉野川|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), including Wataya Villa, where {{ill|Emperor Shōwa|ja|昭和天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}} stayed during the 38th {{ill|National Tree Planting Festival|ja|全国植樹祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} held in Saga Prefecture in 1987 (Showa 62). In addition, the oldest inn in Ureshino is said to be {{ill|Omuraya|ja|大村屋|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, founded in 1830 (the first year of the Tenpō era). In the center of the shopping district’s footbath plaza, there is “{{ill|Siebold|ja|フィリップ・フランツ・フォン・シーボルト|lt=Siebold|lt_ja=シーボルト|qq=draft|qq=draft}}’s Foot Bath,” which is available free of charge. Nearby stands the wooden, two-story (partly three-story) with one basement {{ill|Public Bath|ja|公衆浴場|1=public bathing|lt=Public Bathhouse|qq=draft|qq=draft}} “Furuyu Onsen,” constructed in 1924 (Taishō 13) to a design by a {{ill|German|ja|ドイツ人|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Although by around 2001 its interior and piping had deteriorated, the building’s exterior remained in nearly excellent condition{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀県の近代化遺産-佐賀県近代化遺産（建造物等）総合調査報告書-|year=2002|publisher=佐賀県教育委員会|page=182|series=佐賀県文化財調査報告書第153集}}. However, it was demolished on March 20, 2005 (Heisei 17) due to damage from the {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture Western Offshore Earthquake|ja|福岡県西方沖地震|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Later, in response to local demand, it was reconstructed to replicate its Taishō-era appearance and reopened on April 1, 2010 (Heisei 22) under the new name “Siebold’s Bath”{{Cite web |title=＜重点報道＠嬉野市＞わがまち今昔 シーボルトの湯 {{!}} まちの話題 {{!}} 佐賀新聞ニュース |url=https://www.saga-s.co.jp/articles/-/1114588 |website=佐賀新聞 |date=2024-04-09 |access-date=2024-04-09 |language=ja}}. Also known as the “Hot Spring for Beautiful Skin,” Ureshino Onsen is suitable for drinking. Its signature dish, the hot spring {{ill|Hot Spring Tofu|ja|湯豆腐|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, prepared using the onsen water, is a renowned specialty of Ureshino. In Ureshino City the product is written as “Yudōfu,” and the name “Ureshino Onsen Yudōfu” is trademarked by the city. == History == [[File:Ureshino Onsen 01.jpg|thumb|280px|{{Center|Onsen Town|1=Spa Town|lt=Onsen Town}} ]] Ureshino Onsen first appears in historical records in the ''Hizen Province Fudoki'' ({{ill|Hizen Province Fudoki|ja|肥前国風土記|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), compiled during the Nara period, with a description as a “hot spring that cures the ailments of all people,” although its name is not mentioned嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、272頁. According to legend, {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后|qq=draft|qq=draft}} discovered the hot spring on her return from the {{ill|Conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea|ja|三韓征伐|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and, while soothing her soldiers’ fatigue, exclaimed something akin to “How delightful!”—a remark that was later associated with the naming of “Ureshino.” Other legends tell of either Prince Takaso (from the ''Daidōji Kyuuki'') or an old woman (from the legend of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) exclaiming “ureshi.” These tales, however, were retroactively linked after the name “Ureshino” (originally read “ureshino”) was established, and the exclamation is not considered directly connected to the place name. In fact, the term “ureshino” is first confirmed in historical documents during the Kamakura period, when it was written as “宇礼志野”嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、351～353頁. The origin of the name is attributed to a field located in the upper reaches of the Shioda River; because the word “末” (ure) means “tip” or “end,” the area was called “Sueshino” and later a kanji was assigned to form the name{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀地名うんちく事典|year=2005|publisher=佐賀新聞社|page=93}}. After a period with few records concerning the hot spring, by the late Sengoku period (1570s) records emerge of {{ill|Ryūzōji Takanobu|ja|龍造寺隆信|qq=draft|qq=draft}} recommending hot spring therapy in Ureshino嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、710頁. During the {{ill|Edo Period|ja|江戸時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Ureshino Onsen flourished as Ureshino-juku, a {{ill|Post Town|ja|宿場町|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|Nagasaki Kaidō|ja|長崎街道|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In 1656 (Meireki 2), during the time of the first lord of the {{ill|Hasuike Domain|ja|蓮池藩|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Nabeshima Naotoshi, management of the spring source – previously under the jurisdiction of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – was transferred to the domain, and a roof was added to the open-air bath, converting it into a domain-run bathhouse. The post town was frequented by many travelers, and the state of Ureshino Onsen was recorded in works such as ''Wakan Sansai Zue'' and ''Edo Travelogue''. It appears that from this period it also became known as an entertainment hot spring. After World War II, Ureshino Onsen gained fame as an entertainment hot spring comparable to {{ill|Beppu Onsen|ja|別府温泉|lt=Beppu|lt_ja=別府|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the west. However, each onsen inn has its own distinctive style and character, and while many events are held, comparatively few new facilities have been introduced. In the former Ureshino Town (now part of {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) tea has been cultivated for generations. For this reason, Ureshino City and its tourism association actively promote the area as '''"Hot Spring Land of Tea and Tofu"''', and various initiatives have been undertaken to link the two. In addition, a 2D character themed on hot springs, “Ureshino Rokka” (from {{ill|Onsen Musume|ja|温泉むすめ|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), is used to promote the hot springs{{Cite web |url=https://onsen-musume.jp/character/ureshino_rikka |title=嬉野 六香 |access-date=2024-09-22 |publisher=株式会社エンバウンド |website=温泉むすめ公式サイト}}. == Access == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Tofu.jpg|thumb|190px|{{Center|A Famous Specialty from the Edo Period
'Hot Spring Tofu'}} ]] * Railway (access from {{ill|JR Kyushu|ja|九州旅客鉄道|lt=JR Kyushu|lt_ja=JR九州|qq=draft|qq=draft}} stations) ** About 13 minutes by {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|qq=draft|qq=draft}} from {{ill|Ureshino Onsen Station|ja|嬉野温泉駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|West Kyushu Shinkansen|ja|西九州新幹線|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. ** About 30 minutes by {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|qq=draft|qq=draft}} from {{ill|Takeo Onsen Station|ja|武雄温泉駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|Sasebo Line|ja|佐世保線|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. ** About 1 hour by {{ill|Nishi-Hii Bus|ja|西肥自動車|lt=Nishi-Hii Bus|lt_ja=西肥バス|qq=draft|qq=draft}} from {{ill|Sasebo Station|ja|佐世保駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the Sasebo Line. ** About 30 minutes by {{ill|Yūtoku Bus|ja|祐徳自動車|lt=Yūtoku Bus|lt_ja=祐徳バス|qq=draft|qq=draft}} from {{ill|Hizen Kashima Station|ja|肥前鹿島駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|Nagasaki Main Line|ja|長崎本線|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. ** About 25 minutes by {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|qq=draft|qq=draft}} from {{ill|Karinoki Station|ja|彼杵駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|Omura Line|ja|大村線|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. * Highway Bus *: Use the “{{ill|Kyushu-go|ja|九州号|qq=draft|qq=draft}}” operated by {{ill|Kyushu Express Bus|ja|九州急行バス|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In recent years, the latter has far more frequent service – while the former runs only 4 times a day, the latter operates roughly every 30 minutes. ** About 2 hours from {{ill|Fukuoka City|ja|福岡市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (via {{ill|Hakata Bus Terminal|ja|博多バスターミナル|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Nishitetsu Tenjin Express Bus Terminal|ja|西鉄天神高速バスターミナル|qq=draft|qq=draft}}). ** About 1 hour from {{ill|Nagasaki City|ja|長崎市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (from {{ill|Nagasaki Station|ja|長崎駅|lt=Nagasaki Station Front|lt_ja=長崎駅前|qq=draft|qq=draft}}). * Shared Taxi from the Airport *: With the opening of {{ill|Saga Airport|ja|佐賀空港|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, local taxi companies began operating services. The travel time from Saga Airport is approximately 1 hour. * Private Car *: 5 minutes via the {{ill|Nagasaki Prefectural and Saga Prefectural Route 1 Sasebo-Ureshino West Kyushu Shinkansen Ureshino Onsen Station
''For other access methods, see [[#アクセス|Access]]'' |Water Type = {{ill|Chloride Hot Spring|ja|塩化物泉|1=Brine spring|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chloride Hot Spring|13=User:Immanuelle/Brine spring|qq=}} |Temperature = |Discharge = |pH =7.8 |Liquid Classification = |Osmotic Pressure Classification = |Number of Accommodations = |Total Capacity = |Annual Bath Visitors = |Statistical Year = |External links = [https://spa-u.net/ Ureshino Onsen Tourism Association] |Special Notes = }} '''Ureshino Onsen''' (嬉野温泉) is a {{ill|Hot Spring|ja|温泉|1=Onsen|1=Onsen|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hot Spring|13=User:Immanuelle/Onsen|qq=}} located in {{ill|Saga Prefecture|ja|佐賀県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saga Prefecture|qq=}}, {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ureshino City|qq=}}, and {{ill|Ureshino Town|ja|嬉野町 (佐賀県)|lt=Ureshino Town|lt_ja=嬉野町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ureshino Town|qq=}} (formerly part of {{ill|Hizen Province|ja|肥前国|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hizen Province|qq=}}). Along with {{ill|Takeo Onsen|ja|武雄温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeo Onsen|qq=}}, it is one of the representative hot springs of the prefecture. It has been selected as one of {{ill|Japan's 100 Views|ja|日本百景|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan's 100 Views|qq=}} and is trademarked by Ureshino City under the names “Japan’s Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs Ureshino Onsen” and “Saga–Ureshino Onsen.” == Water Type == * Sodium – Bicarbonate Salt / Chloride Hot Spring It is a baking soda spring renowned for its beauty-enhancing properties, leaving the skin exceptionally smooth after a {{ill|Bathing|ja|入浴|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bathing|qq=}}. Its water quality was chosen by {{ill|Satoshi Fujita|ja|藤田聡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Satoshi Fujita|qq=}} as one of the {{ill|Japan's Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs|ja|日本三大美肌の湯|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan's Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs|qq=}} (the other two being {{ill|Hinokami Onsen|ja|斐乃上温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hinokami Onsen|qq=}} and {{ill|Kirekawa Onsen|ja|喜連川温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kirekawa Onsen|qq=}}). == Onsen Town == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Siebold-no-yu.jpg|thumb|300px|{{Center|Siebold's Bath (シーボルトの湯)}} ]] This hot spring area, which rises in the heart of the town, is one of the largest onsen towns in Kyushu. Nearly 50 {{ill|Ryokan|ja|旅館|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryokan|qq=}} – both large and small – line the streets along the banks of the {{ill|Shioda River|ja|塩田川 (佐賀県)|lt=Shioda River|lt_ja=塩田川|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shioda River|qq=}} (also known as {{ill|Ureshino River|ja|嬉野川|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ureshino River|qq=}}), including Wataya Villa, where {{ill|Emperor Shōwa|ja|昭和天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Shōwa|qq=}} stayed during the 38th {{ill|National Tree Planting Festival|ja|全国植樹祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Tree Planting Festival|qq=}} held in Saga Prefecture in 1987 (Showa 62). In addition, the oldest inn in Ureshino is said to be {{ill|Omuraya|ja|大村屋|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omuraya|qq=}}, founded in 1830 (the first year of the Tenpō era). In the center of the shopping district’s footbath plaza, there is “{{ill|Siebold|ja|フィリップ・フランツ・フォン・シーボルト|lt=Siebold|lt_ja=シーボルト|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Siebold|qq=}}’s Foot Bath,” which is available free of charge. Nearby stands the wooden, two-story (partly three-story) with one basement {{ill|Public Bath|ja|公衆浴場|1=public bathing|lt=Public Bathhouse|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Public Bath|13=User:Immanuelle/public bathing|qq=}} “Furuyu Onsen,” constructed in 1924 (Taishō 13) to a design by a {{ill|German|ja|ドイツ人|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/German|qq=}}. Although by around 2001 its interior and piping had deteriorated, the building’s exterior remained in nearly excellent condition{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀県の近代化遺産-佐賀県近代化遺産（建造物等）総合調査報告書-|year=2002|publisher=佐賀県教育委員会|page=182|series=佐賀県文化財調査報告書第153集}}. However, it was demolished on March 20, 2005 (Heisei 17) due to damage from the {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture Western Offshore Earthquake|ja|福岡県西方沖地震|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukuoka Prefecture Western Offshore Earthquake|qq=}}. Later, in response to local demand, it was reconstructed to replicate its Taishō-era appearance and reopened on April 1, 2010 (Heisei 22) under the new name “Siebold’s Bath”{{Cite web |title=＜重点報道＠嬉野市＞わがまち今昔 シーボルトの湯 {{!}} まちの話題 {{!}} 佐賀新聞ニュース |url=https://www.saga-s.co.jp/articles/-/1114588 |website=佐賀新聞 |date=2024-04-09 |access-date=2024-04-09 |language=ja}}. Also known as the “Hot Spring for Beautiful Skin,” Ureshino Onsen is suitable for drinking. Its signature dish, the hot spring {{ill|Hot Spring Tofu|ja|湯豆腐|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hot Spring Tofu|qq=}}, prepared using the onsen water, is a renowned specialty of Ureshino. In Ureshino City the product is written as “Yudōfu,” and the name “Ureshino Onsen Yudōfu” is trademarked by the city. == History == [[File:Ureshino Onsen 01.jpg|thumb|280px|{{Center|Onsen Town|1=Spa Town|lt=Onsen Town}} ]] Ureshino Onsen first appears in historical records in the ''Hizen Province Fudoki'' ({{ill|Hizen Province Fudoki|ja|肥前国風土記|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hizen Province Fudoki|qq=}}), compiled during the Nara period, with a description as a “hot spring that cures the ailments of all people,” although its name is not mentioned嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、272頁. According to legend, {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Empress Jingū|qq=}} discovered the hot spring on her return from the {{ill|Conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea|ja|三韓征伐|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea|qq=}} and, while soothing her soldiers’ fatigue, exclaimed something akin to “How delightful!”—a remark that was later associated with the naming of “Ureshino.” Other legends tell of either Prince Takaso (from the ''Daidōji Kyuuki'') or an old woman (from the legend of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyotamahime Shrine|qq=}}) exclaiming “ureshi.” These tales, however, were retroactively linked after the name “Ureshino” (originally read “ureshino”) was established, and the exclamation is not considered directly connected to the place name. In fact, the term “ureshino” is first confirmed in historical documents during the Kamakura period, when it was written as “宇礼志野”嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、351～353頁. The origin of the name is attributed to a field located in the upper reaches of the Shioda River; because the word “末” (ure) means “tip” or “end,” the area was called “Sueshino” and later a kanji was assigned to form the name{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀地名うんちく事典|year=2005|publisher=佐賀新聞社|page=93}}. After a period with few records concerning the hot spring, by the late Sengoku period (1570s) records emerge of {{ill|Ryūzōji Takanobu|ja|龍造寺隆信|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryūzōji Takanobu|qq=}} recommending hot spring therapy in Ureshino嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、710頁. During the {{ill|Edo Period|ja|江戸時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Edo Period|qq=}}, Ureshino Onsen flourished as Ureshino-juku, a {{ill|Post Town|ja|宿場町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Post Town|qq=}} on the {{ill|Nagasaki Kaidō|ja|長崎街道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagasaki Kaidō|qq=}}. In 1656 (Meireki 2), during the time of the first lord of the {{ill|Hasuike Domain|ja|蓮池藩|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hasuike Domain|qq=}}, Nabeshima Naotoshi, management of the spring source – previously under the jurisdiction of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyotamahime Shrine|qq=}} – was transferred to the domain, and a roof was added to the open-air bath, converting it into a domain-run bathhouse. The post town was frequented by many travelers, and the state of Ureshino Onsen was recorded in works such as ''Wakan Sansai Zue'' and ''Edo Travelogue''. It appears that from this period it also became known as an entertainment hot spring. After World War II, Ureshino Onsen gained fame as an entertainment hot spring comparable to {{ill|Beppu Onsen|ja|別府温泉|lt=Beppu|lt_ja=別府|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Beppu Onsen|qq=}} in the west. However, each onsen inn has its own distinctive style and character, and while many events are held, comparatively few new facilities have been introduced. In the former Ureshino Town (now part of {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ureshino City|qq=}}) tea has been cultivated for generations. For this reason, Ureshino City and its tourism association actively promote the area as '''"Hot Spring Land of Tea and Tofu"''', and various initiatives have been undertaken to link the two. In addition, a 2D character themed on hot springs, “Ureshino Rokka” (from {{ill|Onsen Musume|ja|温泉むすめ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onsen Musume|qq=}}), is used to promote the hot springs{{Cite web |url=https://onsen-musume.jp/character/ureshino_rikka |title=嬉野 六香 |access-date=2024-09-22 |publisher=株式会社エンバウンド |website=温泉むすめ公式サイト}}. == Access == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Tofu.jpg|thumb|190px|{{Center|A Famous Specialty from the Edo Period
'Hot Spring Tofu'}} ]] * Railway (access from {{ill|JR Kyushu|ja|九州旅客鉄道|lt=JR Kyushu|lt_ja=JR九州|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR Kyushu|qq=}} stations) ** About 13 minutes by {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR Kyushu Bus|qq=}} from {{ill|Ureshino Onsen Station|ja|嬉野温泉駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ureshino Onsen Station|qq=}} on the {{ill|West Kyushu Shinkansen|ja|西九州新幹線|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/West Kyushu Shinkansen|qq=}}. ** About 30 minutes by {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR Kyushu Bus|qq=}} from {{ill|Takeo Onsen Station|ja|武雄温泉駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeo Onsen Station|qq=}} on the {{ill|Sasebo Line|ja|佐世保線|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sasebo Line|qq=}}. ** About 1 hour by {{ill|Nishi-Hii Bus|ja|西肥自動車|lt=Nishi-Hii Line. ** About 30 minutes by {{ill|Yūtoku Bus|ja|祐徳自動車|lt=Yūtoku Bus|lt_ja=祐徳バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yūtoku Bus|qq=}} from {{ill|Hizen Kashima Station|ja|肥前鹿島駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hizen Kashima Station|qq=}} on the {{ill|Nagasaki Main Line|ja|長崎本線|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagasaki Main Line|qq=}}. ** About 25 minutes by {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR Kyushu Bus|qq=}} from {{ill|Karinoki Station|ja|彼杵駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Karinoki Station|qq=}} on the {{ill|Omura Line|ja|大村線|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omura Line|qq=}}. * Highway Bus *: Use the “{{ill|Kyushu-go|ja|九州号|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyushu-go|qq=}}” operated by {{ill|Kyushu Express Bus|ja|九州急行バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyushu Express Bus|qq=}}. There are services that stop at the Ureshino Bus Center ({{ill|National Route 34|ja|国道34号|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Route 34|qq=}}) in the hot spring town and services that stop only at the {{ill|Ureshino Interchange|ja|嬉野インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ureshino Interchange|qq=}} on the {{ill|Nagasaki Expressway|ja|長崎自動車道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagasaki Expressway|qq=}}. In recent years, the latter has far more frequent service – while the former runs only 4 times a day, the latter operates roughly every 30 minutes. ** About 2 hours from {{ill|Fukuoka City|ja|福岡市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukuoka City|qq=}} (via {{ill|Hakata Bus Terminal|ja|博多バスターミナル|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakata Bus Terminal|qq=}} and {{ill|Nishitetsu Tenjin Express Bus Terminal|ja|西鉄天神高速バスターミナル|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitetsu Tenjin Express Bus Terminal|qq=}}). ** About 1 hour from {{ill|Nagasaki City|ja|長崎市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagasaki City|qq=}} (from {{ill|Nagasaki Station|ja|長崎駅|lt=Nagasaki Station Front|lt_ja=長崎駅前|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagasaki Station|qq=}}). * Shared Taxi from the Airport *: With the opening of {{ill|Saga Airport|ja|佐賀空港|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saga Airport|qq=}}, local taxi companies began operating services. The travel time from Saga Airport is approximately 1 hour. * Private Car *: 5 minutes via the {{ill|Nagasaki Prefectural and Saga Prefectural Route 1 Sasebo-Ureshino Line|ja|長崎県道・佐賀県道1号佐世保嬉野線|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagasaki Prefectural and Saga Prefectural Route 1 Sasebo-Ureshino Line|qq=}} from the Ureshino Interchange on the West Kyushu Shinkansen Ureshino Onsen Station
''For other access methods, see [[#アクセス|Access]]'' |Water Type = {{ill|Chloride Hot Spring|ja|塩化物泉|1=Brine spring|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chloride Hot Spring|13=User:Immanuelle/Brine spring|qq=}} |Temperature = |Discharge = |pH =7.8 |Liquid Classification = |Osmotic Pressure Classification = |Number of Accommodations = |Total Capacity = |Annual Bath Visitors = |Statistical Year = |External links = [https://spa-u.net/ Ureshino Onsen Tourism Association] |Special Notes = }} '''Ureshino Onsen''' (嬉野温泉) is a {{ill|Hot Spring|ja|温泉|1=Onsen|1=Onsen|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hot Spring|13=User:Immanuelle/Onsen|qq=}} located in {{ill|Saga Prefecture|ja|佐賀県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saga Prefecture|qq=}}, {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ureshino City|qq=}}, and {{ill|Ureshino Town|ja|嬉野町 (佐賀県)|lt=Ureshino Town|lt_ja=嬉野町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ureshino Town|qq=}} (formerly part of {{ill|Hizen Province|ja|肥前国|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hizen Province|qq=}}). Along with {{ill|Takeo Onsen|ja|武雄温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeo Onsen|qq=}}, it is one of the representative hot springs of the prefecture. It has been selected as one of {{ill|Japan's 100 Views|ja|日本百景|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan's 100 Views|qq=}} and is trademarked by Ureshino City under the names “Japan’s Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs Ureshino Onsen” and “Saga–Ureshino Onsen.” == Water Type == * Sodium – Bicarbonate Salt / Chloride Hot Spring It is a baking soda spring renowned for its beauty-enhancing properties, leaving the skin exceptionally smooth after a {{ill|Bathing|ja|入浴|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bathing|qq=}}. Its water quality was chosen by {{ill|Satoshi Fujita|ja|藤田聡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Satoshi Fujita|qq=}} as one of the {{ill|Japan's Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs|ja|日本三大美肌の湯|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan's Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs|qq=}} (the other two being {{ill|Hinokami Onsen|ja|斐乃上温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hinokami Onsen|qq=}} and {{ill|Kirekawa Onsen|ja|喜連川温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kirekawa Onsen|qq=}}). == Onsen Town == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Siebold-no-yu.jpg|thumb|300px|{{Center|Siebold's Bath (シーボルトの湯)}} ]] This hot spring area, which rises in the heart of the town, is one of the largest onsen towns in Kyushu. Nearly 50 {{ill|Ryokan|ja|旅館|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryokan|qq=}} – both large and small – line the streets along the banks of the {{ill|Shioda River|ja|塩田川 (佐賀県)|lt=Shioda River|lt_ja=塩田川|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shioda River|qq=}} (also known as {{ill|Ureshino River|ja|嬉野川|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ureshino River|qq=}}), including Wataya Villa, where {{ill|Emperor Shōwa|ja|昭和天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Shōwa|qq=}} stayed during the 38th {{ill|National Tree Planting Festival|ja|全国植樹祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Tree Planting Festival|qq=}} held in Saga Prefecture in 1987 (Showa 62). In addition, the oldest inn in Ureshino is said to be {{ill|Omuraya|ja|大村屋|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omuraya|qq=}}, founded in 1830 (the first year of the Tenpō era). In the center of the shopping district’s footbath plaza, there is “{{ill|Siebold|ja|フィリップ・フランツ・フォン・シーボルト|lt=Siebold|lt_ja=シーボルト|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Siebold|qq=}}’s Foot Bath,” which is available free of charge. Nearby stands the wooden, two-story (partly three-story) with one basement {{ill|Public Bath|ja|公衆浴場|1=public bathing|lt=Public Bathhouse|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Public Bath|13=User:Immanuelle/public bathing|qq=}} “Furuyu Onsen,” constructed in 1924 (Taishō 13) to a design by a {{ill|German|ja|ドイツ人|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/German|qq=}}. Although by around 2001 its interior and piping had deteriorated, the building’s exterior remained in nearly excellent condition{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀県の近代化遺産-佐賀県近代化遺産（建造物等）総合調査報告書-|year=2002|publisher=佐賀県教育委員会|page=182|series=佐賀県文化財調査報告書第153集}}. However, it was demolished on March 20, 2005 (Heisei 17) due to damage from the {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture Western Offshore Earthquake|ja|福岡県西方沖地震|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukuoka Prefecture Western Offshore Earthquake|qq=}}. Later, in response to local demand, it was reconstructed to replicate its Taishō-era appearance and reopened on April 1, 2010 (Heisei 22) under the new name “Siebold’s Bath”{{Cite web |title=＜重点報道＠嬉野市＞わがまち今昔 シーボルトの湯 {{!}} まちの話題 {{!}} 佐賀新聞ニュース |url=https://www.saga-s.co.jp/articles/-/1114588 |website=佐賀新聞 |date=2024-04-09 |access-date=2024-04-09 |language=ja}}. Also known as the “Hot Spring for Beautiful Skin,” Ureshino Onsen is suitable for drinking. Its signature dish, the hot spring {{ill|Hot Spring Tofu|ja|湯豆腐|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hot Spring Tofu|qq=}}, prepared using the onsen water, is a renowned specialty of Ureshino. In Ureshino City the product is written as “Yudōfu,” and the name “Ureshino Onsen Yudōfu” is trademarked by the city. == History == [[File:Ureshino Onsen 01.jpg|thumb|280px|{{Center|Onsen Town|1=Spa Town|lt=Onsen Town}} ]] Ureshino Onsen first appears in historical records in the ''Hizen Province Fudoki'' ({{ill|Hizen Province Fudoki|ja|肥前国風土記|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hizen Province Fudoki|qq=}}), compiled during the Nara period, with a description as a “hot spring that cures the ailments of all people,” although its name is not mentioned嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、272頁. According to legend, {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Empress Jingū|qq=}} discovered the hot spring on her return from the {{ill|Conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea|ja|三韓征伐|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea|qq=}} and, while soothing her soldiers’ fatigue, exclaimed something akin to “How delightful!”—a remark that was later associated with the naming of “Ureshino.” Other legends tell of either Prince Takaso (from the ''Daidōji Kyuuki'') or an old woman (from the legend of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyotamahime Shrine|qq=}}) exclaiming “ureshi.” These tales, however, were retroactively linked after the name “Ureshino” (originally read “ureshino”) was established, and the exclamation is not considered directly connected to the place name. In fact, the term “ureshino” is first confirmed in historical documents during the Kamakura period, when it was written as “宇礼志野”嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、351～353頁. The origin of the name is attributed to a field located in the upper reaches of the Shioda River; because the word “末” (ure) means “tip” or “end,” the area was called “Sueshino” and later a kanji was assigned to form the name{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀地名うんちく事典|year=2005|publisher=佐賀新聞社|page=93}}. After a period with few records concerning the hot spring, by the late Sengoku period (1570s) records emerge of {{ill|Ryūzōji Takanobu|ja|龍造寺隆信|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryūzōji Takanobu|qq=}} recommending hot spring therapy in Ureshino嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、710頁. During the {{ill|Edo Period|ja|江戸時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Edo Period|qq=}}, Ureshino Onsen flourished as Ureshino-juku, a {{ill|Post Town|ja|宿場町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Post Town|qq=}} on the {{ill|Nagasaki Kaidō|ja|長崎街道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagasaki Kaidō|qq=}}. In 1656 (Meireki 2), during the time of the first lord of the {{ill|Hasuike Domain|ja|蓮池藩|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hasuike Domain|qq=}}, Nabeshima Naotoshi, management of the spring source – previously under the jurisdiction of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyotamahime Shrine|qq=}} – was transferred to the domain, and a roof was added to the open-air bath, converting it into a domain-run bathhouse. The post town was frequented by many travelers, and the state of Ureshino Onsen was recorded in works such as ''Wakan Sansai Zue'' and ''Edo Travelogue''. It appears that from this period it also became known as an entertainment hot spring. After World War II, Ureshino Onsen gained fame as an entertainment hot spring comparable to {{ill|Beppu Onsen|ja|別府温泉|lt=Beppu|lt_ja=別府|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Beppu Onsen|qq=}} in the west. However, each onsen inn has its own distinctive style and character, and while many events are held, comparatively few new facilities have been introduced. In the former Ureshino Town (now part of {{ill|Ureshino City|ja|嬉野市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ureshino City|qq=}}) tea has been cultivated for generations. For this reason, Ureshino City and its tourism association actively promote the area as '''"Hot Spring Land of Tea and Tofu"''', and various initiatives have been undertaken to link the two. In addition, a 2D character themed on hot springs, “Ureshino Rokka” (from {{ill|Onsen Musume|ja|温泉むすめ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onsen Musume|qq=}}), is used to promote the hot springs{{Cite web |url=https://onsen-musume.jp/character/ureshino_rikka |title=嬉野 六香 |access-date=2024-09-22 |publisher=株式会社エンバウンド |website=温泉むすめ公式サイト}}. == Access == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Tofu.jpg|thumb|190px|{{Center|A Famous Specialty from the Edo Period
'Hot Spring Tofu'}} ]] * Railway (access from {{ill|JR Kyushu|ja|九州旅客鉄道|lt=JR Kyushu|lt_ja=JR九州|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR Kyushu|qq=}} stations) ** About 13 minutes by {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR Kyushu Bus|qq=}} from {{ill|Ureshino Onsen Station|ja|嬉野温泉駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ureshino Onsen Station|qq=}} on the {{ill|West Kyushu Shinkansen|ja|西九州新幹線|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/West Kyushu Shinkansen|qq=}}. ** About 30 minutes by {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR Kyushu Bus|qq=}} from {{ill|Takeo Onsen Station|ja|武雄温泉駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeo Onsen Station|qq=}} on the Use the “{{ill|Kyushu-go|ja|九州号|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyushu-go|qq=}}” operated by {{ill|Kyushu Express Bus|ja|九州急行バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyushu Express Bus|qq=}}. There are services that stop at the Ureshino Bus Center ({{ill|National Route 34|ja|国道34号|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Route 34|qq=}}) in the hot spring town and services that stop only at the {{ill|Ureshino Interchange|ja|嬉野インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ureshino Interchange|qq=}} on the {{ill|Nagasaki Expressway|ja|長崎自動車道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagasaki Expressway|qq=}}. In recent years, the latter has far more frequent service – while the former runs only 4 times a day, the latter operates roughly every 30 minutes. ** About 2 hours from {{ill|Fukuoka City|ja|福岡市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukuoka City|qq=}} (via {{ill|Hakata Bus Terminal|ja|博多バスターミナル|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakata Bus Terminal|qq=}} and {{ill|Nishitetsu Tenjin Express Bus Terminal|ja|西鉄天神高速バスターミナル|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitetsu Tenjin Express Bus Terminal|qq=}}). ** About 1 hour from {{ill|Nagasaki City|ja|長崎市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagasaki City|qq=}} (from {{ill|Nagasaki Station|ja|長崎駅|lt=Nagasaki Station Front|lt_ja=長崎駅前|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagasaki Station|qq=}}). * Shared Taxi from the Airport *: With the opening of {{ill|Saga Airport|ja|佐賀空港|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saga Airport|qq=}}, local taxi companies began operating services. The travel time from Saga Airport is approximately 1 hour. * Private Car *: 5 minutes via the {{ill|Nagasaki Prefectural and Saga Prefectural Route 1 Sasebo-Ureshino West Kyushu Shinkansen Ureshino Onsen Station
''For other access methods, see [[#アクセス|Access]]'' |Water Type = [[:en:Brine spring|Brine spring]] |Temperature = |Discharge = |pH =7.8 |Liquid Classification = |Osmotic Pressure Classification = |Number of Accommodations = |Total Capacity = |Annual Bath Visitors = |Statistical Year = |External links = [https://spa-u.net/ Ureshino Onsen Tourism Association] |Special Notes = }} '''Ureshino Onsen''' (嬉野温泉) is a [[:en:Onsen|Onsen]] located in [[:en:Saga Prefecture|Saga Prefecture]], [[:en:Ureshino, Saga|Ureshino City]], and {{ill|Ureshino Town|ja|嬉野町 (佐賀県)|lt=Ureshino Town|lt_ja=嬉野町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ureshino Town|qq=}} (formerly part of [[:en:Hizen Province|Hizen Province]]). Along with {{ill|Takeo Onsen|ja|武雄温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeo Onsen|qq=}}, it is one of the representative hot springs of the prefecture. It has been selected as one of [[:en:100 Landscapes of Japan (Shōwa era)|Japan's 100 Views]] and is trademarked by Ureshino City under the names “Japan’s Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs Ureshino Onsen” and “Saga–Ureshino Onsen.” == Water Type == * Sodium – Bicarbonate Salt / Chloride Hot Spring It is a baking soda spring renowned for its beauty-enhancing properties, leaving the skin exceptionally smooth after a [[:en:Bathing|Bathing]]. Its water quality was chosen by {{ill|Satoshi Fujita|ja|藤田聡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Satoshi Fujita|qq=}} as one of the {{ill|Japan's Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs|ja|日本三大美肌の湯|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan's Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs|qq=}} (the other two being {{ill|Hinokami Onsen|ja|斐乃上温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hinokami Onsen|qq=}} and {{ill|Kirekawa Onsen|ja|喜連川温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kirekawa Onsen|qq=}}). == Onsen Town == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Siebold-no-yu.jpg|thumb|300px|{{Center|Siebold's Bath (シーボルトの湯)}} ]] This hot spring area, which rises in the heart of the town, is one of the largest onsen towns in Kyushu. Nearly 50 [[:en:Ryokan|Ryokan]] – both large and small – line the streets along the banks of the {{ill|Shioda River|ja|塩田川 (佐賀県)|lt=Shioda River|lt_ja=塩田川|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shioda River|qq=}} (also known as {{ill|Ureshino River|ja|嬉野川|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ureshino River|qq=}}), including Wataya Villa, where [[:en:Hirohito|Emperor Shōwa]] stayed during the 38th {{ill|National Tree Planting Festival|ja|全国植樹祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Tree Planting Festival|qq=}} held in Saga Prefecture in 1987 (Showa 62). In addition, the oldest inn in Ureshino is said to be {{ill|Omuraya|ja|大村屋|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omuraya|qq=}}, founded in 1830 (the first year of the Tenpō era). In the center of the shopping district’s footbath plaza, there is “[[:en:Philipp Franz von Siebold|Siebold]]’s Foot Bath,” which is available free of charge. Nearby stands the wooden, two-story (partly three-story) with one basement [[:en:Public bathing|Public Bathhouse]] “Furuyu Onsen,” constructed in 1924 (Taishō 13) to a design by a [[:en:Germans|German]]. Although by around 2001 its interior and piping had deteriorated, the building’s exterior remained in nearly excellent condition{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀県の近代化遺産-佐賀県近代化遺産（建造物等）総合調査報告書-|year=2002|publisher=佐賀県教育委員会|page=182|series=佐賀県文化財調査報告書第153集}}. However, it was demolished on March 20, 2005 (Heisei 17) due to damage from the [[:en:2005 Fukuoka earthquake|Fukuoka Prefecture Western Offshore Earthquake]]. Later, in response to local demand, it was reconstructed to replicate its Taishō-era appearance and reopened on April 1, 2010 (Heisei 22) under the new name “Siebold’s Bath”{{Cite web |title=＜重点報道＠嬉野市＞わがまち今昔 シーボルトの湯 {{!}} まちの話題 {{!}} 佐賀新聞ニュース |url=https://www.saga-s.co.jp/articles/-/1114588 |website=佐賀新聞 |date=2024-04-09 |access-date=2024-04-09 |language=ja}}. Also known as the “Hot Spring for Beautiful Skin,” Ureshino Onsen is suitable for drinking. Its signature dish, the hot spring {{ill|Hot Spring Tofu|ja|湯豆腐|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hot Spring Tofu|qq=}}, prepared using the onsen water, is a renowned specialty of Ureshino. In Ureshino City the product is written as “Yudōfu,” and the name “Ureshino Onsen Yudōfu” is trademarked by the city. == History == [[File:Ureshino Onsen 01.jpg|thumb|280px|{{Center|Onsen Town|1=Spa Town|lt=Onsen Town}} ]] Ureshino Onsen first appears in historical records in the ''Hizen Province Fudoki'' ({{ill|Hizen Province Fudoki|ja|肥前国風土記|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hizen Province Fudoki|qq=}}), compiled during the Nara period, with a description as a “hot spring that cures the ailments of all people,” although its name is not mentioned嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、272頁. According to legend, [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]] discovered the hot spring on her return from the {{ill|Conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea|ja|三韓征伐|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea|qq=}} and, while soothing her soldiers’ fatigue, exclaimed something akin to “How delightful!”—a remark that was later associated with the naming of “Ureshino.” Other legends tell of either Prince Takaso (from the ''Daidōji Kyuuki'') or an old woman (from the legend of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyotamahime Shrine|qq=}}) exclaiming “ureshi.” These tales, however, were retroactively linked after the name “Ureshino” (originally read “ureshino”) was established, and the exclamation is not considered directly connected to the place name. In fact, the term “ureshino” is first confirmed in historical documents during the Kamakura period, when it was written as “宇礼志野”嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、351～353頁. The origin of the name is attributed to a field located in the upper reaches of the Shioda River; because the word “末” (ure) means “tip” or “end,” the area was called “Sueshino” and later a kanji was assigned to form the name{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀地名うんちく事典|year=2005|publisher=佐賀新聞社|page=93}}. After a period with few records concerning the hot spring, by the late Sengoku period (1570s) records emerge of [[:en:Ryūzōji Takanobu|Ryūzōji Takanobu]] recommending hot spring therapy in Ureshino嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、710頁. During the [[:en:Edo period|Edo Period]], Ureshino Onsen flourished as Ureshino-juku, a {{ill|Post Town|ja|宿場町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Post Town|qq=}} on the [[:en:Nagasaki Kaidō|Nagasaki Kaidō]]. In 1656 (Meireki 2), during the time of the first lord of the [[:en:Hasunoike Domain|Hasuike Domain]], Nabeshima Naotoshi, management of the spring source – previously under the jurisdiction of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyotamahime Shrine|qq=}} – was transferred to the domain, and a roof was added to the open-air bath, converting it into a domain-run bathhouse. The post town was frequented by many travelers, and the state of Ureshino Onsen was recorded in works such as ''Wakan Sansai Zue'' and ''Edo Travelogue''. It appears that from this period it also became known as an entertainment hot spring. After World War II, Ureshino Onsen gained fame as an entertainment hot spring comparable to [[:en:Beppu Onsen|Beppu]] in the west. However, each onsen inn has its own distinctive style and character, and while many events are held, comparatively few new facilities have been introduced. In the former Ureshino Town (now part of [[:en:Ureshino, Saga|Ureshino City]]) tea has been cultivated for generations. For this reason, Ureshino City and its tourism association actively promote the area as '''"Hot Spring Land of Tea and Tofu"''', and various initiatives have been undertaken to link the two. In addition, a 2D character themed on hot springs, “Ureshino Rokka” (from {{ill|Onsen Musume|ja|温泉むすめ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onsen Musume|qq=}}), is used to promote the hot springs{{Cite web |url=https://onsen-musume.jp/character/ureshino_rikka |title=嬉野 六香 |access-date=2024-09-22 |publisher=株式会社エンバウンド |website=温泉むすめ公式サイト}}. == Access == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Tofu.jpg|thumb|190px|{{Center|A Famous Specialty from the Edo Period
'Hot Spring Tofu'}} ]] * Railway (access from [[:en:Kyushu Railway Company|JR Kyushu]] stations) ** About 13 minutes by {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR Kyushu Bus|qq=}} from [[:en:Ureshino-Onsen Station|Ureshino Onsen Station]] on the [[:en:Nishi Kyushu Shinkansen|West Kyushu Shinkansen]]. ** About 30 minutes by {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR Kyushu Bus|qq=}} from [[:en:Takeo-Onsen Station|Takeo Onsen Station]] on the [[:en:Sasebo Line|Sasebo Line]]. ** About 1 hour by [[:en:Saihi Motor|Nishi-Hii Bus]] from [[:en:Sasebo Station|Sasebo Station]] on the Sasebo Line. ** About 30 minutes by {{ill|Yūtoku Bus|ja|祐徳自動車|lt=Yūtoku Bus|lt_ja=祐徳バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yūtoku Bus|qq=}} from [[:en:Hizen-Kashima Station|Hizen Kashima Station]] on the [[:en:Nagasaki Main Line|Nagasaki Main Line]]. ** About 25 minutes by {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR Kyushu Bus|qq=}} from [[:en:Sonogi Station|Karinoki Station]] on the [[:en:Ōmura Line|Omura Line]]. * Highway Bus *: Use the “{{ill|Kyushu-go|ja|九州号|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyushu-go|qq=}}” operated by {{ill|Kyushu Express Bus|ja|九州急行バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyushu Express Bus|qq=}}. There are services that stop at the Ureshino Bus Center ([[:en:Japan National Route 34|National Route 34]]) in the hot spring town and services that stop only at the {{ill|Ureshino Interchange|ja|嬉野インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ureshino Interchange|qq=}} on the [[:en:Nagasaki Expressway|Nagasaki Expressway]]. In recent years, the latter has far more frequent service – while the former runs only 4 times a day, the latter operates roughly every 30 minutes. ** About 2 hours from [[:en:Fukuoka|Fukuoka City]] (via {{ill|Hakata Bus Terminal|ja|博多バスターミナル|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakata Bus Terminal|qq=}} and {{ill|Nishitetsu Tenjin Express Bus Terminal|ja|西鉄天神高速バスターミナル|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitetsu Tenjin Express Bus Terminal|qq=}}). ** About 1 hour from [[:en:Nagasaki|Nagasaki City]] (from [[:en:Nagasaki Station|Nagasaki Station Front]]). * Shared Taxi from the Airport *: With the opening of [[:en:Saga Airport|Saga Airport]], local taxi companies began operating services. The travel time from Saga Airport is approximately 1 hour. * Private Car *: 5 minutes via the {{ill|Nagasaki Prefectural and Saga Prefectural Route 1 Sasebo-Ureshino Line|ja|長崎県道・佐賀県道1号佐世保嬉野線|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagasaki Prefectural and Saga Prefectural Route 1 Sasebo-Ureshino Line|qq=}} from the Ureshino Interchange on the [[:en:Nagasaki Expressway|Nagasaki Expressway]]. == References == == Related Literature == *{{Cite book |Language=Japanese |author=Masamichi Ikeda|year=1898|title=Ureshino Onsen Chronicles|id={{NDLJP|766546}}|quote= }} == See Also == {{commonscat|Ureshino Onsen}} * {{ill|Tourist Attractions in Saga Prefecture|ja|佐賀県の観光地|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tourist Attractions in Saga Prefecture|qq=}} * [[:en:Nishi Kyushu Shinkansen|West Kyushu Shinkansen]] * [[:en:Ureshino-Onsen Station|Ureshino Onsen Station]] * {{ill|Hizen Dream Road|ja|肥前夢街道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hizen Dream Road|qq=}} * {{ill|Wataya Villa|ja|和多屋別荘|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wataya Villa|qq=}} * {{ill|Irifune-sō|ja|入船荘|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Irifune-sō|qq=}} * [[:en:Types of prostitution in modern Japan|Soapland]] * [[:en:Yuki Yanagita|Yagita Yūki]] … (conducts self-training at Ureshino Onsen every year). * The townscape of {{ill|Shiodazu|ja|塩田津|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiodazu|qq=}} ({{ill|Important Preservation District for Groups of Traditional Buildings|ja|重要伝統的建造物群保存地区|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Preservation District for Groups of Traditional Buildings|qq=}}) … the post town following ''For other access methods, see [[#アクセス|Access]]'' |Water Type = [[:en:Brine spring|Brine spring]] |Temperature = |Discharge = |pH =7.8 |Liquid Classification = |Osmotic Pressure Classification = |Number of Accommodations = |Total Capacity = |Annual Bath Visitors = |Statistical Year = |External links = [https://spa-u.net/ Ureshino Onsen Tourism Association] |Special Notes = }} '''Ureshino Onsen''' (嬉野温泉) is a [[:en:Onsen|Onsen]] located in [[:en:Saga Prefecture|Saga Prefecture]], [[:en:Ureshino, Saga|Ureshino City]], and {{ill|Ureshino Town|ja|嬉野町 (佐賀県)|lt=Ureshino Town|lt_ja=嬉野町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ureshino Town|qq=}} (formerly part of [[:en:Hizen Province|Hizen Province]]). It has been selected as one of [[:en:100 Landscapes of Japan (Shōwa era)|Japan's 100 Views]] and is trademarked by Ureshino City under the names “Japan’s Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs Ureshino Onsen” and “Saga–Ureshino Onsen.” == Water Type == * Sodium – Bicarbonate Salt / Chloride Hot Spring It is a baking soda spring renowned for its beauty-enhancing properties, leaving the skin exceptionally smooth after a [[:en:Bathing|Bathing]]. 'Hot Spring Tofu'}} ]] * Railway (access from [[:en:Kyushu Railway Company|JR Kyushu]] stations) ** About 13 minutes by {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR Kyushu Bus|qq=}} from [[:en:Ureshino-Onsen Station|Ureshino Onsen Station]] on the [[:en:Nishi Kyushu Shinkansen|West Kyushu Shinkansen]]. ** About 30 minutes by {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR Kyushu Bus|qq=}} from [[:en:Takeo-Onsen Station|Takeo Onsen Station]] on the [[:en:Sasebo Line|Sasebo Line]]. ** About 1 hour by [[:en:Saihi Motor|Nishi-Hii Bus]] from [[:en:Sasebo Station|Sasebo Station]] on the Sasebo Line. ** About 30 minutes by {{ill|Yūtoku Bus|ja|祐徳自動車|lt=Yūtoku Bus|lt_ja=祐徳バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yūtoku Bus|qq=}} from [[:en:Hizen-Kashima Station|Hizen Kashima Station]] on the [[:en:Nagasaki Main Line|Nagasaki Main Line]]. ** About 25 minutes by {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR Kyushu Bus|qq=}} from [[:en:Sonogi Station|Karinoki Station]] on the [[:en:Ōmura Line|Omura Line]]. * Highway Bus *: Use the “{{ill|Kyushu-go|ja|九州号|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyushu-go|qq=}}” operated by {{ill|Kyushu Express Bus|ja|九州急行バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyushu Express Bus|qq=}}. {{infobox Onsen |Name = Ureshino Onsen |image = Ureshino onsen.jpg |Comment = |Location = [[:en:Saga Prefecture|Saga Prefecture]] [[:en:Ureshino, Saga|Ureshino City]] {{ill|Ureshino Town|ja|嬉野町 (佐賀県)|lt=Ureshino Town|lt_ja=嬉野町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ureshino Town|qq=}} |Access = Railway : [[:en:Sasebo Line|Sasebo Line]] [[:en:Takeo-Onsen Station|Takeo Onsen Station]] via {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR Kyushu Bus|qq=}} for about 30 minutes
West Kyushu Shinkansen Ureshino Onsen Station
''For other access methods, see [[#アクセス|Access]]'' |Water Type = [[:en:Brine spring|Brine spring]] |Temperature = |Discharge = |pH =7.8 |Liquid Classification = |Osmotic Pressure Classification = |Number of Accommodations = |Total Capacity = |Annual Bath Visitors = |Statistical Year = |External links = [https://spa-u.net/ Ureshino Onsen Tourism Association] |Special Notes = }} '''Ureshino Onsen''' (嬉野温泉) is a [[:en:Onsen|Onsen]] located in [[:en:Saga Prefecture|Saga Prefecture]], [[:en:Ureshino, Saga|Ureshino City]], and {{ill|Ureshino Town|ja|嬉野町 (佐賀県)|lt=Ureshino Town|lt_ja=嬉野町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ureshino Town|qq=}} (formerly part of [[:en:Hizen Province|Hizen Province]]). Along with {{ill|Takeo Onsen|ja|武雄温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeo Onsen|qq=}}, it is one of the representative hot springs of the prefecture. It has been selected as one of [[:en:100 Landscapes of Japan (Shōwa era)|Japan's 100 Views]] and is trademarked by Ureshino City under the names “Japan’s Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs Ureshino Onsen” and “Saga–Ureshino Onsen.” == Water Type == * Sodium – Bicarbonate Salt / Chloride Hot Spring It is a baking soda spring renowned for its beauty-enhancing properties, leaving the skin exceptionally smooth after a [[:en:Bathing|Bathing]]. Its water quality was chosen by {{ill|Satoshi Fujita|ja|藤田聡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Satoshi Fujita|qq=}} as one of the {{ill|Japan's Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs|ja|日本三大美肌の湯|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan's Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs|qq=}} (the other two being {{ill|Hinokami Onsen|ja|斐乃上温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hinokami Onsen|qq=}} and {{ill|Kirekawa Onsen|ja|喜連川温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kirekawa Onsen|qq=}}). == Onsen Town == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Siebold-no-yu.jpg|thumb|300px|{{Center|Siebold's Bath (シーボルトの湯)}} ]] This hot spring area, which rises in the heart of the town, is one of the largest onsen towns in Kyushu. Nearly 50 [[:en:Ryokan|Ryokan]] – both large and small – line the streets along the banks of the {{ill|Shioda River|ja|塩田川 (佐賀県)|lt=Shioda River|lt_ja=塩田川|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shioda River|qq=}} (also known as {{ill|Ureshino River|ja|嬉野川|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ureshino River|qq=}}), including Wataya Villa, where [[:en:Hirohito|Emperor Shōwa]] stayed during the 38th {{ill|National Tree Planting Festival|ja|全国植樹祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Tree Planting Festival|qq=}} held in Saga Prefecture in 1987 (Showa 62). In addition, the oldest inn in Ureshino is said to be {{ill|Omuraya|ja|大村屋|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omuraya|qq=}}, founded in 1830 (the first year of the Tenpō era). In the center of the shopping district’s footbath plaza, there is “[[:en:Philipp Franz von Siebold|Siebold]]’s Foot Bath,” which is available free of charge. Nearby stands the wooden, two-story (partly three-story) with one basement [[:en:Public bathing|Public Bathhouse]] “Furuyu Onsen,” constructed in 1924 (Taishō 13) to a design by a [[:en:Germans|German]]. Although by around 2001 its interior and piping had deteriorated, the building’s exterior remained in nearly excellent condition{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀県の近代化遺産-佐賀県近代化遺産（建造物等）総合調査報告書-|year=2002|publisher=佐賀県教育委員会|page=182|series=佐賀県文化財調査報告書第153集}}. However, it was demolished on March 20, 2005 (Heisei 17) due to damage from the [[:en:2005 Fukuoka earthquake|Fukuoka Prefecture Western Offshore Earthquake]]. Later, in response to local demand, it was reconstructed to replicate its Taishō-era appearance and reopened on April 1, 2010 (Heisei 22) under the new name “Siebold’s Bath”{{Cite web |title=＜重点報道＠嬉野市＞わがまち今昔 シーボルトの湯 {{!}} まちの話題 {{!}} 佐賀新聞ニュース |url=https://www.saga-s.co.jp/articles/-/1114588 |website=佐賀新聞 |date=2024-04-09 |access-date=2024-04-09 |language=ja}}. Also known as the “Hot Spring for Beautiful Skin,” Ureshino Onsen is suitable for drinking. Its signature dish, the hot spring {{ill|Hot Spring Tofu|ja|湯豆腐|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hot Spring Tofu|qq=}}, prepared using the onsen water, is a renowned specialty of Ureshino. In Ureshino City the product is written as “Yudōfu,” and the name “Ureshino Onsen Yudōfu” is trademarked by the city. == History == [[File:Ureshino Onsen 01.jpg|thumb|280px|{{Center|Onsen Town|1=Spa Town|lt=Onsen Town}} ]] Ureshino Onsen first appears in historical records in the ''Hizen Province Fudoki'' ({{ill|Hizen Province Fudoki|ja|肥前国風土記|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hizen Province Fudoki|qq=}}), compiled during the Nara period, with a description as a “hot spring that cures the ailments of all people,” although its name is not mentioned嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、272頁. According to legend, [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]] discovered the hot spring on her return from the {{ill|Conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea|ja|三韓征伐|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea|qq=}} and, while soothing her soldiers’ fatigue, exclaimed something akin to “How delightful!”—a remark that was later associated with the naming of “Ureshino.” Other legends tell of either Prince Takaso (from the ''Daidōji Kyuuki'') or an old woman (from the legend of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyotamahime Shrine|qq=}}) exclaiming “ureshi.” These tales, however, were retroactively linked after the name “Ureshino” (originally read “ureshino”) was established, and the exclamation is not considered directly connected to the place name. In fact, the term “ureshino” is first confirmed in historical documents during the Kamakura period, when it was written as “宇礼志野”嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、351～353頁. The origin of the name is attributed to a field located in the upper reaches of the Shioda River; because the word “末” (ure) means “tip” or “end,” the area was called “Sueshino” and later a kanji was assigned to form the name{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀地名うんちく事典|year=2005|publisher=佐賀新聞社|page=93}}. After a period with few records concerning the hot spring, by the late Sengoku period (1570s) records emerge of [[:en:Ryūzōji Takanobu|Ryūzōji Takanobu]] recommending hot spring therapy in Ureshino嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、710頁. During the [[:en:Edo period|Edo Period]], Ureshino Onsen flourished as Ureshino-juku, a {{ill|Post Town|ja|宿場町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Post Town|qq=}} on the [[:en:Nagasaki Kaidō|Nagasaki Kaidō]]. In 1656 (Meireki 2), during the time of the first lord of the [[:en:Hasunoike Domain|Hasuike Domain]], Nabeshima Naotoshi, management of the spring source – previously under the jurisdiction of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyotamahime Shrine|qq=}} – was transferred to the domain, and a roof was added to the open-air bath, converting it into a domain-run bathhouse. The post town was frequented by many travelers, and the state of Ureshino Onsen was recorded in works such as ''Wakan Sansai Zue'' and ''Edo Travelogue''. It appears that from this period it also became known as an entertainment hot spring. After World War II, Ureshino Onsen gained fame as an entertainment hot spring comparable to [[:en:Beppu Onsen|Beppu]] in the west. However, each onsen inn has its own distinctive style and character, and while many events are held, comparatively few new facilities have been introduced. In the former Ureshino Town (now part of [[:en:Ureshino, Saga|Ureshino City]]) tea has been cultivated for generations. For this reason, Ureshino City and its tourism association actively promote the area as '''"Hot Spring Land of Tea and Tofu"''', and various initiatives have been undertaken to link the two. In addition, a 2D character themed on hot springs, “Ureshino Rokka” (from {{ill|Onsen Musume|ja|温泉むすめ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onsen Musume|qq=}}), is used to promote the hot springs{{Cite web |url=https://onsen-musume.jp/character/ureshino_rikka |title=嬉野 六香 |access-date=2024-09-22 |publisher=株式会社エンバウンド |website=温泉むすめ公式サイト}}. == Access == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Tofu.jpg|thumb|190px|{{Center|A Famous Specialty from the Edo Period
'Hot Spring Tofu'}} ]] * Railway (access from [[:en:Kyushu Railway Company|JR Kyushu]] stations) ** About 13 minutes by {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR Kyushu Bus|qq=}} from [[:en:Ureshino-Onsen Station|Ureshino Onsen Station]] on the [[:en:Nishi Kyushu Shinkansen|West Kyushu Shinkansen]]. ** About 30 minutes by {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR Kyushu Bus|qq=}} from [[:en:Takeo-Onsen Station|Takeo Onsen Station]] on the [[:en:Sasebo Line|Sasebo Line]]. ** About 1 hour by [[:en:Saihi Motor|Nishi-Hii Bus]] from [[:en:Sasebo Station|Sasebo Station]] on the Sasebo Line. ** About 30 minutes by {{ill|Yūtoku Bus|ja|祐徳自動車|lt=Yūtoku Bus|lt_ja=祐徳バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yūtoku Bus|qq=}} from [[:en:Hizen-Kashima Station|Hizen Kashima Station]] on the [[:en:Nagasaki Main Line|Nagasaki Main Line]]. ** About 25 minutes by {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR Kyushu Bus|qq=}} from [[:en:Sonogi Station|Karinoki Station]] on the [[:en:Ōmura Line|Omura Line]]. * Highway Bus *: Use the “{{ill|Kyushu-go|ja|九州号|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyushu-go|qq=}}” operated by {{ill|Kyushu Express Bus|ja|九州急行バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyushu Express Bus|qq=}}. There are services that stop at the Ureshino Bus Center ([[:en:Japan National Route 34|National Route 34]]) in the hot spring town and services that stop only at the {{ill|Ureshino Interchange|ja|嬉野インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ureshino Interchange|qq=}} on the [[:en:Nagasaki Expressway|Nagasaki Expressway]]. In recent years, the latter has far more frequent service – while the former runs only 4 times a day, the latter operates roughly every 30 minutes. ** About 2 hours from [[:en:Fukuoka|Fukuoka City]] (via {{ill|Hakata Bus Terminal|ja|博多バスターミナル|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakata Bus Terminal|qq=}} and {{ill|Nishitetsu Tenjin Express Bus Terminal|ja|西鉄天神高速バスターミナル|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitetsu Tenjin Express Bus Terminal|qq=}}). ** About 1 hour from [[:en:Nagasaki|Nagasaki City]] (from [[:en:Nagasaki Station|Nagasaki Station Front]]). * Shared Taxi from the Airport *: With the opening of [[:en:Saga Airport|Saga Airport]], local taxi companies began operating services. The travel time from Saga Airport is approximately 1 hour. * Private Car *: 5 minutes via the {{ill|Nagasaki Prefectural and Saga Prefectural Route 1 Sasebo-Ureshino Line|ja|長崎県道・佐賀県道1号佐世保嬉野線|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagasaki Prefectural and Saga Prefectural Route 1 Sasebo-Ureshino Line|qq=}} from the Ureshino Interchange on the [[:en:Nagasaki Expressway|Nagasaki Expressway]]. == References == == Related Literature == *{{Cite book |Language=Japanese |author=Masamichi Ikeda|year=1898|title=Ureshino Onsen Chronicles|id={{NDLJP|766546}}|quote= }} == See Also == {{commonscat|Ureshino Onsen}} * {{ill|Tourist Attractions in Saga Prefecture|ja|佐賀県の観光地|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tourist {{infobox Onsen |Name = Ureshino Onsen |image = Ureshino onsen.jpg |Comment = |Location = [[:en:Saga Prefecture|Saga Prefecture]] [[:en:Ureshino, Saga|Ureshino City]] {{ill|Ureshino Town|ja|嬉野町 (佐賀県)|lt=Ureshino Town|lt_ja=嬉野町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ureshino Town|qq=}} |Access = Railway : [[:en:Sasebo Line|Sasebo Line]] [[:en:Takeo-Onsen Station|Takeo Onsen Station]] via {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR Kyushu Bus|qq=}} for about 30 minutes
West Kyushu Shinkansen Ureshino Onsen Station
''For other access methods, see [[#アクセス|Access]]'' |Water Type = [[:en:Brine spring|Brine spring]] |Temperature = |Discharge = |pH =7.8 |Liquid Classification = |Osmotic Pressure Classification = |Number of Accommodations = |Total Capacity = |Annual Bath Visitors = |Statistical Year = |External links = [https://spa-u.net/ Ureshino Onsen Tourism Association] |Special Notes = }} '''Ureshino Onsen''' (嬉野温泉) is a [[:en:Onsen|Onsen]] located in [[:en:Saga Prefecture|Saga Prefecture]], [[:en:Ureshino, Saga|Ureshino City]], and {{ill|Ureshino Town|ja|嬉野町 (佐賀県)|lt=Ureshino Town|lt_ja=嬉野町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ureshino Town|qq=}} (formerly part of [[:en:Hizen Province|Hizen Province]]). Along with {{ill|Takeo Onsen|ja|武雄温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeo Onsen|qq=}}, it is one of the representative hot springs of the prefecture. It has been selected as one of [[:en:100 Landscapes of Japan (Shōwa era)|Japan's 100 Views]] and is trademarked by Ureshino City under the names “Japan’s Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs Ureshino Onsen” and “Saga–Ureshino Onsen.” == Water Type == * Sodium – Bicarbonate Salt / Chloride Hot Spring It is a baking soda spring renowned for its beauty-enhancing properties, leaving the skin exceptionally smooth after a [[:en:Bathing|Bathing]]. Its water quality was chosen by {{ill|Satoshi Fujita|ja|藤田聡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Satoshi Fujita|qq=}} as one of the {{ill|Japan's Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs|ja|日本三大美肌の湯|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan's Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs|qq=}} (the other two being {{ill|Hinokami Onsen|ja|斐乃上温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hinokami Onsen|qq=}} and {{ill|Kirekawa Onsen|ja|喜連川温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kirekawa Onsen|qq=}}). == Onsen Town == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Siebold-no-yu.jpg|thumb|300px|{{Center|Siebold's Bath (シーボルトの湯)}} ]] This hot spring area, which rises in the heart of the town, is one of the largest onsen towns in Kyushu. Nearly 50 [[:en:Ryokan|Ryokan]] – both large and small – line the streets along the banks of the {{ill|Shioda River|ja|塩田川 (佐賀県)|lt=Shioda River|lt_ja=塩田川|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shioda River|qq=}} (also known as {{ill|Ureshino River|ja|嬉野川|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ureshino River|qq=}}), including Wataya Villa, where [[:en:Hirohito|Emperor Shōwa]] stayed during the 38th {{ill|National Tree Planting Festival|ja|全国植樹祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Tree Planting Festival|qq=}} held in Saga Prefecture in 1987 (Showa 62). In addition, the oldest inn in Ureshino is said to be {{ill|Omuraya|ja|大村屋|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omuraya|qq=}}, founded in 1830 (the first year of the Tenpō era). In the center of the shopping district’s footbath plaza, there is “[[:en:Philipp Franz von Siebold|Siebold]]’s Foot Bath,” which is available free of charge. Nearby stands the wooden, two-story (partly three-story) with one basement [[:en:Public bathing|Public Bathhouse]] “Furuyu Onsen,” constructed in 1924 (Taishō 13) to a design by a [[:en:Germans|German]]. Although by around 2001 its interior and piping had deteriorated, the building’s exterior remained in nearly excellent condition{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀県の近代化遺産-佐賀県近代化遺産（建造物等）総合調査報告書-|year=2002|publisher=佐賀県教育委員会|page=182|series=佐賀県文化財調査報告書第153集}}. However, it was demolished on March 20, 2005 (Heisei 17) due to damage from the [[:en:2005 Fukuoka earthquake|Fukuoka Prefecture Western Offshore Earthquake]]. Later, in response to local demand, it was reconstructed to replicate its Taishō-era appearance and reopened on April 1, 2010 (Heisei 22) under the new name “Siebold’s Bath”{{Cite web |title=＜重点報道＠嬉野市＞わがまち今昔 シーボルトの湯 {{!}} まちの話題 {{!}} 佐賀新聞ニュース |url=https://www.saga-s.co.jp/articles/-/1114588 |website=佐賀新聞 |date=2024-04-09 |access-date=2024-04-09 |language=ja}}. Also known as the “Hot Spring for Beautiful Skin,” Ureshino Onsen is suitable for drinking. Its signature dish, the hot spring {{ill|Hot Spring Tofu|ja|湯豆腐|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hot Spring Tofu|qq=}}, prepared using the onsen water, is a renowned specialty of Ureshino. In Ureshino City the product is written as “Yudōfu,” and the name “Ureshino Onsen Yudōfu” is trademarked by the city. == History == [[File:Ureshino Onsen 01.jpg|thumb|280px|{{Center|Onsen Town|1=Spa Town|lt=Onsen Town}} ]] Ureshino Onsen first appears in historical records in the ''Hizen Province Fudoki'' ({{ill|Hizen Province Fudoki|ja|肥前国風土記|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hizen Province Fudoki|qq=}}), compiled during the Nara period, with a description as a “hot spring that cures the ailments of all people,” although its name is not mentioned嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、272頁. According to legend, [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]] discovered the hot spring on her return from the {{ill|Conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea|ja|三韓征伐|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea|qq=}} and, while soothing her soldiers’ fatigue, exclaimed something akin to “How delightful!”—a remark that was later associated with the naming of “Ureshino.” Other legends tell of either Prince Takaso (from the ''Daidōji Kyuuki'') or an old woman (from the legend of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyotamahime Shrine|qq=}}) exclaiming “ureshi.” These tales, however, were retroactively linked after the name “Ureshino” (originally read “ureshino”) was established, and the exclamation is not considered directly connected to the place name. In fact, the term “ureshino” is first confirmed in historical documents during the Kamakura period, when it was written as “宇礼志野”嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、351～353頁. The origin of the name is attributed to a field located in the upper reaches of the Shioda River; because the word “末” (ure) means “tip” or “end,” the area was called “Sueshino” and later a kanji was assigned to form the name{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀地名うんちく事典|year=2005|publisher=佐賀新聞社|page=93}}. After a period with few records concerning the hot spring, by the late Sengoku period (1570s) records emerge of [[:en:Ryūzōji Takanobu|Ryūzōji Takanobu]] recommending hot spring therapy in Ureshino嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、710頁. During the [[:en:Edo period|Edo Period]], Ureshino Onsen flourished as Ureshino-juku, a {{ill|Post Town|ja|宿場町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Post Town|qq=}} on the [[:en:Nagasaki Kaidō|Nagasaki Kaidō]]. In 1656 (Meireki 2), during the time of the first lord of the [[:en:Hasunoike Domain|Hasuike Domain]], Nabeshima Naotoshi, management of the spring source – previously under the jurisdiction of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyotamahime Shrine|qq=}} – was transferred to the domain, and a roof was added to the open-air bath, converting it into a domain-run bathhouse. The post town was frequented by many travelers, and the state of Ureshino Onsen was recorded in works such as ''Wakan Sansai Zue'' and ''Edo Travelogue''. It appears that from this period it also became known as an entertainment hot spring. After World War II, Ureshino Onsen gained fame as an entertainment hot spring comparable to [[:en:Beppu Onsen|Beppu]] in the west. However, each onsen inn has its own distinctive style and character, and while many events are held, comparatively few new facilities have been introduced. In the former Ureshino Town (now part of [[:en:Ureshino, Saga|Ureshino City]]) tea has been cultivated for generations. For this reason, Ureshino City and its tourism association actively promote the area as '''"Hot Spring Land of Tea and Tofu"''', and various initiatives have been undertaken to link the two. In addition, a 2D character themed on hot springs, “Ureshino Rokka” (from {{ill|Onsen Musume|ja|温泉むすめ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onsen Musume|qq=}}), is used to promote the hot springs{{Cite web |url=https://onsen-musume.jp/character/ureshino_rikka |title=嬉野 六香 |access-date=2024-09-22 |publisher=株式会社エンバウンド |website=温泉むすめ公式サイト}}. == Access == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Tofu.jpg|thumb|190px|{{Center|A Famous Specialty from the Edo Period
'Hot Spring Tofu'}} ]] * Railway (access from [[:en:Kyushu Railway Company|JR Kyushu]] stations) ** About 13 minutes by {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR Kyushu Bus|qq=}} from [[:en:Ureshino-Onsen Station|Ureshino Onsen Station]] on the [[:en:Nishi Kyushu Shinkansen|West Kyushu Shinkansen]]. ** About 30 minutes by {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR Kyushu Bus|qq=}} from [[:en:Takeo-Onsen Station|Takeo Onsen Station]] on the [[:en:Sasebo Line|Sasebo Line]]. ** About 1 hour by [[:en:Saihi Motor|Nishi-Hii Bus]] from [[:en:Sasebo Station|Sasebo Station]] on the Sasebo Line. ** About 30 minutes by {{ill|Yūtoku Bus|ja|祐徳自動車|lt=Yūtoku Bus|lt_ja=祐徳バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yūtoku Bus|qq=}} from [[:en:Hizen-Kashima Station|Hizen Kashima Station]] on the [[:en:Nagasaki Main Line|Nagasaki Main Line]]. ** About 25 minutes by {{ill|JR Kyushu Bus|ja|JR九州バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR Kyushu Bus|qq=}} from [[:en:Sonogi Station|Karinoki Station]] on the [[:en:Ōmura Line|Omura Line]]. * Highway Bus *: Use the “{{ill|Kyushu-go|ja|九州号|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyushu-go|qq=}}” operated by {{ill|Kyushu Express Bus|ja|九州急行バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyushu Express Bus|qq=}}. There are services that stop at the Ureshino Bus Center ([[:en:Japan National Route 34|National Route 34]]) in the hot spring town and services that stop only at the {{ill|Ureshino Interchange|ja|嬉野インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ureshino Interchange|qq=}} on the [[:en:Nagasaki Expressway|Nagasaki Expressway]]. In recent years, the latter has far more frequent service – while the former runs only 4 times a day, the latter operates roughly every 30 minutes. ** About 2 hours from [[:en:Fukuoka|Fukuoka City]] (via {{ill|Hakata Bus Terminal|ja|博多バスターミナル|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakata Bus Terminal|qq=}} and {{ill|Nishitetsu Tenjin Express Bus Terminal|ja|西鉄天神高速バスターミナル|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitetsu Tenjin Express Bus Terminal|qq=}}). ** About 1 hour from [[:en:Nagasaki|Nagasaki City]] (from [[:en:Nagasaki Station|Nagasaki Station Front]]). * Shared Taxi from the Airport *: With the opening of [[:en:Saga Airport|Saga Airport]], local taxi companies began operating services. The travel time from Saga Airport is approximately 1 hour. * Private Car *: 5 minutes via the {{ill|Nagasaki Prefectural and Saga Prefectural Route 1 Sasebo-Ureshino Line|ja|長崎県道・佐賀県道1号佐世保嬉野線|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagasaki Prefectural and Saga Prefectural Route 1 Sasebo-Ureshino Line|qq=}} from the Ureshino Interchange on the [[:en:Nagasaki Expressway|Nagasaki Expressway]]. == References == == Related Literature == *{{Cite book |Language=Japanese |author=Masamichi Ikeda|year=1898|title=Ureshino Onsen Chronicles|id={{NDLJP|766546}}|quote= }} == See Also == {{commonscat|Ureshino Onsen}} * {{ill|Tourist Attractions in Saga Prefecture|ja|佐賀県の観光地|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tourist Attractions in Saga Prefecture|qq=}} * [[:en:Nishi Kyushu Shinkansen|West Kyushu Shinkansen]] * [[:en:Ureshino-Onsen Station|Ureshino Onsen Station]] * {{ill|Hizen Dream Road|ja|肥前夢街道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hizen Dream Road|qq=}} * {{ill|Wataya Villa|ja|和多屋別荘|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wataya Villa|qq=}} * {{ill|Irifune-sō|ja|入船荘|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Irifune-sō|qq=}} * [[:en:Types of prostitution in modern Japan|Soapland]] * [[:en:Yuki Yanagita|Yagita Yūki]] … (conducts self-training at Ureshino Onsen every year). * The townscape of {{ill|Shiodazu|ja|塩田津|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiodazu|qq=}} ({{ill|Important Preservation District for Groups of Traditional Buildings|ja|重要伝統的建造物群保存地区|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Preservation District for Groups of Traditional Buildings|qq=}}) … the post town following Ureshino-juku. == External Links == * [https://spa-u.net/ Ureshino Onsen Tourism Association] * [https://www.nicovideo.jp/watch/1269845231 Nico Nico Douga Ureshino Onsen Public Bath “Siebold’s Bath”] After a period with few records concerning the hot spring, by the late Sengoku period (1570s) records emerge of [[:en:Ryūzōji Takanobu|Ryūzōji Takanobu]] recommending hot spring therapy in Ureshino嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、710頁. During the [[:en:Edo period|Edo Period]], Ureshino Onsen flourished as Ureshino-juku, a {{ill|Post Town|ja|宿場町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Post Town|qq=}} on the [[:en:Nagasaki Kaidō|Nagasaki Kaidō]]. In 1656 (Meireki 2), during the time of the first lord of the [[:en:Hasunoike Domain|Hasuike Domain]], Nabeshima Naotoshi, management of the spring source – previously under the jurisdiction of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyotamahime Shrine|qq=}} – was transferred to the domain, and a roof was added to the open-air bath, converting it into a domain-run bathhouse. The post town was frequented by many travelers, and the state of Ureshino Onsen was recorded in works such as ''Wakan Sansai Zue'' and ''Edo Travelogue''. It appears that from this period it also became known as an entertainment hot spring. After World War II, Ureshino Onsen gained fame as an entertainment hot spring comparable to [[:en:Beppu Onsen|Beppu]] in the west. However, each onsen inn has its own distinctive style and character, and while many events are held, comparatively few new facilities have been introduced. In the former Ureshino Town (now part of [[:en:Ureshino, Saga|Ureshino City]]) tea has been cultivated for generations. For this reason, Ureshino City and its tourism association actively promote the area as '''"Hot Spring Land of Tea and Tofu"''', and various initiatives have been undertaken to link the two. In addition, a 2D character themed on hot springs, “Ureshino Rokka” (from {{ill|Onsen Musume|ja|温泉むすめ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onsen Musume|qq=}}), is used to promote the hot springs{{Cite web |url=https://onsen-musume.jp/character/ureshino_rikka |title=嬉野 六香 |access-date=2024-09-22 |publisher=株式会社エンバウンド |website=温泉むすめ公式サイト}}. == Access == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Tofu.jpg|thumb|190px|{{Center|A Famous Specialty from the Edo Period
