West Kyushu Shinkansen Ureshino Onsen Station
''For other access methods, see [[#アクセス|Access]]'' |Water Type = {{ill|Brine spring|en|Brine spring|WD=Q11428612|lt=Brine spring|1=Brine spring}} |Temperature = |Discharge = |pH =7.8 |Liquid Classification = |Osmotic Pressure Classification = |Number of Accommodations = |Total Capacity = |Annual Bath Visitors = |Statistical Year = |External links = [https://spa-u.net/ Ureshino Onsen Tourism Association] |Special Notes = }} '''Ureshino Onsen''' (嬉野温泉) is a {{ill|Onsen|en|Onsen|WD=Q655311|lt=Onsen|1=Onsen}} located in {{ill|Saga Prefecture|en|Saga Prefecture|WD=Q160420|lt=Saga Prefecture|1=Saga Prefecture}}, {{ill|Ureshino, Saga|en|Ureshino, Saga|WD=Q634130|lt=Ureshino City|1=Ureshino, Saga}}, and {{ill|Ureshino Town|ja|嬉野町 (佐賀県)|lt=Ureshino Town|lt_ja=嬉野町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ureshino Town|1=Ureshino|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q15259967}} (formerly part of {{ill|Hizen Province|en|Hizen Province|WD=Q906926|lt=Hizen Province|1=Hizen Province}}). Along with {{ill|Takeo Onsen|ja|武雄温泉|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeo Onsen|qq=}}, it is one of the representative hot springs of the prefecture. It has been selected as one of {{ill|100 Landscapes of Japan (Shōwa era)|en|100 Landscapes of Japan (Shōwa era)|WD=Q2806722|lt=Japan's 100 Views|1=100 Landscapes of Japan (Shōwa era)}} and is trademarked by Ureshino City under the names “Japan’s Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs Ureshino Onsen” and “Saga–Ureshino Onsen.” == Water Type == * Sodium – Bicarbonate Salt / Chloride Hot Spring It is a baking soda spring renowned for its beauty-enhancing properties, leaving the skin exceptionally smooth after a {{ill|Bathing|en|Bathing|WD=Q327651|lt=Bathing|1=Bathing}}. Its water quality was chosen by {{ill|Satoshi Fujita|ja|藤田聡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Satoshi Fujita|1=Satoshi Fujita|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11624881}} as one of the {{ill|Japan's Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs|ja|日本三大美肌の湯|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan's Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs|1=Japan's Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11507114}} (the other two being {{ill|Hinokami Onsen|ja|斐乃上温泉|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hinokami Onsen|1=Q11500713|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11500713}} and {{ill|Kirekawa Onsen|ja|喜連川温泉|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kirekawa Onsen|1=Kitsuregawa Onsen|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11419259}}). == Onsen Town == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Siebold-no-yu.jpg|thumb|300px|{{Center|Siebold's Bath (シーボルトの湯)}} ]] This hot spring area, which rises in the heart of the town, is one of the largest onsen towns in Kyushu. Nearly 50 {{ill|Ryokan|en|Ryokan|WD=Q562930|lt=Ryokan|1=Ryokan}} – both large and small – line the streets along the banks of the {{ill|Shioda River|ja|塩田川 (佐賀県)|lt=Shioda River|lt_ja=塩田川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shioda River|1=Shiota River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q48747422}} (also known as {{ill|Ureshino River|ja|嬉野川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ureshino River|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}), including Wataya Villa, where {{ill|Hirohito|en|Hirohito|WD=Q34479|lt=Emperor Shōwa|1=Hirohito}} stayed during the 38th {{ill|National Tree Planting Festival|ja|全国植樹祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Tree Planting Festival|1=National Tree-Planting Festival|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11389414}} held in Saga Prefecture in 1987 (Showa 62). In addition, the oldest inn in Ureshino is said to be {{ill|Omuraya|ja|大村屋|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omuraya|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, founded in 1830 (the first year of the Tenpō era). In the center of the shopping district’s footbath plaza, there is “{{ill|Philipp Franz von Siebold|en|Philipp Franz von Siebold|WD=Q77140|lt=Siebold|1=Philipp Franz von Siebold}}’s Foot Bath,” which is available free of charge. Nearby stands the wooden, two-story (partly three-story) with one basement {{ill|Public bathing|en|Public bathing|WD=Q785952|lt=Public Bathhouse|1=Public bathing}} “Furuyu Onsen,” constructed in 1924 (Taishō 13) to a design by a {{ill|Germans|en|Germans|WD=Q42884|lt=German|1=Germans}}. Although by around 2001 its interior and piping had deteriorated, the building’s exterior remained in nearly excellent condition{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀県の近代化遺産-佐賀県近代化遺産（建造物等）総合調査報告書-|year=2002|publisher=佐賀県教育委員会|page=182|series=佐賀県文化財調査報告書第153集}}. However, it was demolished on March 20, 2005 (Heisei 17) due to damage from the {{ill|2005 Fukuoka earthquake|en|2005 Fukuoka earthquake|WD=Q4604346|lt=Fukuoka Prefecture Western Offshore Earthquake|1=2005 Fukuoka earthquake}}. Later, in response to local demand, it was reconstructed to replicate its Taishō-era appearance and reopened on April 1, 2010 (Heisei 22) under the new name “Siebold’s Bath”{{Cite web |title=＜重点報道＠嬉野市＞わがまち今昔 シーボルトの湯 {{!}} まちの話題 {{!}} 佐賀新聞ニュース |url=https://www.saga-s.co.jp/articles/-/1114588 |website=佐賀新聞 |date=2024-04-09 |access-date=2024-04-09 |language=ja}}. Also known as the “Hot Spring for Beautiful Skin,” Ureshino Onsen is suitable for drinking. Its signature dish, the hot spring {{ill|Hot Spring Tofu|ja|湯豆腐|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hot Spring Tofu|1=yudofu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11264372}}, prepared using the onsen water, is a renowned specialty of Ureshino. In Ureshino City the product is written as “Yudōfu,” and the name “Ureshino Onsen Yudōfu” is trademarked by the city. == History == [[File:Ureshino Onsen 01.jpg|thumb|280px|{{Center|Onsen Town|1=Spa Town|lt=Onsen Town}} ]] Ureshino Onsen first appears in historical records in the ''Hizen Province Fudoki'' ({{ill|Hizen Province Fudoki|ja|肥前国風土記|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hizen Province Fudoki|1=Hizen no Kuni Fudoki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q111890610}}), compiled during the Nara period, with a description as a “hot spring that cures the ailments of all people,” although its name is not mentioned嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、272頁. According to legend, {{ill|Empress Jingū|en|Empress Jingū|WD=Q232803|lt=Empress Jingū|1=Empress Jingū}} discovered the hot spring on her return from the {{ill|Conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea|ja|三韓征伐|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea|1=Three Han Campaign|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11249435}} and, while soothing her soldiers’ fatigue, exclaimed something akin to “How delightful!”—a remark that was later associated with the naming of “Ureshino.” Other legends tell of either Prince Takaso (from the ''Daidōji Kyuuki'') or an old woman (from the legend of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyotamahime Shrine|1=Q11633963|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11633963}}) exclaiming “ureshi.” These tales, however, were retroactively linked after the name “Ureshino” (originally read “ureshino”) was established, and the exclamation is not considered directly connected to the place name. In fact, the term “ureshino” is first confirmed in historical documents during the Kamakura period, when it was written as “宇礼志野”嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、351～353頁. The origin of the name is attributed to a field located in the upper reaches of the Shioda River; because the word “末” (ure) means “tip” or “end,” the area was called “Sueshino” and later a kanji was assigned to form the name{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀地名うんちく事典|year=2005|publisher=佐賀新聞社|page=93}}. After a period with few records concerning the hot spring, by the late Sengoku period (1570s) records emerge of {{ill|Ryūzōji Takanobu|en|Ryūzōji Takanobu|WD=Q1076150|lt=Ryūzōji Takanobu|1=Ryūzōji Takanobu}} recommending hot spring therapy in Ureshino嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、710頁. During the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|WD=Q184963|lt=Edo Period|1=Edo period}}, Ureshino Onsen flourished as Ureshino-juku, a {{ill|Post Town|ja|宿場町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Post Town|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 宿場|1=Shukuba|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1209783}} on the {{ill|Nagasaki Kaidō|en|Nagasaki Kaidō|WD=Q1352312|lt=Nagasaki Kaidō|1=Nagasaki Kaidō}}. In 1656 (Meireki 2), during the time of the first lord of the {{ill|Hasunoike Domain|en|Hasunoike Domain|WD=Q3034444|lt=Hasuike Domain|1=Hasunoike Domain}}, Nabeshima Naotoshi, management of the spring source – previously under the jurisdiction of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyotamahime Shrine|1=Q11633963|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11633963}} – was transferred to the domain, and a roof was added to the open-air bath, converting it into a domain-run bathhouse. The post town was frequented by many travelers, and the state of Ureshino Onsen was recorded in works such as ''Wakan Sansai Zue'' and ''Edo Travelogue''. It appears that from this period it also became known as an entertainment hot spring. After World War II, Ureshino Onsen gained fame as an entertainment hot spring comparable to {{ill|Beppu Onsen|en|Beppu Onsen|WD=Q4890932|lt=Beppu|1=Beppu Onsen}} in the west. However, each onsen inn has its own distinctive style and character, and while many events are held, comparatively few new facilities have been introduced. In the former Ureshino Town (now part of {{ill|Ureshino, Saga|en|Ureshino, Saga|WD=Q634130|lt=Ureshino City|1=Ureshino, Saga}}) tea has been cultivated for generations. For this reason, Ureshino City and its tourism association actively promote the area as '''"Hot Spring Land of Tea and Tofu"''', and various initiatives have been undertaken to link the two. In addition, a 2D character themed on hot springs, “Ureshino Rokka” (from {{ill|Onsen Musume|ja|温泉むすめ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onsen Musume|1=Onsen Musume|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q30531379}}), is used to promote the hot springs{{Cite web |url=https://onsen-musume.jp/character/ureshino_rikka |title=嬉野 六香 |access-date=2024-09-22 |publisher=株式会社エンバウンド |website=温泉むすめ公式サイト}}. == Access == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Tofu.jpg|thumb|190px|{{Center|A Famous Specialty from the Edo Period

''For other access methods, see [[#アクセス|Access]]'' |Water Type = {{ill|Brine spring|en|Brine spring|WD=Q11428612|lt=Brine spring|1=Brine spring}} |Temperature = |Discharge = |pH =7.8 |Liquid Classification = |Osmotic Pressure Classification = |Number of Accommodations = |Total Capacity = |Annual Bath Visitors = |Statistical Year = |External links = [https://spa-u.net/ Ureshino Onsen Tourism Association] |Special Notes = }} '''Ureshino Onsen''' (嬉野温泉) is a {{ill|Onsen|en|Onsen|WD=Q655311|lt=Onsen|1=Onsen}} located in {{ill|Saga Prefecture|en|Saga Prefecture|WD=Q160420|lt=Saga Prefecture|1=Saga Prefecture}}, {{ill|Ureshino, Saga|en|Ureshino, Saga|WD=Q634130|lt=Ureshino City|1=Ureshino, Saga}}, and {{ill|Ureshino Town|ja|嬉野町 (佐賀県)|lt=Ureshino Town|lt_ja=嬉野町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ureshino Town|1=Ureshino|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q15259967}} (formerly part of {{ill|Hizen Province|en|Hizen Province|WD=Q906926|lt=Hizen Province|1=Hizen Province}}). Along with {{ill|Takeo Onsen|ja|武雄温泉|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeo Onsen|qq=}}, it is one of the representative hot springs of the prefecture. It has been selected as one of {{ill|100 Landscapes of Japan (Shōwa era)|en|100 Landscapes of Japan (Shōwa era)|WD=Q2806722|lt=Japan's 100 Views|1=100 Landscapes of Japan (Shōwa era)}} and is trademarked by Ureshino City under the names “Japan’s Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs Ureshino Onsen” and “Saga–Ureshino Onsen.” == Water Type == * Sodium – Bicarbonate Salt / Chloride Hot Spring It is a baking soda spring renowned for its beauty-enhancing properties, leaving the skin exceptionally smooth after a {{ill|Bathing|en|Bathing|WD=Q327651|lt=Bathing|1=Bathing}}. Its water quality was chosen by {{ill|Satoshi Fujita|ja|藤田聡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Satoshi Fujita|1=Satoshi Fujita|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11624881}} as one of the {{ill|Japan's Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs|ja|日本三大美肌の湯|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan's Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs|1=Japan's Three Great Beautiful Skin Hot Springs|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11507114}} (the other two being {{ill|Hinokami Onsen|ja|斐乃上温泉|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hinokami Onsen|1=Q11500713|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11500713}} and {{ill|Kirekawa Onsen|ja|喜連川温泉|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kirekawa Onsen|1=Kitsuregawa Onsen|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11419259}}). == Onsen Town == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Siebold-no-yu.jpg|thumb|300px|{{Center|Siebold's Bath (シーボルトの湯)}} ]] This hot spring area, which rises in the heart of the town, is one of the largest onsen towns in Kyushu. Nearly 50 {{ill|Ryokan|en|Ryokan|WD=Q562930|lt=Ryokan|1=Ryokan}} – both large and small – line the streets along the banks of the {{ill|Shioda River|ja|塩田川 (佐賀県)|lt=Shioda River|lt_ja=塩田川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shioda River|1=Shiota River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q48747422}} (also known as {{ill|Ureshino River|ja|嬉野川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ureshino River|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}), including Wataya Villa, where {{ill|Hirohito|en|Hirohito|WD=Q34479|lt=Emperor Shōwa|1=Hirohito}} stayed during the 38th {{ill|National Tree Planting Festival|ja|全国植樹祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Tree Planting Festival|1=National Tree-Planting Festival|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11389414}} held in Saga Prefecture in 1987 (Showa 62). In addition, the oldest inn in Ureshino is said to be {{ill|Omuraya|ja|大村屋|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omuraya|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, founded in 1830 (the first year of the Tenpō era). In the center of the shopping district’s footbath plaza, there is “{{ill|Philipp Franz von Siebold|en|Philipp Franz von Siebold|WD=Q77140|lt=Siebold|1=Philipp Franz von Siebold}}’s Foot Bath,” which is available free of charge. Nearby stands the wooden, two-story (partly three-story) with one basement {{ill|Public bathing|en|Public bathing|WD=Q785952|lt=Public Bathhouse|1=Public bathing}} “Furuyu Onsen,” constructed in 1924 (Taishō 13) to a design by a {{ill|Germans|en|Germans|WD=Q42884|lt=German|1=Germans}}. Although by around 2001 its interior and piping had deteriorated, the building’s exterior remained in nearly excellent condition{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀県の近代化遺産-佐賀県近代化遺産（建造物等）総合調査報告書-|year=2002|publisher=佐賀県教育委員会|page=182|series=佐賀県文化財調査報告書第153集}}. However, it was demolished on March 20, 2005 (Heisei 17) due to damage from the {{ill|2005 Fukuoka earthquake|en|2005 Fukuoka earthquake|WD=Q4604346|lt=Fukuoka Prefecture Western Offshore Earthquake|1=2005 Fukuoka earthquake}}. Later, in response to local demand, it was reconstructed to replicate its Taishō-era appearance and reopened on April 1, 2010 (Heisei 22) under the new name “Siebold’s Bath”{{Cite web |title=＜重点報道＠嬉野市＞わがまち今昔 シーボルトの湯 {{!}} まちの話題 {{!}} 佐賀新聞ニュース |url=https://www.saga-s.co.jp/articles/-/1114588 |website=佐賀新聞 |date=2024-04-09 |access-date=2024-04-09 |language=ja}}. Also known as the “Hot Spring for Beautiful Skin,” Ureshino Onsen is suitable for drinking. Its signature dish, the hot spring {{ill|Hot Spring Tofu|ja|湯豆腐|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hot Spring Tofu|1=yudofu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11264372}}, prepared using the onsen water, is a renowned specialty of Ureshino. In Ureshino City the product is written as “Yudōfu,” and the name “Ureshino Onsen Yudōfu” is trademarked by the city. == History == [[File:Ureshino Onsen 01.jpg|thumb|280px|{{Center|Onsen Town|1=Spa Town|lt=Onsen Town}} ]] Ureshino Onsen first appears in historical records in the ''Hizen Province Fudoki'' ({{ill|Hizen Province Fudoki|ja|肥前国風土記|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hizen Province Fudoki|1=Hizen no Kuni Fudoki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q111890610}}), compiled during the Nara period, with a description as a “hot spring that cures the ailments of all people,” although its name is not mentioned嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、272頁. According to legend, {{ill|Empress Jingū|en|Empress Jingū|WD=Q232803|lt=Empress Jingū|1=Empress Jingū}} discovered the hot spring on her return from the {{ill|Conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea|ja|三韓征伐|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea|1=Three Han Campaign|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11249435}} and, while soothing her soldiers’ fatigue, exclaimed something akin to “How delightful!”—a remark that was later associated with the naming of “Ureshino.” Other legends tell of either Prince Takaso (from the ''Daidōji Kyuuki'') or an old woman (from the legend of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyotamahime Shrine|1=Q11633963|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11633963}}) exclaiming “ureshi.” These tales, however, were retroactively linked after the name “Ureshino” (originally read “ureshino”) was established, and the exclamation is not considered directly connected to the place name. In fact, the term “ureshino” is first confirmed in historical documents during the Kamakura period, when it was written as “宇礼志野”嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、351～353頁. The origin of the name is attributed to a field located in the upper reaches of the Shioda River; because the word “末” (ure) means “tip” or “end,” the area was called “Sueshino” and later a kanji was assigned to form the name{{Cite book|Language=Japanese |title=佐賀地名うんちく事典|year=2005|publisher=佐賀新聞社|page=93}}. After a period with few records concerning the hot spring, by the late Sengoku period (1570s) records emerge of {{ill|Ryūzōji Takanobu|en|Ryūzōji Takanobu|WD=Q1076150|lt=Ryūzōji Takanobu|1=Ryūzōji Takanobu}} recommending hot spring therapy in Ureshino嬉野町史編さん執筆委員会『嬉野町史　上巻』1980th year 、710頁. During the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|WD=Q184963|lt=Edo Period|1=Edo period}}, Ureshino Onsen flourished as Ureshino-juku, a {{ill|Post Town|ja|宿場町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Post Town|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 宿場|1=Shukuba|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1209783}} on the {{ill|Nagasaki Kaidō|en|Nagasaki Kaidō|WD=Q1352312|lt=Nagasaki Kaidō|1=Nagasaki Kaidō}}. In 1656 (Meireki 2), during the time of the first lord of the {{ill|Hasunoike Domain|en|Hasunoike Domain|WD=Q3034444|lt=Hasuike Domain|1=Hasunoike Domain}}, Nabeshima Naotoshi, management of the spring source – previously under the jurisdiction of {{ill|Toyotamahime Shrine|ja|豊玉姫神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyotamahime Shrine|1=Q11633963|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11633963}} – was transferred to the domain, and a roof was added to the open-air bath, converting it into a domain-run bathhouse. The post town was frequented by many travelers, and the state of Ureshino Onsen was recorded in works such as ''Wakan Sansai Zue'' and ''Edo Travelogue''. It appears that from this period it also became known as an entertainment hot spring. After World War II, Ureshino Onsen gained fame as an entertainment hot spring comparable to {{ill|Beppu Onsen|en|Beppu Onsen|WD=Q4890932|lt=Beppu|1=Beppu Onsen}} in the west. However, each onsen inn has its own distinctive style and character, and while many events are held, comparatively few new facilities have been introduced. In the former Ureshino Town (now part of {{ill|Ureshino, Saga|en|Ureshino, Saga|WD=Q634130|lt=Ureshino City|1=Ureshino, Saga}}) tea has been cultivated for generations. For this reason, Ureshino City and its tourism association actively promote the area as '''"Hot Spring Land of Tea and Tofu"''', and various initiatives have been undertaken to link the two. In addition, a 2D character themed on hot springs, “Ureshino Rokka” (from {{ill|Onsen Musume|ja|温泉むすめ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onsen Musume|1=Onsen Musume|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q30531379}}), is used to promote the hot springs{{Cite web |url=https://onsen-musume.jp/character/ureshino_rikka |title=嬉野 六香 |access-date=2024-09-22 |publisher=株式会社エンバウンド |website=温泉むすめ公式サイト}}. == Access == [[File:Ureshino Onsen Tofu.jpg|thumb|190px|{{Center|A Famous Specialty from the Edo Period
